Boundary $c\leq1$ Liouville CFT from the Bootstrap
Panos Betzios; Paul Ghiringhelli; Olga Papadoulaki; Ioannis Tsiares

We construct boundary Liouville conformal field theory at central charge $c\leq1$ with FZZT-type boundary conditions and show that it satisfies the Cardy--Lewellen sewing constraints on the disk and the annulus. Using the analytic bootstrap we derive the so far missing boundary three-point and bulk-to-boundary structure constants and a consistent disk one-point function as explicit meromorphic functions of the Liouville momenta. In sharp contrast to $c\geq25$, the open-string spectrum between two ``timelike'' FZZT boundaries is \emph{discrete}, yet non-trivially consistent through open-closed duality with the \emph{continuous} closed-string spectrum of Ribault and Santachiara.
Laura Cossu; Bruce Olberding; Giovanni Secreti

Motivated by examples such as the local rings of projective integral schemes and the Zariski-Riemann space of a field, we develop a geometry for continuously indexed families of subrings of a commutative ring $R$. The indexing spaces are Stone spaces, and continuity is taken with respect to the Zariski topology on the space of subrings. To each such family we associate a subsheaf of the constant sheaf with value $R$ whose stalks are the indexed subrings. This gives a patch ringed space. Its global sections are locally constant $R$-valued functions whose value at each point belongs to the corresponding subring. The ring of global sections, with this representation, is the associated patch algebra. Our main result establishes an algebra-geometry correspondence between these continuously indexed families of subrings and patch ringed spaces that can be expressed as a category equivalence, with each of the two categories dually equivalent to the category of patch algebras. Thus the indexing space, its sheaf, and the indexed subrings can be recovered functorially from the associated patch algebra, which serves as a coordinate ring for this geometry. We describe kernels and factorizations of patch algebra morphisms in geometric terms and characterize their injectivity and surjectivity. We include applications to Pierce duality and Bhatt-Scholze $w$-localizations of integral separated quasi-compact schemes.
Transfer of Weisfeiler-Leman equivalence under graph operations

The Weisfeiler-Leman algorithms WL(k) for $k\ge1$ form a hierarchy of increasingly powerful tests for graph isomorphism. We study how the equivalence relations they induce on graphs transfer through a graph operation $Φ$: for a given $k$, what level of WL-equivalence between graphs $H_1$ and $H_2$ guarantees WL(k)-equivalence of graphs $Φ(H_1)$ and $Φ(H_2)$? We call the least such level the transfer parameter $τ_Φ(k)$ and determine it exactly for the line graph operation $Φ= L$: $τ_L(k)=2k+1$ for $k\ge2$, while $τ_L(1)=1$. We also extend these results to the $(r,S)$-line graphs, which generalize the line graph from edges to $r$-cliques by connecting two cliques when their intersection size lies in a prescribed set $S$. For these operations we prove that $τ_{r,S}(1)=r-1$ for every $S$ and, for certain choices of $S$, that $τ_{r,S}(k)=rk+r-1$ for $k\ge r$, and we bound the transfer parameter in the remaining range. Our upper bounds on transfer parameters follow from a treewidth analysis of diagrammatic expansions of homomorphism counts into $Φ(H)$ as linear combinations of homomorphism counts into $H$. The matching lower bounds combine explicit constructions of witness graphs with the homomorphism-distinguishing closedness of graphs of bounded treewidth.
A wider state, not wider arithmetic, for single-precision time integration

Single precision (FP32) halves the memory and data movement of double precision (FP64), and on accelerators is often several times faster. Its rounding errors are harmless except in the stored state. A modified equation for Runge-Kutta methods in Shu-Osher form and linear multistep methods separates the rounding of the stored state, a forcing proportional to $1/Δt$, from truncation and from right-hand-side rounding, which sets a $Δt$-independent floor. We bound this forcing for strong-stability-preserving schemes and identify two mechanisms that keep its sign fixed, so it accumulates as a bias: past a turnaround step, refining the step increases the error, in FP64 as in FP32. For a model oscillator the analysis predicts the floor and the FP32-to-FP64 ratios of turnaround step and minimum error within 30%. Our remedy needs no FP64 arithmetic: each state variable is stored as the unevaluated sum of two FP32 numbers, updated with error-free transformations, while every right-hand-side evaluation stays in FP32. Unlike compensated summation, it needs no rewriting of the scheme. In model problems from geophysical flow, mechanical dynamics and celestial mechanics, with five Runge-Kutta and multistep schemes, it restores design-order convergence to the floor. In large-eddy simulations of a high-lift airplane wing on three refined grids, up to 544 million cells, with time steps $Δt$, $Δt/2$ and $Δt/4$, FP32 overpredicts the lift by 2.1, 4.5 and 7.7%, while the two-float lift agrees with FP64 within 0.3% on every grid, and on graphics processing units the production solver runs 1.6 to 2.7 times faster than FP64.
Designing an Adaptive Robust and Evolutionary-Game Framework for Minimum Shipment Quotas in Capacity-Constrained Freight Markets
Hossein Mirzaee; Ali Keyvandarian; Hamed Samarghandi

Minimum shipment quota regulations ensure that socially critical commodities are not excluded from capacity-constrained freight markets by profit-driven allocation. Existing models of such regulation are deterministic and static, assuming perfect market knowledge and instantaneous convergence to a rational equilibrium. This paper relaxes both assumptions through a framework combining adaptive robust optimization, multi-objective optimization, and evolutionary game theory. A robust optimization model first characterizes the regulator's quota-setting problem under uncertain commodity availability, trading social welfare against enforcement cost to generate a Pareto frontier of quota policies. This frontier then defines the regulator's strategy space in a three-population evolutionary game in which the regulator, suppliers, and carrier co-evolve under replicator dynamics, so that the prevailing policy emerges from the interaction of the three players. The framework is calibrated to a Canadian rail freight case study that covers crude oil, corn, barley, and oat. Quota regulation raises social welfare from 65.0 to 288.2 million CAD, at an enforcement cost of about 2% of the gain. Two findings carry particular policy weight: capacity shortfalls fall entirely on unprotected commodities the carrier ships voluntarily, sparing both the highest-margin and the protected products; and a fall in transport cost can end the regulation while the exclusion it was designed to correct persists, because the margin observable before bidding diverges from the margin prevailing once suppliers adapt.
A convolution inequality and the Krzyż conjecture

Using a sharp bound for convolutions of non-negative trigonometric polynomials with the Fejér kernel resembling a pointwise variant of Bernstein's inequality for polynomials, we prove new properties of extremal functions for the Krzyż conjecture. In particular, we resolve a 1993 conjecture of Peretz by showing that if $f$ is extremal for some coefficient, then $|f(0)|\leq 1/e$. Furthermore, we show that if equality holds in this estimate for every extremal function, then the Krzyż conjecture is true.
On the one-arm probability for the metric graph Gaussian free field in high dimensions
Pierre-François Rodriguez; Jialu Shi; Wen Zhang

We consider the sign clusters of the Gaussian free field on the cable system of a transient weighted graph with volume growth exponent $α$ and Green function decay exponent $ν$. We prove that the probability that the cluster of a vertex reaches distance $R$ is of order $R^{-β}$ when $2α<3ν$, where $β=α-ν$ is the walk dimension, and that the same holds up to a logarithmic factor in the upper bound when $2α=3ν$. On $\mathbb Z^d$ these conditions read $d>6$ and $d=6$. The upper bound combines a general entropic bound, which compares the law of the cluster under the critical loop soup and under a massive one, with a Simon-Lieb-type inequality for the massive field derived from its Markov property. The arguments are robust and require no transitivity. The lower bound follows from a competition between the capacity and the volume of the cluster. In both bounds, the key quantity is the expected exit time of the random walk from balls, which links the volume of the cluster to its radius.
Stable soliton resolution for the corotational Skyrme model

We study the classical Skyrme model. Under corotational symmetry, we prove that (i) stationary solutions, or Skyrmions, are unique in every topological degree; (ii) the Cauchy problem is globally well-posed in a nonlinear energy space; and (iii) stable soliton resolution holds: every finite-energy solution scatters to the Skyrmion of the same degree. Our key observation is that subcritical equivariant Yang--Mills dynamics emerge near the origin and suppress concentration.
Gepner stability conditions on hypersurface categories
Anibal Aravena; Peize Liu; Jenia Tevelev

We construct numerical Bridgeland stability conditions on the category of graded matrix factorizations of every smooth complex projective hypersurface of degree $d\ge2$. These conditions are of Gepner type $(τ,2/d)$, where $τ$ is the grading shift autoequivalence. By Orlov's theorem, this gives stability conditions of Gepner type on all Calabi--Yau hypersurfaces and on Kuznetsov components of all Fano hypersurfaces. These conditions satisfy a mass-Hom bound and the support property on the full numerical Grothendieck group. Semistable objects of fixed numerical class and phase admit proper good moduli spaces.
Rellich-Poincaré inequalities and improved Rellich inequalities

We study linear variational problems on bounded domains $Ω\subset \mathbb R^d$ involving the Dirichlet biharmonic operator $Δ^{2}$ and the Rellich potential $|x|^{-4}$, under the assumption $0\in\overlineΩ$. The case $0\in\partialΩ$ is particularly noteworthy and subtle.
On the Gabor frame set of polynomial-Gaussian windows

We prove two sufficient conditions for the frame property of Gabor systems $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)=\{e^{2πi mb\,\cdot}g(\cdot-ak):k,m\in\mathbb{Z} \}$ generated by polynomial--Gaussian windows $g(t)=P(t)e^{-ct^2}$, where $c>0$ and $P$ is a nonzero complex polynomial of degree $n$. The conditions depend only on the product $ab$ of the lattice parameters and the degree of $P$. First, $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is a frame whenever $ab<1$ is irrational. Second, if $ab=p/q<1$, with $p,q\in\mathbb{N}$ coprime, then $\mathcal{G}(g,a,b)$ is a frame whenever $q-p>n$. Consequently, in the region $ab<1$, failure of the frame property can occur only on rational hyperbolas whose reduced denominator and numerator differ by at most $n$. The proof extends the translated-Wronskian method of Faulhuber and Petersen [\emph{The frame set of the first Hermite function}, arXiv:2609.02610] from the first Hermite function to arbitrary polynomial multiples of a Gaussian, combining a multiplicity estimate for Wronskians with Jensen's formula.
Plotkin-optimal pure quantum LRCs with large minimum distances from NMDS codes
Yang Li; Shitao Li; Gaojun Luo; San Ling

Quantum locally recoverable codes (qLRCs) are a class of quantum error-correcting codes that can recover an erased qudit by accessing only a few other qudits. This paper develops a general framework for constructing optimal pure qLRCs that attain the Plotkin-like bound, referred to as Plotkin-optimal pure qLRCs, from Hermitian dual-containing near maximum-distance separable (NMDS) codes. Focusing on a special class of NMDS codes called extended subcodes of generalized Reed-Solomon (ESGRS) codes, we determine their localities by analyzing certain subset sum problems over finite fields. By further exploiting the algebraic structures of ESGRS codes and related codes, we construct four families of Plotkin-optimal pure qLRCs with large lengths and more flexible minimum distances than existing constructions. These constructions provide strong global error-correction capability while retaining local recovery. To the best of our knowledge, they give the first families of qLRCs attaining the pure Plotkin-like bound. In addition, by using the resulting locality property, we resolve in the negative a related problem on ESGRS codes supporting combinatorial designs.
A simple adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging method for unconstrained convex optimization in $p$-norm geometry
Bowen Li; Danqing Zhou; Chuan He

Efficient preconditioning plays an important role in large-scale first-order optimization. In this paper, we propose an adaptive accelerated optimistic dual averaging ($\text{A}^2$ODA) method for unconstrained convex optimization that adopts low-cost preconditioning based on $p$-norm geometry for $p\in[2,\infty]$. The method is line-search-free and employs a new stepsize selection technique based on an aggregated affine lower model. Its update structure is simple and unified across $p\in[2,\infty]$, with the case $p>2$ requiring no more elaborate updates than the Euclidean case $p=2$. Under a generalized local smoothness condition, we derive a convergence bound that separates the effects of constant and gap-dependent curvature, with the latter potentially yielding faster-decaying terms. In the special case of local smoothness, this bound recovers a nearly optimal convergence rate.
Toric gravitational instantons with four fixed points
Lars Andersson; Mattias Dahl; Gustav Nilsson

We classify the simply connected toric gravitational instantons whose torus action has four fixed points. They are the hyperkähler multi-Eguchi--Hanson and multi-Taub--NUT metrics with four collinear centres, the asymptotically flat instantons on Li and Sun's manifold $X_3$, up to scale one for each twist at infinity in $(0,1)$ for a fixed orientation of the torus, and, up to scale, a single further instanton with an ALF end, which is not hyperkähler. The last two are Hermitian for neither orientation. In particular, the toric asymptotically flat instanton on $X_3$ with a given twist is unique up to scale, as conjectured by Li and Sun. The proof combines the solitonic form of Geroch's conjecture, which turns smoothness into polynomial equations for the soliton data, with a convexity principle adapted from Aksteiner. At a fixed asymptotic parameter, the cone errors of the conical metrics with a given rod structure are the gradient of a strictly convex function of the rod lengths, and the strict convexity gives uniqueness. Existence follows from an explicit solution for the ALF end and, for the AF ends, from Li and Sun's existence theorem. We also outline how a chart of Aksteiner identifies these AF instantons with those found by Teo.
Morse accessibility with applications to Coxeter groups
Matthew Cordes; Annette Karrer; Kim Ruane

In this paper we begin developing a theory of Morse hierarchies for finitely generated groups. Very roughly, a Morse hierarchy is a iterative splitting of a group over subgroups that do not contribute to the Morse boundary of the ambient group.
 We apply this theory to Coxeter groups, establishing new combinatorial criteria that distinguish certain Coxeter groups from other Coxeter groups as well as right-angled Artin groups up to quasi-isometry. We highlight the consequences for the right-angled case. To build the reader's intuition, the last section provides many examples of Morse hierarchies and their subtleties.
 Finally, there is an appendix by the second author and Vivian He that extends these ideas to the metrizable Cashen--Mackay topology on the Morse boundary.
Convex ribbon disks, quasipositivity, and Lagrangian sliceness

We introduce a version of convex surface theory for immersed ribbon surfaces with Legendrian boundary. As an application, we establish a special case of K3: Problem 1.70 on sharpness in the slice-Bennequin inequality implying quasipositivity, and a special case of a conjecture of Cornwell, Ng, and Sivek on characterizing Lagrangian sliceness. Specifically, we prove that if $K$ is a knot that bounds a "star-shaped" ribbon disk and satisfies $\overline{\mathrm{sl}}(K) = -1$ (resp.\ $\overline{\mathrm{tb}}(K) = -1$), then $K$ is quasipositive (resp.\ Lagrangian slice). In fact, we prove these statements for any fixed transverse (resp.\ Legendrian) representative.
Uniform local smoothing for the derivative NLS and the soliton mass threshold

Harrop-Griffiths, Killip, Ntekoume and Vişan proved that the derivative nonlinear Schrödinger equation (DNLS) is globally well-posed in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$. A key ingredient of their proof is a local smoothing estimate. It holds on $L^2$-equicontinuous sets of initial data, but it cannot hold on $L^2$-balls, because rescaled stationary solitons, all of mass $2π$, violate it. This raises a natural question: for which masses $m$ does local smoothing hold uniformly on the ball $\{M(q_0)\le m\}$? We prove three results. First, we give a quantitative version of the local smoothing estimate in which the data enter only through the mass and an explicit frequency scale $κ(q_0)$. On time intervals of length $2T$ the bound grows like $1+κ(q_0)^2T$, and the stationary soliton shows that the power of $κ$ cannot be lowered below one. Second, we prove uniform local smoothing on balls of small mass, together with a scale-invariant Morrey-type form and a localized $L^4_{t,x}$ bound. Third, we analyse the soliton family from both sides. The uniform constant must blow up at least like $(2π-m)^{-1}$ as $m\uparrow 2π$, while every soliton of mass $m<2π$ satisfies local smoothing with a constant $O((2π-m)^{-1})$. These facts single out the stationary-soliton mass $2π$, which is also the Hayashi--Ozawa coercivity threshold, as the natural candidate for the sharp threshold. We formulate this as a conjecture, give a spectral reformulation in terms of the Kaup--Newell scattering data, and discuss the obstacles to a proof.
An Exact QFT/Lattice Map for Fermions

We construct an exact map between continuum fermion fields and lattice fields in 1+1 dimensions. This map rewrites a continuum Hamiltonian as a lattice Hamiltonian with nearest-neighbor couplings and an infinite-dimensional local Hilbert space. The resulting lattice model reproduces exactly the energy spectrum, global operator algebra, chiral symmetries, and anomalies of the continuum QFT on any finite lattice. Unlike domain wall fermions, truncating the local Hilbert space introduces no extra massless modes, and the entanglement entropy of an interval converges as the truncation is removed. The lattice local algebras are of type I and lie between the type III continuum algebras of nested spatial regions, in accordance with the split property. We demonstrate this construction explicitly for $N$ Majorana fermions, realizing the $\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{L}\times\mathrm{O}(N)_\mathrm{R}$ lattice chiral symmetry. We also construct an exact lattice model for the Schwinger model and numerically reproduce the mass gap $e/\sqrtπ$.
Remap for ALE Hydrodynamics via Direct Interpolation and Constraint Optimization
Brendan Keith; Dohyun Kim; Boyan Lazarov; Ketan Mittal; Cosmin G. Petra; Mathias R. Schmidt; Vladimir Z. Tomov

This work presents an optimization-based remap approach for arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian (ALE) hydrodynamics that preserves sharp features and physical bounds while conserving global quantities such as volume, mass, momentum, and total energy. Achieving these properties is the main challenge in remap methods. The presented approach is well-suited for high-order finite element (FE) discretizations and ALE methods that allow for large, purely Lagrangian displacements between successive remeshing and remapping steps. Recent advances in parallel, GPU-capable interpolation routines enable the initial transfer of all fields via direct physical-space interpolation, avoiding computationally costly and diffusive pseudo-transient PDE-based advection. The interpolation produces bounded fields with minimal numerical diffusion. However, it may violate the desired conservation of global properties. Thus, a subsequent optimization step restores conservation while preserving physical bounds. The presented method provides minimally diffusive remapping of finite element fields of arbitrary order. Moreover, it directly remaps quantities defined at integration points, eliminating the need for projection onto finite element spaces. The approach also mitigates typical challenges associated with synchronizing primal variables and conserved quantities in advection-based remap methods. The proposed optimization-based remap method is evaluated using standard two- and three-dimensional remap benchmarks and full ALE hydrodynamics simulations.
Mapping-space Gromov--Witten classes and the Fano variety of lines

Let $Y$ be a smooth cubic 3-fold. We show that $S^2 \times Y$ admits an infinite sequence of cohomologous symplectic forms which are all deformation equivalent but pairwise non-isotopic; McDuff showed the corresponding result on $(S^2)^2 \times T^2$, but these appear to be the first simply-connected and monotone examples. The results are obtained from McDuff's bordism-flavoured Gromov--Witten invariant, re-interpreted cohomologically in terms of an evaluation map valued in the space of maps from the 2-sphere to a symplectic target. The application then relies on classical properties of the Fano space of lines on $Y$. We also discuss higher-dimensional generalisations.
We present a proper 12-colouring for all associahedra. This gives the first constant upper bound on chromatic number for this family, and disproves a conjecture of Fabila-Monroy et al. from 2009.
On the number of tiles in $[n]^d$
Anubhab Ghosal; Jeck Lim; Elad Tzalik

Let $\mathcal{T}(n,d)$ denote the set of subsets of $[n]^d$ that tile $\mathbb Z^d$ by translations, and write $T(n,d)=|\mathcal{T}(n,d)|$. We show that almost every tile in $\mathcal{T}(n,1)$ tiles $\mathbb{Z}$ by an arithmetic progression, thus determining $T(n,1)$ asymptotically. In higher dimensions, we prove that $T(n,d)=O_d\!\left(n^{C_d}3^{n^d/3}\right)$, confirming a conjecture of Benjamini, Kozma and Tzalik. In the other direction, we prove that $T(n,d)\geq (1-o(1))n^{\binom d2}3^{n^d/3}$ when $3\mid n$. This shows one cannot take $C_d=d-1$ for $d\geq 3$, answering a question due to the same authors negatively. Finally, we also obtain nearly tight bounds in dimension two. Our upper bounds rely on a new observation realising tiles as maximal independent sets in truncated Cayley graphs.
Quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximation for exponential random graphs in the single-phase critical regime

We establish quantitative non-Gaussian and Gaussian approximations for edge-count fluctuations in dense exponential random graphs at single-phase criticality of any fixed even order $2m_*\ge 4$. The Hamiltonians use injective homomorphism counts of fixed simple graphs, with nonnegative leading coefficients for the higher-order terms. In bounded calibrated windows, edge-density fluctuations on the scale $n^{-1/m_*}$ admit an explicit non-Gaussian approximation with error $O(n^{-1/m_*})$. For parameter perturbations by fixed multiples of $n^{-1}$ with a nonzero first-order drift correction at the critical density, the deterministically centered edge count admits a Gaussian approximation on the scale $n^{(3m_*-2)/(2m_*-1)}$, with error $O(n^{-1/(2m_*-1)})$. Both rates hold in Wasserstein and Kolmogorov distances. The key step is to construct auxiliary kernels for exterior graphs outside an event of exponentially small probability. These kernels contract uniformly on the full row state space and agree with the conditional Gibbs updates on typical row configurations, yielding the conditional cumulant estimates used in Stein's method.
Diastolic inequalities for the distance function min-max width of spheres

In this article, we investigate inequalities involving the min-max width associated to the distance function and the area of two-dimensional Riemannian spheres. This geometric invariant naturally arises as min-max methods are applied for the distance function defined on the space of pairs of points. Our methods involve careful constructions of sweepouts that can be performed under the hypothesis that the Riemannian sphere does not contain stable closed geodesics. Improved bounds are obtained under further geometric assumptions (positive curvature, pinching condition, and antipodal symmetry). In the cases of a pinching condition or antipodal symmetry, our inequalities are optimal.
Dynamical Properties of the Multiple Elastic Pendulum

This article studies the dynamical properties of the multiple elastic pendulum formed by an arbitrary number of point masses connected in a chain by elastic springs. First, using the Lagrangian formulation, the equations of motion governing the system's behavior, accounting for both large-angle displacements and elastic deformations, are derived. It is shown that well-established, low-dimensional systems, such as the classical double elastic pendulum, can be systematically recovered as particular cases directly from the general equations of motion after applying the appropriates particular conditions. The behavior of the system under small oscillations near its stable equilibrium is also investigated. For this case, the linearized equations allow the solution of the eigenvalue problem, demonstrating that in this case uncoupled behavior between the angular displacements and the spring elongations.
Counterexamples to the Happy Edge Conjecture in Plane Spanning Trees
Oswin Aichholzer; Joseph Dorfer; Peter Kramer; Christian Rieck; Birgit Vogtenhuber

We study the problem of reconfiguring plane, straight-line spanning trees on point sets in the plane. A flip is a reconfiguration step in which one edge of a tree is replaced with another, yielding again a plane spanning tree. For a given point set $P$, the flip graph has a vertex for each plane spanning tree on $P$, and an edge between any two trees that differ by a single flip.
 The folklore happy edge conjecture suggests that any edge shared by both the initial and the target tree (a happy edge) is never flipped in a shortest flip sequence. This conjecture was computationally verified for up to 10 points in convex position.
 In this paper, we disprove this conjecture both on general point sets and on point sets in convex position by providing two counterexamples on $16$ and $30$ points, respectively. The counterexample for point sets in general position also holds for compatible flips, while the happy edge property holds for compatible flips in convex point sets as shown by Aichholzer, Dorfer, and Vogtenhuber [GD 2025].
Supercritical level-set percolation on finite graphs

We continue the study of bond percolation on finite graphs induced by the level-sets of the zero-average Gaussian free field on the associated metric graph. In our previous work Goswami and Pal (2026), we analyzed the critical and near-critical behavior of this model on uniform expanders, focusing on the volume of the largest cluster. In the present paper, we investigate the size of the second largest cluster in the supercritical regime --- the phase where one expects a unique giant component. We prove that the second largest cluster is at most of logarithmic order with high probability. The estimates hold uniformly over deterministic graphs with a bounded maximum degree and a spectral gap bounded away from zero. In particular, we do not require any assumption regarding regularity, girth or local geometry. This picture is substantially different from Bernoulli percolation, where the second largest supercritical cluster can have polynomial volume under identical hypotheses. The proof relies on expansion properties of the underlying graph and the Dirichlet martingale framework developed in Goswami and Pal (2026).
The tensor triangular geometry of valuation domains
Tobias Barthel; Drew Heard; Beren Sanders; Changhan Zou

We study the tensor triangular geometry of derived categories of valuation domains, obtaining complete ring-theoretic characterizations of their main structural properties. In particular, although valuation domains are almost always non-noetherian, their derived categories always satisfy the local-to-global principle and hence the detection property. We establish precise criteria for homological detection, stratification, and homological stratification, revealing a clear hierarchy among these properties. Notably, we obtain examples of derived categories of commutative rings that are homologically stratified and satisfy the local-to-global principle, but are not stratified. We also determine when the category of modules over a valuation domain has Gabriel dimension, and use this to provide a negative answer to a question of Balchin, Gómez and Stevenson. Overall, valuation domains provide a rich class of non-noetherian rings whose derived categories can be understood in considerable depth.
The Lee-Huang-Yang Formula in the Hard-Core Simplified Approach to the Bose gas
Mohamed El Hedi Bahri; Ian Jauslin

We study the hard-core variant of the Simplified Approach to the ground state of the dilute Bose gas. The hard-core potential has been the subject of renewed attention, and is physically relevant to realistic atomic Bose gases. The hard-core Simple Equation is an integro-differential equation, and we construct its solution via a monotone iteration scheme and prove existence and uniqueness (in a restricted sense) of the solution. The energy per particle $e$ and the density $ρ$ of the solution are shown to satisfy the Lee-Huang-Yang formula $e = 2πρ(1 + \frac{128}{15\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ))$ as $ρ\to 0$, and the condensate fraction $η$ predicted by the hard-core Simple Equation is shown to satisfy $η= 1 - \frac{8}{3\sqrtπ}\sqrtρ + o(\sqrtρ)$ as $ρ\to 0$, in agreement with Bogolyubov's theory. We thus extend results of Carlen, Jauslin, Lieb to the hard-core case.
 The hard-core equation is defined on its own terms, and the proofs proceed by approximating the hard-core potential with the soft-core potentials $m\,χ_{\{|x| \le 1\}}$ of increasing height $m$: at fixed energy, we establish the $L^1$ convergence of the corresponding solutions and the convergence of their densities at an $O(m^{-1/2})$ rate, and we show that the Lee-Huang-Yang expansions of the energy and of the condensate fraction for the soft-core equations hold with errors uniform in $m$, so that they survive the hard-core limit.
A note on cohomogeneity one Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds

K. Broder recently classified the closed Einstein 4-manifolds whose isometry groups have dimension at least three. The proof reduces the problem to the study of cohomogeneity-one Einstein metrics invariant under $SU(2)$, however a few cases are not treated. We reconcile the missing cases using Broder's techniques with minimal modifications.
The Critical Cauchy Boundary for Gibbs Partitions

We study critical Gibbs partitions whose component law is in the domain of attraction of a spectrally positive stable law of index one. In the dense phase, we prove a local limit theorem for the number of components and functional limits for their sizes. We also describe convergent and divergent condensation regimes, and a phase transition at a boundary in which the dense and condensation contributions compete.
Minimal model of a Plateau-Rayleigh instability of a solid binary alloy nanowire: impacts of surface segregation

Minimal model and its linear stability analysis (LSA) for Plateau-Rayleigh (PR) instability of an intermixed, solid binary alloy nanowire is presented. Model accounts only for the surface diffusions of the alloy components without anisotropies of a surface energies, and for a classical thermodynamic surface segregation. Model allows to assess a deviation of a longwave instability cutoff wavelength $λ_c$ from the classical value $2πr_0$ (a wire circumference) as a function of a surface composition deviation from its equilibrium value, a wire radius, and a bulk concentration of a minority component. Results of LSA are presented for AuNi, PtNi, and CoNi nanowires, where an important distinction is that a surface segregation curve for CoNi is qualitatively different from the one for AuNi and PtNi. For each nanowire there is a sizable region of a parameter space where $λ_c<2πr_0$ and correspondingly, a fastest growing perturbation wavelength $λ_{max}$ is also less than a wire circumference. This is in stark contrast to PR instability of a single-component nanowire transporting mass by surface diffusion - in this case $λ_c$ and $λ_{max}$ are larger than a wire circumference. Strong surface segregation is primarily responsible for unusually small $λ_c$ and $λ_{max}$. Results suggest that a large number of small and closely spaced nanoparticles may emerge upon disintegration via annealing of a binary alloy nanowire.
Conformal Prediction at Performative Equilibrium: The Price of Performativity

Conformal prediction gives finite-sample coverage when calibration and test points are exchangeable, but exchangeability can fail when deployment changes the data distribution. We study conformal prediction in performative settings, where the deployed predictor affects the data distribution, and seek prediction sets valid at performative equilibrium: coverage must hold under $D(f^\star)$ for a performatively stable predictor $f^\star$. Under total-variation $L$-sensitivity of the distribution map, we prove a phase transition at $L=1$. If $L \ge 1$, no finite-sample procedure can uniformly guarantee both equilibrium-valid coverage and nontrivial prediction sets. If $L<1$, the minimax excess miscoverage over informative procedures is $\widetildeΩ(1/((1-L)\sqrt{n}))$, implying a sample-complexity inflation of order $1/(1-L)^2$ for fixed excess miscoverage. Our main technical tool is a transfer theorem: any procedure returning a predictor within $\varepsilon$ of equilibrium yields equilibrium-valid coverage up to an additive $L\varepsilon$ term after split-conformal calibration. We instantiate the theorem with two retraining algorithms: a model-free method for discretizable classes and a parametric tail-averaged method that matches the $n$- and $L$-dependence of this rate up to logarithmic factors. Experiments, including semi-synthetic credit scoring, demonstrate the predicted threshold behavior and scaling laws.
De Rham cohomological architectures for PINNs and PDEs with topological holes

We attempt to alleviate failure modes of classical physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in scenarios of topological pathologies corresponding to punctures, holes, poles, and voids by introducing de Rham cohomological augmentations, or Hodge-de Rham PINNs. Vanilla PINNs often encounter pitfalls in hole-based settings due to discontinuous interfaces, nonzero closed path integration, path dependence, correspondence to exact forms via the exterior derivative, etc., therefore we absolve traditional failures via parameterizing a 1-form by the Hodge-Morrey-Friedrichs (HMF) decomposition for manifolds with boundary, drawing a connection to de Rham cohomology such as through the HMF isomorphism theorem. 1-forms can act as representations of scalar-valued PDE solutions through integral operator mappings. We propose performing a PINN-based loss on the parameterized 1-form through an associated PDE, which subsequently solves the potential-based PINN problem and moreover remedies the failures of vanilla PINNs via the Sobolev-regular operator under a Fréchet differentiation interconnection. The operator relationship often has a nontrivial closed-form and often requires integration or a case-by-case analysis, which we address thoroughly in our experiments. When an integrability condition is not met on our losses, we can equip exhaustion functions to train the networks. We demonstrate our methods on the Aharonov-Bohm effect, which, to our understanding, is largely nonexistent in PINN literature. We develop theoretical guarantees of our methods and demonstrate our pathological safeguards on a broad selection of topologically-adverse problems, including scenarios of inexact forms, and those of nontrivial harmonics and coexact terms.
Alperin weight bijections and dimensions of simple modules

We propose a new refinement of the (blockwise) Alperin weight conjecture taking dimensions of simple modules (or degrees of irreducible Brauer characters) into consideration. This is similar to Giannelli's refinement of the (Alperin--)McKay conjecture. We prove this new refinement for blocks with a cyclic or Klein four defect group, for inertial blocks (which include the Broué--Puig nilpotent blocks), and for $p$-blocks of $p$-solvable groups.
On the van der Corput property for cubes
Steve Fan; Andrew Lott; Ákos Magyar; Máté Matolcsi; Imre Z. Ruzsa

We prove a power-saving form of the van der Corput property for cubes. As a consequence, we obtain a power-saving bound $|A|\ll_\varepsilon N^{59/60+\varepsilon}$ for sets $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ with no nonzero cube differences.
Maru Sarazola; Brandon T. Shapiro; Inna Zakharevich

In this paper we classify the algebraic K-theory of sets equipped with an action by a finite abelian monoid. The main tool developed for this purpose is an Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem, which gives a decomposition of monoid sets analogous to the decomposition given by the Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem for G-sets.
Global Existence for a Drift-Diffusion Model of Electrical Discharge in MEMS

We study a coupled elliptic-parabolic system modelling electrical discharge in a micro-electro-mechanical (MEMS) capacitor: a Poisson equation for the electrostatic potential, coupled to drift-diffusion equations for the ion and electron densities with a Townsend ionization source whose rate per electron grows linearly in the electric field. Gimperlein, He and Lacey proved local well-posedness and left open whether the densities blow up in finite time. We first prove a continuation criterion in a weak norm: a finite-time singularity forces the space charge to be unbounded in H^1_D, the dual of the space of H^1 functions vanishing on the electrodes, so blow-up cannot be quasi-neutral. We then exclude it altogether when the two diffusivities coincide and the vacuum field is bounded: the weak solution is then global in time. To our knowledge this is the first global existence result without smallness assumptions for a drift-diffusion-Poisson model of gas discharge whose ionization rate is unbounded in the field. The proof uses the electrostatic energy and the number of carriers in place of the usual free energy: the ionization source cancels in the energy balance, the Joule heating is dissipative, and the two quantities close through a linear Gronwall inequality. Numerical experiments on a discharge in a micrometre gap, with the Townsend constants and the mobilities of air, provide evidence for the extension to unequal diffusivities and bear on the existence of a breakdown threshold.
A near-quadratic lower bound for the Brown--Erdős--Sós $(9,6)$-problem
Xiangliang Kong; Chong Shangguan; Xin Wang

Let $f_3(n,e+3,e)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex $3$-uniform hypergraph containing no $e$ distinct edges spanning at most $e+3$ vertices. It has long been conjectured that $f_3(n,e+3,e)\ge n^{2-o(1)}$ for every fixed $e\ge3$. We prove that $f_3(n,9,6)\ge n^2\exp(-O((\log n)^{2/3}))$, settling the first unsolved case of the conjecture.
Weak solutions to granular medium equations via stochastic particle approximations

We establish weak existence for McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations associated with granular medium equations with porous medium diffusion, for m>1 in arbitrary dimension. The result covers a class of nonconvex potentials with locally Lipschitz gradients of polynomial growth. Our particle approximation generates nonlinear diffusion through density-dependent noise and allows initial densities with finite Boltzmann entropy but infinite internal energy.
The Connectivity Threshold for Friends and Strangers graphs
Bruno Baldissera; Gabriel Dias do Couto; Simon Griffiths; Luiz Moreira

The concept of the Friends and Strangers graph $FS(G,H)$ associated with two graphs $G$ and $H$ was recently introduced by Defant and Kravitz and has generated significant interest. In a companion article, joint with Alon, they consider the behaviour of $FS(G,H)$ in the case where $G$ and $H$ are Erdős-Rényi random graphs, and prove that the threshold for connectivity is of the form $n^{-1/2+o(1)}$. In this paper we prove that the threshold is $n^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log{n}}$, up to a multiplicative constant, answering a question from Alon, Defant and Kravitz.
Geometric classification of imaginaries in pseudofinite fields

In [Pil07], Pillay showed that every imaginary in a proper pair of algebraically closed fields is interalgebraic with an imaginary of a certain algebraic form. In this paper, we establish an analogue for lovely pairs of pseudofinite fields. After naming countably many constants, we prove that every imaginary in lovely pairs of pseudofinite fields is interalgebraic with an imaginary of the same algebraic form as [Pil07] in the corresponding pairs of finite extensions of pseudofinite fields.
Localisations of rings of weak global dimension at most one

We characterise the commutative rings of weak global dimension at most one whose derived categories can be stratified by the Balmer-Favi support theory. For such rings, this yields a bijective correspondence between the class of localising subcategories of the derived category, and the subsets of the Zariski spectrum. For a large class of rings of weak global dimension at most one including all valuation domains, this occurs if and only if the ring is locally strongly discrete, if and only if the Telescope conjecture holds, and if and only if the module category has Gabriel dimension. However, we also give an example of a valuation domain where all these conditions fail, and yet the residue fields generate its derived category and we can classify all the localising subcategories of $D(R)$. Additionally, in the same example, we show that the Balchin-Stevenson smashing support cannot stratify $D(R)$ either.
Coherence and the Hilbert-syzygy identity for power series over valuation domains
Mohamed Amine Aouichaoui; Adam Jones; Yiding Wang

Let $V$ be a complete valuation domain of rank 1, and let $Γ$ be its value group. We investigate the power series ring $V[[t]]$, and finally answer the long standing question of when this ring is coherent. Specifically, we prove that it is coherent if and only if $V$ is almost maximal, and either $Γ= \mathbb{R}$ or $Γ$ is discrete. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the weak Hilbert-syzygy identity $w. dim V [[X]] = w. dim V + 1$ holds if and only if $V[[X]]$ is a coherent ring.
Anisotropic Minkowski flows: well-posedness and asymptotic behaviour
Giulia Anastasi; Filippo Cagnetti; Massimiliano Morini

We study anisotropic Minkowski-type curvature flows associated with a perimeter defined through oscillations on Wulff neighbourhoods. The anisotropy may be non-smooth, and in particular crystalline, while the mobility may differ from the anisotropy, provided a natural compatibility condition is satisfied. We compute the first variation of the perimeter and introduce a weak formulation in terms of distance functions and measure-valued nonlocal Cahn-Hoffman fields. By means of a nonlocal minimising movement scheme and suitable estimates for the evolution of Wulff shapes, we prove existence of weak superflows and subflows starting from arbitrary closed sets. Under the additional assumption that the initial level sets have compact boundary, a comparison principle yields existence and uniqueness of the level set flow. Finally, we prove that variational weak flows converge, up to fattening, as $r\searrow 0$ to the weak flow of the local anisotropic, possibly crystalline, curvature motion. The main step in the proof consists in averaging the nonlocal Cahn-Hoffman measures to obtain vector fields converging to a local Cahn-Hoffman field.
Logarithmic Regret for Alternating Mirror Descent

Alternating online mirror descent (AltOMD) is a simple learning rule for zero-sum games, which improves upon simultaneous OMD numerically and theoretically. Previous work obtained $O(T^{1/3})$ and $O(T^{1/5})$ regret bounds for AltOMD, by leveraging modified-energy-function-based analyses. However, settling whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret has remained an open question. In this paper we resolve the question of whether AltOMD achieves near-constant regret in the affirmative. In particular, we show an $O(log(T))$ regret bound on the sum of the players' external regrets for any two-player zero-sum bilinear game with compact convex strategy sets, under mild regularity assumptions on the regularizers. We verify that our assumptions hold for the negative entropy regularizer, thereby obtaining logarithmic regret for the alternating multiplicative weights updates algorithm. The regret bound also yields an $O(log(T)/T)$ duality gap bound for the averaged strategies.
Accelerated Concatenation of Stepsize Schedules for Smooth Strongly Convex Gradient Descent

This work considers stepsize schedules for gradient descent on smooth strongly convex objectives. We develop a curvature-dependent concatenation framework for constructing stepsize schedules of arbitrary length with sharp worst-case guarantees. Within this framework, we introduce two families of schedules for the function-value gap and gradient norm of the last iterate, respectively. For each fixed condition number $κ=L/μ>1$, both families attain iteration complexity $Θ(κ^ρ\log(1/ε))$ for sufficiently small $ε$, where $ρ=\log_{\sqrt2+1}2\approx0.7864$. This complexity is optimal up to a subpolynomial factor in $κ$ among predetermined nonnegative stepsize schedules. The framework also recovers the strongly convex silver schedule at power-of-two iteration budgets and applies to smooth convex and smooth weakly convex functions.
Modulational stability of finite-depth Stokes waves with constant vorticity

We investigate the effect of constant vorticity on the modulational spectral stability of small-amplitude periodic gravity waves for the two-dimensional finite-depth water-wave system. We derive an explicit stability criterion that agrees with the prediction obtained by Thomas, Kharif and Manna [43] through a nonlinear Schrödinger approximation. For waves propagating to the right, we identify a sharp range of dimensionless positive (counterclockwise) vorticity, for which modulational instability is suppressed at every depth, while at any fixed depth sufficiently strong negative (clockwise) vorticity also restores modulational stability. We give a complete description of the spectrum near the origin and identify a figure-eight spectral curve in the unstable regime. A key distinction from the irrotational case is that the usual Hamiltonian factorization of the linearized operator fails at zero Floquet exponent on the full periodic Sobolev space. We therefore carry out a spectral reduction based on reversibility, without relying on Hamiltonian factorization.
The Landau equation: Well-posedness and singularities of homoenergetic solutions
Francisco-Unai Caja-Lopez; Maria Pia Gualdani; Alessia Nota

We consider the inhomogeneous Landau equation and focus on solutions whose density and temperature evolve in time but remain spatially homogeneous. Such solutions are called homoenergetic. We identify one class of initial data for which homoenergetic solutions exist globally in time, and another class for which they develop finite-time hydrodynamic singularities. The initial data are spatially inhomogeneous, neither close to vacuum nor close to equilibrium; both the well-posedness and the finite-time blow-up results hold for all soft and hard potentials.
Handling Customer Preferences in Last-Mile Location-Routing: A Bilevel Optimization Approach
José Emmanuel Gómez-Rocha; José-Fernando Camacho-Vallejo; Elena Fernández

This paper introduces the Location-Routing Problem with Delivery Preferences, a last-mile delivery problem with service flexibility that integrates collection-point activation and routing decisions while accounting for customer choice. The company determines which collection points to activate, which customers to offer home delivery, and the corresponding delivery route. Customers subsequently decide whether to accept the proposed home-delivery service or collect their parcels from an activated collection point according to ranked preferences over delivery time intervals and collection points. This hierarchical interaction is modeled through a bilevel optimization framework, which can be formulated as a mixed-integer bilevel program that incorporates compensation mechanisms for service inconvenience. Two equivalent single-level reformulations that exploit the structure of the customers' problems are developed. In addition, a two-phase heuristic is proposed to generate feasible solutions that can be used as warm starts for the formulations. The computational experiments run to compare the performance of the formulations, show that the warm-start strategy becomes particularly effective as the instance size increases. The comparison with a benchmark model that ignores customer preferences indicates that explicitly accounting for customer choice alters the resulting location-routing configuration while improving customer preference satisfaction at a small increase in the company's overall cost. These findings highlight the importance of jointly considering operational efficiency, service flexibility, and customer autonomy in last-mile delivery planning.
Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the $O(N)$ Model

Let $μ$ be a probability distribution on a spin system with $n$ sites and possibly infinite spin spaces. We prove local-to-global spectral-gap bounds for block Glauber dynamics. Given a symmetric, entrywise nonnegative matrix $A$ with zero diagonal and $λ_{\max}(A)<1$ encoding local spectral bounds for a spin system, we derive global spectral-gap bounds for block dynamics on its marginal distributions. These bounds are sharp: the Gaussian system with covariance $(I-A)^{-1}$ attains equality for every choice of disjoint blocks. Our proof extends the Bochner method through an abstract inequality for orthogonal projections on Hilbert spaces.
 As an application, we prove that Glauber dynamics for the $O(N)$ model, with $N\geq 2$, arbitrary external fields, and couplings of either sign, has spectral gap at least $(1-\|J_{\mathrm{abs}}\|_{\mathrm{op}}/N)/n$, where $J$ is the interaction matrix and $J_{\mathrm{abs}}=(|J_{ij}|)$.
 We also obtain spectral bounds for swap walks and local spectral expansion of partite simplicial complexes. For complexes formed from disjoint groups of ranks in random flags of subspaces over $\mathbb F_q$, we obtain a one-sided local spectral expansion bound of $2\sqrt q/(q+1)$. This bound is independent of the number and sizes of each group, and is nontrivial for every prime power $q$.
 Finally, for random forests $F$ of any finite graph with arbitrary positive edge weights, we prove that
 \[
 \Pr(e,f\in F)\le \frac{4}{3} \Pr(e\in F)\Pr(f\in F)
 \]
 for distinct edges $e,f$, improving the factor 2 supplied by general log-concavity bounds for matroid independent sets. The argument combines our extended Bochner method with the analysis of an auxiliary real stable polynomial.
Regret-based Characterization, Information Limits, and the Sample Complexity of Auditing Adaptive Policies

A policy can earn its performance by where it locates on average or by reacting to information. For any Markov policy $π$ in a finite-horizon MDP, let $ν$ be its open-loop marginal, which plays $π$'s average action distribution at each step. We show that $J(π)-J(ν)$ equals $\sum_t tr Cov(Q^ν_t,π_t)$ under endogenous dynamics. Audits based on immediate costs alone can have the wrong sign. Writing the covariance as a joint-versus-product gap gives the bound $|J(π)-J(ν)|\le\sum_t span_t\sqrt{I(s_t;a_t)/2}$, with a sharp constant. Hence, an MDP's adaptivity gap is bounded by the information that its optimal policy uses. Estimating $J(π)-J(ν)$ from $π$'s own bandit-feedback logs takes $Θ(\barχ^2 \log(1/η)/δ^2)$ rounds, where $\barχ^2$ is an average $χ^2$-divergence. At the same time, deterministic non-constant policies cannot be audited at all. We also provide an importance-sampling auditor for episodic MDPs.
CQ-collocation BEMs for exterior wave propagation problems: the 3D Neumann case
Davide Collato; Silvia Falletta; Giovanni Monegato; Letizia Scuderi

In this paper, we consider three-dimensional exterior wave propagation problems with non-homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We reformulate the problem as a space-time boundary integral equation involving a hypersingular operator. To solve the resulting formulation, we combine Lubich's convolution quadrature with a shifted collocation boundary element discretization and investigate numerically the efficiency, stability, and convergence of the resulting numerical scheme. Numerical tests show that the proposed approach achieves an accuracy comparable to that of Lubich's convolution quadrature combined with a Galerkin boundary element method, and provide numerical evidence of the unconditional stability of the collocation scheme.
Using adelic intersection theory and following the method envisioned by Parshin and Moret-Bailly, we prove a conjecture of Vojta for curves of genus two and a weak form of the $abc$ conjecture
Evgeniya Akhmedova; Thomas Lam; Calvin Yost-Wolff
We give an example of a tiling of the $m=4$ amplituhedron that has fewer cells than that of the magic number conjecture. The tiling uses an injective degree two cell.
H-sober spaces and Hofmann-Mislove type theorems

A $T_0$-space is called $ω$-sober if every irreducible closed subset having a countable dense subset is the closure of a unique point. This is precisely $H$-sobriety for the countable irreducible subset system $\mathcal R^ω$. We give two natural Hofmann--Mislove representations in the general $H$-sobriety framework: filters induced by $H$-sets of $X$ characterize $H$-sobriety, whereas filters induced by $H$-sets of the Smyth power space characterize super $H$-sobriety. Their relation is expressed by property $Q$. A minimal closed set argument with a countable selection proves that $\mathcal R^ω$ has property $Q$. Consequently, $X$ is $ω$-sober if and only if its Smyth power space is $ω$-sober, equivalently, every countable irreducible compact-family filter has a compact saturated representation. We also obtain equivalent recovery, compact-intersection and representation conditions for an enlarged class containing the proper Scott-open filters with countable open bases and the filters induced by countable irreducible subsets. A further equivalent formulation uses traces on countable subspaces. The filtered-family specializations recover well-filteredness and $ω$-well-filteredness. Explicit examples show that $ω$-sobriety strictly implies $ω$-well-filteredness, which strictly implies representation for countable open bases alone.
2D Navier-Stokes with viscosity-dependent Navier slip: strong convergence for unbounded initial velocity

For the two-dimensional incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with Navier friction on a smooth, bounded, simply connected domain, we establish strong vorticity convergence along a subsequence in the vanishing viscosity limit for initial vorticity in $L^p$ with $p>1$. The friction coefficients may grow as viscosity vanishes under an explicit growth restriction depending on $p$, which includes regimes of vanishing slip length. The main challenge, even for viscosity-independent friction, is to control the vorticity generated at the boundary. We split the vorticity into contributions from the initial data and the boundary. By combining renormalization and estimates for the normal velocity near the boundary, we show that the boundary contribution vanishes in the inviscid limit. As a consequence, the limiting Euler solutions conserve kinetic energy.
Physics-informed traditional and generative Mori-Zwanzig-reduced models for multiscale systems
Emily Williams; Saad Qadeer; Amanda Howard; Panos Stinis

Model reduction via the Mori-Zwanzig (MZ) formalism is well understood for coarse-grained representations constructed from standard basis functions such as Fourier functions. We show that the same formalism can be used to build reduced-order models in bases discovered by physics-informed machine learning. The fluctuation-dissipation theorem (FDT) is used to close the resulting non-Markovian evolution equations for the expansion coefficients of the learned basis. We further introduce a complementary, generative closure model. Relative to the Markovian dynamics alone, both the MZ and generative closures substantially improve predictions of the filtered states.
Non-local approximations for the Schrödinger operator with a general point interaction via the non-relativistic limit

We consider the one-dimensional Dirac operator $D_{A,c}$ with a general, not necessarily self-adjoint, point interaction at the origin, whose strength is described by an arbitrary complex $2\times 2$ matrix $A$ and suitably rescaled by the speed of light $c$, together with its non-local approximations $D_{A,c}^ε$ obtained by replacing the Dirac distribution by a rank-one projection onto a scaled function $v_ε$. It is known that $D_{A,c}^ε\to D_{A,c}$ as $ε\to 0+$ and that $D_{A,c}-c^2/2$ converges, as $c\to+\infty$, to the Schrödinger operator $H_A$ with the general point interaction, both in the norm resolvent sense. We prove that the first convergence is uniform with respect to $c$ in a neighbourhood of $+\infty$, and we provide explicit rates of convergence. Combining this with an explicit computation of the non-relativistic limit of $D_{A,c}^ε$ for fixed $ε$, we show that the two limits can be interchanged and that the corresponding double limit exists. As a by-product we obtain a family of non-local, rank-two approximations $H_A^ε$ of $H_A$ that converge to $H_A$ in the norm resolvent sense. Contrary to the relativistic setting, the coupling constants of $H_A^ε$ are renormalized; we give an explicit formula for this renormalization.

In this note we prove a simple generalization of cohomology and base-change which seems to be missing from standard sources. We illustrate its usefulness by providing an alternative proof of a result of Ishimura on descent of vector bundles along blowups at a smooth center.
The P-Ideal Dichotomy and the Failure of Two-Cardinal Square Principles
We prove that the $\mathrm{P}$-ideal dichotomy implies the negation of the square principle $\square(λ, ω)$ for every regular cardinal $λ\geqω_2$.
Divisibility Properties of Odd Part and Even Part Sums in Cubic Partitions

A cubic partition of a positive integer $n$ is a partition of $n$ in which even parts may appear in two distinct colors. The purpose of this paper is to study the arithmetic functions $COS(n)$ and $CES(n)$, which denote the sums of all odd and even parts, respectively, in all cubic partitions of $n$. We obtain their generating functions and divisor-sum formulas, and establish Ramanujan-type congruences modulo $3$, $4$, $5$, and $7$. To prove these congruences, we use Lambert series, classical theta-function identities, dissections, coefficient extraction, and weighted Euler identities.
Ensembles of Random Partition-Based Models under Covariate Shift

Distribution shifts, including covariate shifts, are ubiquitous in real-world applications of machine learning. Empirical evidence suggests that, across a variety of models with and without downstream adaptation, ensembles tend to be more robust to covariate shift than single models. We extend the theory of covariate shift severity from single models to ensembles, providing theoretical justification for the empirical trends. We introduce new discrepancy measures of covariate shift severity to control the risk of partition-based kernel estimators. We then show that with sufficient ensemble size, these models can achieve minimax-optimal risk convergence rates under covariate shift. Our results suggest that modelers can expect to need larger ensemble sizes for more severe covariate shifts.
Hopf algebra polynomial identities in the Sweedler algebra

Using Mac Lane's PROPs, one can introduce multilinear polynomial identities that involve all the operations of a Hopf algebra: the (co)multiplication, the (co)unit and the antipode. We find bases for polynomial identities and calculate their codimensions for the Sweedler algebra, treating it first as an ordinary associative algebra over a field and second as a Hopf algebra.
Rasterization-based discontinuous integration on the GPU
Manuel Saberi; Muqtasid Tashfin; Andreas Vogel

In this paper, we propose a method based on rasterization in computer graphics for the integration of discontinuous functions accurately and efficiently on the GPU. The proposed method takes advantage of the massively parallel architecture of GPUs via a modified graphics pipeline, where discontinuities are encoded through geometric primitives and processed in the rasterization stage, and multisample anti-aliasing (MSAA) is used to improve integration accuracy across subdomain interfaces. We present both hardware- and software-based pipelines and compare their performance in terms of accuracy as well as computational effort on modern GPU hardware with adaptive quadrature on the CPU. For the tested hardware, at approximately comparable median relative error, the hardware pipeline is up to around $100\text{x}$ faster than adaptive quadrature, while the single- and double-precision software pipelines achieve up to $840\text{x}$ and $1200\text{x}$ speedups compared to their adaptive quadrature counterparts. We use the finite cell method as model problem, where cutcells represent discontinuous integrands at the interface of the physical and fictitious domains and demonstrate the performance of the proposed method using numerical benchmarks. The end-to-end finite cell solution runtime is reduced by a factor of $8.3$ to $9.5$ in the single-precision pipeline and by a factor of $62$ to $72$ in the double-precision pipeline at the prescribed integration settings. Therefore, results indicate that the rasterization-based integration method is a promising alternative for the accurate and efficient integration of discontinuous functions in demanding applications on the GPU.
Base change between canonical basis and path basis

Almost 30 years ago Littelmann conjectured that there is a unitriangular base change between the dual canonical basis and the path vector basis for all symmetrizable Kac-Moody Lie algebras. In this paper we give a positive answer to the conjecture for the case of classical Lie algebras and type $G_2$, when the path model is given by standard Young tableaux.
Weighted Max Cut in Subcubic Graphs

For a graph $G$ with nonnegative edge weights, let $\operatorname{mc}(G,w)$ denote the maximum total weight of a cut and let $w(G)$ denote the total edge weight. We prove that every edge-weighted triangle-free subcubic graph satisfies $\operatorname{mc}(G,w)\geq \frac{15}{19}w(G)$, improving the bound of $\frac{8}{11}$ due to Gutin and Yeo. For subcubic graphs of odd girth at least seven and nine, we strengthen this bound to $\frac{47}{59}w(G)$ and $\frac45w(G)$, respectively, establishing the conjecture of Gutin and Yeo for graphs of odd girth at least nine. Our proofs combine structural properties of vertex partitions with randomized cut constructions and convex combinations of the resulting bounds.
A Smooth Shioda-Tate Isomorphism for Elliptically Fibered 4-Manifolds

This paper studies a subgroup of the mapping class group of an elliptically fibered $4$-manifold $π: M\to B$, inspired by number theory. The smooth Mordell-Weil group $\mathrm{MW}(π)$ is the group of isotopy classes of smooth sections of $π$. We construct a smooth analog of the Shioda-Tate isomorphism, identifying $\mathrm{MW(π)}$ with the quotient of $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$ by the trivial lattice of $π$. This shows that $\mathrm{MW}(π)$ can be computed explicitly from $H^2(M;\mathbb{Z})$. As an application, we show that the natural inclusion of the holomorphic Mordell-Weil group into the smooth one is an isomorphism if and only if $M$ is a rational elliptic surface. As another application, we show that $\mathrm{MW}(π)$ satisfies a strong version of Nielsen realization: any torsion element of $\mathrm{MW}(π)$ is represented by a holomorphic translation of $M$ of the same order.
Uniform asymptotics for the Kleitman-West problem

Two distinct $r$-element sets are adjacent if their intersection has size $r-1$. The Kleitman-West problem, equivalently formulated as the edge-isoperimetric problem on the Johnson graph $J(n,r)$, asks for the maximum number $M_r(n,m)$ of unordered adjacent pairs in a family of $m$ $r$-element subsets of an $n$-element set, and for the families attaining this maximum. For every fixed integer $r\ge2$, we determine this maximum asymptotically as $n\to\infty$, uniformly over the entire range of family sizes.
 Specifically, for each integer $1\le j\le r$, define $F_j(p)=\max\{p^{1+1/j},\,2p-1+(1-p)^{1+1/j}\}$ for $0\le p\le1$, and $G_j(x)=\lfloor x\rfloor+F_j(x-\lfloor x\rfloor)$ for $x\ge0$. With \[ P_r(n,m)=\sum_{j=1}^r\frac{n^{j+1}}{2(j-1)!}G_j\!\left(\frac{j!m}{n^j}\right)-\frac{r(r-1)}4mn-\frac m2, \] we prove that \[ \lim_{n\to\infty}\max_{2\le m\le\binom nr}\left|\frac{M_r(n,m)}{P_r(n,m)}-1\right|=0. \] The remaining cases satisfy $M_r(n,0)=M_r(n,1)=0$. The proof first establishes the asymptotic formula for dense families using a sharp inequality for bounded random variables, with equality attained by a random variable taking at most two values. To extend the result uniformly to all family sizes, we extract groups of sets sharing a fixed subset, apply the dense estimates after deleting that subset, and control the adjacent pairs not contained in any one group.
An elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity for rank-one planar Lipschitz maps

We give an elementary proof of a tangent-cone identity which might be known to specialists in geometric measure theory. It concerns Lipschitz mappings $g$ from the closed unit ball $B\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$. Let $x$ be an interior point of differentiability of $g$ at which $Dg(x)$ has rank one. If the upper one-dimensional Hausdorff density of $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ is at most one, then the tangent cone to $g(B)$ at $g(x)$ coincides with the image of $Dg(x)$. This property is used in the proof of rigidity for the four-gradient problem. We provide a detailed, self-contained proof based on differentiability, connectedness and elementary estimates for one-dimensional Hausdorff measure, without using advanced methods from geometric measure theory.
On partitions with bounded multiplicity restrictions on even parts and with the largest part being odd

Andrews and El Bachraoui (\textit{RACSAM} \textbf{119}, \textit{Article Number 4 (2025)}) established identities relating $4$-regular partitions to partitions with distinct even parts whose largest part is odd. As an extension to their work, in this paper we define partitions of a positive integer $n$ with bounded multiplicity restriction on even parts and whose largest part is odd. We prove some identities relating our partition functions and $2r$-regular partition function, and show that identities due to Andrews and El Bachraoui follow as particular cases.
Decompositions of homomorphisms of abelian $p$-groups with $p^2$-bounded target

Let $p$ be a prime. We classify homomorphisms $H:V_1\to V_2$ between abelian $p$-groups that are direct sums of cyclic groups, under the assumption $p^2V_2=0$. We prove that every such homomorphism is isomorphic to a direct sum of finite indecomposable representations and that this decomposition is unique up to isomorphism and reordering of the summands.

This survey concerns Stein's analytic family of generalized spherical means and the associated maximal operator. We review Stein's original theorem, the sharp necessary conditions for boundedness, and the complete theory for radial functions. We then explain the connection between positive results and local smoothing estimates for the half-wave propagator and, more generally, for Fourier integral operators. This point of view yields the sharp two-dimensional result through the work of Guth, H. Wang, and R. Zhang and, when combined with the recent local smoothing theorems, an improved higher-dimensional range. As a byproduct, the maximal operator associated with the first radial derivative of spherical means is bounded on $L^p(\R^4)$ for $2<p<3$, a case left open in recent work of Kwaśnicki. We keep track of the relation between the local smoothing exponents and the resulting maximal estimates, and identify the region that remains open.
A Generalized Lai--Wei Construction and New Families of Area-Minimizing Hypercones

Our results are twofold. Inspired by recent work on weighted spheres, we extend the Lai--Wei construction from one to several independent isoparametric inputs, replacing its profile curve by a hypersurface profile to generate minimal hypersurfaces in spheres. Using a curvature criterion, we obtain new infinite families of area-minimizing hypercones from the original construction and its extensions.
Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms

Using the bisection bound of Monien and Preis, Fomin and Høie proved in 2006 that every graph of maximum degree 3 on $n$ vertices has pathwidth at most $n/6+o(n)$. We prove that the pathwidth, bisection width and cutwidth of these graphs are at most $c_3 n+o(n)$, where $c_3=\frac{3}{4π}\arccos\frac56\approx0.1398$. For bisection width this improves the bound $n/6+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis (2006) and extends to all such graphs the bound that Lichev and Mitsche (2023) obtained for random cubic graphs. For maximum degree 4, we prove that bisection width and cutwidth are at most $n/3+o(n)$, improving the bound $2n/5+o(n)$ of Monien and Preis for 4-regular graphs, and that pathwidth is at most $0.2458n$, improving the bound $n/3$ of Fomin, Gaspers, Saurabh and Stepanov (2009). We show that every graph with $m$ edges has pathwidth at most $7m/48+o(n)$, improving the bound $13m/75$ of Scott and Sorkin (2007), and we give further bounds of the form $\sum_{d\ge3}a_d n_d+o(n)$ with $a_d<1$, where $n_d$ is the number of vertices of degree $d$. The path decompositions, and linear orderings of the stated cutwidth, can be computed in polynomial time.
 Instead of deriving pathwidth bounds from bisection width, we give each vertex a Gaussian label, a weighted sum of independent standard normal variables over a ball around it, and sweep a threshold through the labels; the bags are frontiers, the vertices above the threshold with a neighbor below it. We bound the probability that a vertex lies in a frontier by comparison with an explicit Gaussian model of a vertex and its neighbors.
 Faster exact algorithms follow: for feedback vertex set and the traveling salesperson problem on graphs of bounded maximum or average degree, and on general graphs for minimum weight dominating set (by branching until the instance is sparse), Max 2-CSP and counting subgraphs with $k$ edges (by the bound in $m$).
Large cardinals, small violations of choice
Hope Duncan; Gabriel Goldberg; Asaf Karagila

We study the relationship between large cardinals and Blass' Small Violation of Choice ($\mathsf{SVC}$), which states that the Axiom of Choice holds in a set-generic extension of the universe. Our main theorem is that in the presence of a supercompact cardinal, either the Axiom of Choice fails significantly, or else $\mathsf{SVC}$ holds in $L(\mathcal P(\mathrm{Ord}))$. We show that a supercompact is not strong enough to reflect $\mathsf{SVC}$, while an extendible cardinal is. If we assume Usuba's Loś Property holds for the supercompact, then we can outright derive $\mathsf{SVC}$ in the universe.
Positive solutions to the nonlinear Choquard equation: symmetry, uniqueness, and nondegeneracy
Jiankang Xia; Chengxiang Zhang; Xu Zhang

We study the symmetry, uniqueness, and nondegeneracy of positive solutions to the Choquard equation $-Δu+u=(I_α*u^p)u^{p-1}$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$, which have long remained open problems. For $N\geq3$, $α\in(0,N)$, and $\frac{N+α}{N}<p<\frac{N+α}{N-2}$,we prove that every positive $H^1$-solution is radially symmetric and strictly decreasing in the radial variable. The symmetry proof relies on the moving-plane method, where the sublinear singularity is controlled by analyzing the far-field behavior of the nonlocal term. Uniqueness and nondegeneracy are established through a functional framework hinging on a nonnegative joint form and a Schur complement argument.Radial nondegeneracy and Morse index one are obtained by ruling out the spectral interval $(0,p-1]$ via a strict cumulative Riesz identity, which leads to uniqueness through a Nehari two-well argument. Nondegeneracy in the full space $H^1(\mathbb{R}^N)$ follows from the spherical-harmonic decomposition of the linearized form. These results hold for the full range of $p$ when $α=2$, and for $p\geq2$ when $α\in(2,N)$. The cases $α\in(0,2)$ and $α\in(2,N)$ with $p<2$ remain open.
A Random Matrix Analysis of Symmetric Tensor Unfolding
Tom Szwagier; Xiaoyi Mai; José Henrique de Morais Goulart

We study a fundamental problem in machine learning: partial recovery of a planted signal $\boldsymbol{v} \in \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$ from a spiked tensor $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{X}} = λ\, \boldsymbol{v}^{\otimes p} + \boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$, where $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ has symmetric Gaussian entries of variance $\asymp n^{-1}$. While previous works replace $\boldsymbol{\mathsf{Z}}$ by an i.i.d. standard Gaussian tensor to circumvent technical difficulties caused by dependencies, this paper directly analyzes the symmetric model via random matrix theory. We show that the square unfolding algorithm is subject to a sharp phase transition for partial recovery at $λ\asymp n^{(p-2) / 4}$, validating an open conjecture from Montanari and Richard (2014). We get precise expressions for the limiting spectral distribution, deterministic equivalent, phase transition threshold and overlap. The main message is that unfolded symmetric tensors spectrally behave like standard Wigner matrices, up to simple transformations accounting for high-order symmetries. We consider extensions to multiple orthogonal spikes, recursive unfolding and non-square unfolding via disproportionate random matrix theory, leading to an interesting conjectured statistical-computational tradeoff regarding the choice of unfolding: square versus long.
Solving the Nonlinear Westervelt Equation in Ultrasound Propagation Using Physics-Informed Neural Networks

Modeling the nonlinear acoustic wave propagation in biological tissues needs accuracy, especially in ultrasound imaging and therapeutic applications. The 1D Westervelt equation, \( p_{xx} - p_{tt} + γ\, p_{ttt} + η\,(p^{2})_{tt}=0, \) could be used to describe a finite-amplitude ultrasound propagation in these tissues. This equation accounts for nonlinearity, \(η\), and attenuation, \(γ\). To solve this equation, we observe that traditional solvers may struggle to do so correctly. This is due to the difficulties arising from the nonlinear nature of the equation. We solve the equation by defining three synthetic cases - linear (\(η=0.001\), \(γ=10^{-6}\)), shock-dominated (\(η=0.02\), \(γ=10^{-6}\)), and dissipation-dominated (\(η=0.01\), \(γ=5\times10^{-4}\)) - and using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to showcase the solution. A sinusoidal activation function is used to capture the oscillatory behavior of the problem. The results of our study, with PDE residual converging to at least \(10^{-6}\), boundary condition loss to \(10^{-5}\), and the PINN loss converging to \(10^{-5}\) for each case at \(30,000\) epochs, show that \(γ\) scales the rate of amplitude decay, while \(η\) governs frequency-dependent phase speeds.
Do Ray-Traced Cities Make a Better Channel Prior for an Unseen Site? A Pre-Registered Study in Simulation, and a Test on Measured Channels that Reverses It

Channel estimators at a newly deployed base station usually start from 3GPP stochastic channel models, which describe no particular street. We ask whether a channel prior pooled from many ray-traced cities serves an unseen site better than the 3GPP CDL models, and whether learned estimators make the difference. With Sionna RT on 14 city scenes, LMMSE estimation from covariance priors, leave-one-city-out evaluation, and pass/fail bars written down before each main experiment, we find in simulation that the pooled prior sits about 0.6 dB from a site-trained estimator with no site measurements, about what CDL reaches after 50 measurements. Learned models added little: at most 0.65 dB in estimation, and in channel prediction a simple classical method beat CNN predictors by 1.8-12 dB from 2 ms ahead. On measured channels from the DICHASUS outdoor dataset (1.272 GHz, three 2x8 arrays on one building) the result reversed: the pooled ray-traced prior was 3.2-4.1 dB worse than CDL. The simulated channels were too clean; with users at the real distances, even a scattering level tuned from 50 site measurements left the prior about 2 dB behind CDL. A pre-registered follow-on on two more measured environments found the generic CDL prior 2.1-4.7 dB from a site-trained one: no further in a factory hall than on the street, furthest in a small lab room. Finally, a hallway model calibrated to measurements by differentiable ray tracing reproduced delay spread, but as a prior in an unmeasured part of the hallway it was 4.5 dB worse than CDL on the full array. All measured results come from one sounder.
Mapping class group actions on the cohomology of configuration spaces of surfaces

Let X be a closed oriented surface of genus at least 2 and P a finite subset of X. We bound the action of the mapping class group of (X,P) on the rational cohomology groups of the ordered configuration spaces F_n(X-P) of X-P. In particular, we show that, when #P < 2, the diagonal action of the mapping class group on the direct sum of the H^n(F_n(X-P)) is faithful, and determine its kernel when #P > 1.
Quasiconformal distortion of the lower dimension and applications
Efstathios Konstantinos Chrontsios Garitsis; Jeremy T. Tyson

We study the distortion of the lower dimension and lower spectrum of sets under quasiconformal mappings. As an application, we verify weighted Hardy--Sobolev inequalities in Euclidean domains arising as quasiconformal images of domains with sufficiently regular boundaries. The regularity in question is phrased in terms of estimates for either the Assouad or the lower dimension of the complement. We also provide dilatation-dependent classification results for certain planar open sets.
