These results lead to constructive algorithms which we analyse rigorously and implement in the open-source Python package CRNNondim, available at https://github.com/georgio-hawi/crnnondim . Given a polynomial system or CRN, CRNNondim determines species and time scalings that bring variables as close to unity as possible while minimising the number of free parameters, and among the admissible scalings it chooses free parameters that result in the corresponding dimensionless system being sparse and simple. We apply CRNNondim to numerous well-known biological and biochemical models, yielding simpler dimensionless systems with fewer free parameters, and interpreting the parameters that govern their dynamics.
D-equivalence conjecture for hyperkähler varieties of generalized Kummer type
Will Donovan; Chengxi Wang; Nantao Zhang

We show that birationally equivalent hyperkähler varieties of generalized Kummer type are derived equivalent, confirming the D-equivalence conjecture in this case. Combined with recent results of other authors, this settles the conjecture for all known deformation types of hyperkähler varieties. The kernel is built from an equivariant Fourier-Mukai kernel on the sum-zero loci of powers of an abelian surface. We deform it along diagonal twistor paths, using the hyperholomorphic endomorphism algebra. Comparing wall hyperplanes gives a common twisted derived category for two adjacent birational models, and a finite sequence of wall crossings then gives the equivalence.
Universal bounds for decompositions of PL manifolds

The geometric dimension of a nonempty compact PL manifold $N$ is the smallest nonnegative integer $d$ for which $N$ admits a handle decomposition with all handles of index at most $d$. A PL filling of a compact PL manifold is a decomposition into compact codimension $0$ PL submanifolds, called sectors, with pairwise disjoint interiors and intersections described by standard local models. We advance Singhof's program of simplifying the sectors of a filling and their intersections. Specifically, for integers $m, \ell\ge 1$ and nonnegative integers $a_1\le\cdots\le a_\ell$, we prove that every closed PL $m$-manifold admits a filling into $\ell$ sectors whose nonempty $r$-fold intersections have geometric dimension at most $a_r$ for each $1\le r\le \ell$ if and only if \[ a_{λ_1}+\cdots+a_{λ_q}\ge m-\ell+1 \] for every partition $λ_1+\cdots+λ_q=\ell$ into positive integers. Under the same inequalities, any prescribed $\ell$-sector filling of the boundary of a compact PL $m$-manifold extends to a filling with the corresponding relative handle index bounds. Necessity follows from the cup-product obstructions of Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. To prove sufficiency, we develop compatible handle trades that simplify intersections in increasing order of depth. For nondecreasing tuples of nonnegative integers, our theorem resolves the PL classification problem posed by Courte, Moussard, Ren, and Zhou. In particular, we obtain the bound $(2,2,4)$ for $3$-sector fillings in dimension $6$ and improve the $5$-sector bound $(1,2,3,3,4)$ of Rubinstein and Tillmann to $(1,2,2,3,4)$ in dimension $8$.
On nearly Lefschetz fibrations and spinal open books
Hyunki Min; Agniva Roy; Luya Wang

We survey the recent development of spinal open books and nearly Lefschetz fibrations. The focus is on explaining past and new results regarding the detection of symplectic fillability and classification of symplectic fillings of contact 3-manifolds in light of the new machinery. We give many examples and a list of open questions. This can be considered as an additional chapter to the lecture notes by Ozbacgi and Wendl.
Time to AC-t: When AC-transmission changes capacity expansion planning
Lara Booth; Shiva Madadkhani; Ruaridh Macdonald; Priya L. Donti

Capacity expansion models often dramatically simplify the physics of how power flows through a transmission network in order to preserve computational tractability. However, with the rapid growth of electrification, large loads, renewables, and storage, increased realism in planning future grids is imperative. We extend the open-source capacity expansion model GenX with AC optimal power flow physics, and analyze generation, storage, and transmission investment decisions for 20-zone, hourly models of Germany and Texas. We compare our results against those using two common approximations, the transport model and DC optimal power flow. We find that total costs and emissions largely agree across all formulations. However, we find substantial differences in outputs related to transmission, generation siting, storage, and reactive-power support between the approximate formulations and the true AC physics formulation. We identify where AC physics changes planning decisions and discuss how to potentially capture these effects without the full computational cost.
Bounds for Orthogonal Expansion Coefficients via Weighted Primitives

For trigonometric and polynomial orthogonal expansions, we present coefficient bounds with an explicit numerator determined by the total variation of the function and the largest cumulative signed area of the weighted basis element. This area, denoted by $M_n$, is the sharp constant in the corresponding weighted integral estimate. We calculate or bound $M_n$ for several classical systems, thereby obtaining quantitative inequalities beyond an asymptotic statement of coefficient decay. Integration between consecutive zeros gives a geometric interpretation of the estimate. The comparison includes Chebyshev polynomials of the first three kinds, Legendre, Jacobi, Gegenbauer, and ordinary Laguerre polynomials, with normalization and boundary conditions stated explicitly. Classical estimates and their elementary consequences are organized as Fourier analysis in inequalities. In the controlled distortion application, ideal curves have selected coefficients absent, and restrictions on the variation, corridor width, and number of extrema of admissible departures give explicit guarantees for those coefficients.
Adaptive data-driven reduced-order models for reciprocal MIMO port-Hamiltonian dynamical systems

Port-Hamiltonian (pH) systems provide a general framework for modeling a broad class of physical dynamical systems, including systems with dissipation. Constructing accurate and robust data-driven reduced-order models for general pH systems is challenging. In this work, we focus on an important subclass of pH systems satisfying reciprocity, a property arising naturally in a variety of models. Rather than seeking to preserve the full pH structure, we exploit the additional symmetry provided by reciprocity to develop an efficient data-driven reduced-order modeling approach. We show that every minimal realization of a reciprocal system is self-adjoint with respect to a generally indefinite inner product and can, up to a similarity transformation preserving the pH structure, be represented in a Krein space with a signature inner product. This observation motivates a Galerkin projection onto a tangential rational Krylov subspace with respect to the corresponding indefinite inner product. Although the resulting projection involves full-order state solutions and the unknown inner product, we show that its reduced mass and stiffness matrices can be constructed directly from transfer-function data through a Loewner formulation. We then propose a greedy data-driven procedure that adaptively selects both interpolation frequencies and tangential directions. At every iteration, the frequency is chosen according to the largest transfer-function approximation error, while the tangential direction is selected from a dominant singular direction of the corresponding matrix-valued residual. Numerical experiments for wave propagation in lossy media demonstrate improved approximation efficiency compared with block adaptive interpolation. We further apply the method to spectral mass gauging of a three-dimensional propellant tank to provide an accurate estimate of the tank volume through Weyl's law.
Minimax signal detection in regression under differential privacy

We establish minimax separation rates across sparsity levels for regression signal detection under $(ε, δ)$-central differential privacy, considering linear regression with an unknown error distribution and generalised linear models (GLMs) with an unknown intercept. Without sparsity restrictions, the separation rates for linear regression and GLMs with binary responses match the private Gaussian mean testing rate up to polylogarithmic factors. For GLMs with more than two possible response outcomes, additional information in the marginal response distribution permits faster detection of sufficiently small signals when the dimension exceeds the sample size $n$. Our upper bounds are based on a reduction to private mean testing, tests of dependence between the response and sparse covariate projections, and a response-only test that is adjusted for the unknown intercept. The resulting procedure adapts to unknown sparsity and matches our lower bounds up to polylogarithmic factors. We also construct polynomial-time tests that attain these rates when $ε\gtrsim n^{-1/2}$, and compare their numerical performance with existing private procedures.
StreamLTT: Risk Certification for Policy Selection under Stream Dependence

Learn-then-Test (LTT) provides a general framework for certifying deployment policies against a prescribed risk target, but its standard formulation targets a fixed population risk estimated from calibration losses. In sequential deployment, losses may instead be dependent and nonstationary, so the risk of a fixed policy can evolve with the observed history. We introduce StreamLTT, which replaces this fixed population risk with average predictable risk, defined by conditioning each decision's loss on the information available before its outcome is revealed. Conditional centering turns empirical deviations from this target into a martingale sum, enabling both a test that adapts to predictable variance and a finite-sample Hoeffding alternative. Combined with family-wise error rate control, StreamLTT yields a simultaneously certified policy region that supports subsequent deployment selection. Across seven forecasting datasets and seven deployment risks, StreamLTT places the certified frontier substantially closer to the prescribed risk target than IID, robust-variance, block-bootstrap, and concentration-based alternatives, while empirical family-wise error closely follows the prescribed level. A finite-sample ablation further shows that the predictable-risk formulation drives the tighter risk frontier, while adaptation to predictable variance makes more effective use of the available family-wise error budget. StreamLTT therefore extends risk-certified policy selection to dependent deployment streams by addressing both what risk should be certified and how it should be tested.
Revisiting the Upper Bild of Quaternionic Numerical Ranges

The upper bild of the quaternionic numerical range provides a convex representative of the generally nonconvex quaternionic numerical range. Although its convexity is known, the geometry of the upper bild is difficult to describe explicitly, even for 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices.
 In this paper, we revisit the upper bild of quaternionic numerical ranges from both algebraic and geometric viewpoints. We first point out gaps in Kumar's proof. We then investigate several special classes of 2-by-2 quaternionic matrices and describe their shapes and boundary structures in the closed upper complex half-plane directly in terms of the standard eigenvalues and the off-diagonal entry of the Schur form.
 For the general 2-by-2 case, we use a different canonical form. Following So and Thompson, we prove the concavity of the upper-boundary function through the associated complex representation. For the lower boundary, we obtain a distance-to-a-disk representation and use convex optimization to prove its convexity. We also treat the degenerate cases. Together with the connectedness of the vertical sections, these results give an alternative proof of the convexity of the upper bild for arbitrary quaternionic matrices.
A Review of Max-Pressure Traffic Signal Control Algorithms: State of the Art and Research Opportunities
Abdullah Al Asif; Chaopeng Tan; Vikash V. Gayah; Hao Liu

Max-Pressure (MP) has emerged as a widely studied decentralized traffic signal control framework, thanks to its desirable theoretical properties and strong control performance. Early research on MP focused on improving control performance by exploring different variables of the traffic state for the definition of pressure. Subsequent studies expanded MP to incorporate the complexity of real-world transportation systems and emerging technologies. This paper provides a comprehensive review of these developments. The review first introduces the theoretical foundations of MP and examines early developments in movement weight definition. It then synthesizes major extensions for multimodal and multiscale network control, followed by recent developments in connected and automated vehicle (CAV) environments and the integration of MP with artificial intelligence (AI) and data-driven methods. Beyond summarizing existing approaches, this review examines their underlying assumptions, data requirements, implementation considerations, and practical limitations. Based on this comprehensive review, key research gaps and future directions are identified, including remaining limitations in the theoretical foundations of MP and the underexplored integration of autonomous vehicle control with the MP framework. Overall, this review provides a structured perspective on the evolution and current state of MP control and highlights opportunities for developing more proactive, robust, and practically deployable MP-based traffic control methods.
Fixed-grid schemes for fractional moving-boundary problems

The Landau transformation xi = x/s(t) is the usual way to hold a moving boundary in place. It fails for fractional time derivatives because they have no chain rule: the transformed operator gains a nonlocal integral with a closed form only for self-similar fronts. We develop a sharp-interface finite-difference scheme for the conservation-consistent memory-flux fractional Stefan problem on a fixed grid, storing the memory limit h(x) = s^-1(x) as the time each node melts. The front is advanced using an integrated energy balance, with the singular source timed to the sub-step crossing instant. Against a known self-similar solution, the front constant is accurate to 0.02 to 0.11%, whereas competing formulations differ by 17 to 27% at alpha = 0.6. A remaining positivity violation follows from dt/t0 ~ s0^(1 - 2/alpha) and disappears on a front-locked time grid. We also derive two exact solutions with non-power-law fronts: a source-dominated solution and a Mittag-Leffler traveling wave, and verify the scheme against both. Neural-network solvers for moving boundaries are often trained in normalized coordinates; for alpha < 1, this silently changes the problem, while the change vanishes at alpha = 1, where checks are commonly performed. In the classical limit, our scheme is more accurate in 12 ms than a reimplemented moving-boundary network in 177 s.
Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound
Ryan Gabrys; Shubhransh Singhvi; Eitan Yaakobi

We construct binary codes that attain the classical Gilbert-Varshamov redundancy guarantee for a fixed number of edit errors, with deterministic polynomial-time construction, encoding, and decoding. For every fixed integer $t\ge 1$ and all sufficiently large block lengths $n$, our codes correct any combination of at most $t$ insertions, deletions, and substitutions in total, with redundancy at most $2t\log_2 n+O_t(1)$. All algorithms run in polynomial time in $n$ for fixed $t$, and decoding recovers the original information message. This realizes the classical counting guarantee algorithmically without enumerating the exponentially large space of binary words.
Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras: a Kauffman diagram perspective

We describe Hochschild cohomology of Temperley--Lieb algebras by explicit minimal-resolution coordinates and multilinear operations on Kauffman diagrams. For each doubled-line basic algebra, a finite four-term bimodule complex is verified by a signed-shuffle comparison and an augmented contracting homotopy. We compute cocycles and coboundaries and recover the known cup product and Gerstenhaber bracket in explicit representatives. Over $\mathbb C$, at nonzero root-of-unity loop parameters, we construct a tower-compatible derivation and the marked-circle two-cocycle. Their classes are nonzero on every nonsemisimple block; their cup products therefore represent all positive classes over the centre. Relative full twists give a compact expression for the derivation. Worked planar diagrams distinguish the cup product from insertion and strict cochain equalities from equalities of classes. A finite-lattice section interprets the marked-circle operation as loop-weight response, derives its planar Potts normalization, and exhibits a six-vertex realization. It also shows why passing to a deformable spin representation may annihilate the class with different coefficients. No thermodynamic conclusion is claimed, and the even-strand zero-parameter family remains separate.

We encode certain sets of partitions by regular languages of boundary words, so that their generating functions become rational series in the quantum plane $RU=qUR$. An equality between two partition counts is certified by writing the difference of their series as $(1-U)a+b(1-R)$, with $a,b$ converging $q$-adically. We show that $a,b$ may be chosen as solutions of finite holonomic systems of $q$-difference equations computed from the automata, and describe finite certificates of their convergence, together with bounded searches for such certificates; the searches need not succeed, but a false identity is always detected.
 As an application, we prove the three-row, level-two case of Primc's conjecture, which equates counts of coloured partitions subject to local multiplicity conditions with counts of coloured partitions whose parts lie in prescribed residue classes modulo eight.
Some instances of modularity for residually reducible representations in the mixed case

Let $F$ be a totally real field, abelian over $\Q$, in which an odd prime $p$ splits completely, and let $ρ:G_F\to\GL_2(\overline\Q_p)$ be an odd irreducible representation which is de Rham with distinct Hodge--Tate weights at the places above $p$ and whose residual representation is reducible. We consider the \emph{mixed} case of the Fontaine--Mazur conjecture, in which $ρ$ is reducible at some places above $p$ and irreducible at the others. This case is not covered by the work of Pan and Zhang. We prove some instances of modularity in this situation. Our main result is that $ρ$ is modular if it is non-split at every place above $p$ where it is reducible, by combining Zhang's pro-modularity theorem with a classicality criterion based on Emerton's ordinary parts. Together with a theorem of Zhao on local indecomposability, this gives the modularity of the $λ$-adic representations attached to abelian varieties of $\GL_2$-type in the mixed case, and, using a result of Snowden, of potentially modular representations of parallel weight two under a mild additional condition. It also gives the modularity of representations whose local type at every place above $p$ is of discrete series type, and, through a member of the compatible system with interchanged Hodge-Tate weights, of potentially modular representations of weight $(2,k)$ over real quadratic fields with Steinberg type at one place above $p$, under conditions on that member.
Toward Quillen stratification for the odd primary Steenrod algebra

Fix an odd prime $p$ and let $A$ be the mod $p$ Steenrod algebra. There is a normal sub-Hopf algebra $D$ of $A$, and we show that the cohomology of $A$ is $F$-isomorphic to the subalgebra of the cohomology of $D$ which is invariant under the $A$-action. We also show that the sub-Hopf algebras of $A$ with bounded profile function detect nilpotence in cohomology.
Pseudo-Fredholm operators form a regularity on Hilbert spaces
Zakariae Aznay; Fadil Chabbabi; Hassan Zariouh

Let $H$ be a complex Hilbert space. We prove that the class of pseudo-Fredholm operators on $H$ is a regularity in the sense of Kordula and Müller. We also prove that the classes of left and right generalized Drazin invertible operators are regularities on $H$. Consequently, the generalized Kato spectrum and the corresponding generalized Drazin spectra satisfy the spectral mapping theorem. We construct an operator $T$ on a separable complex Banach space such that $T^2$ is right generalized Drazin invertible whereas $T$ is not pseudo-Fredholm. In particular, the power axiom need not hold for pseudo-Fredholm operators on Banach spaces. Finally, we show that the accumulation sets of the approximate point and surjectivity spectra define regularities on Banach spaces, yielding another proof of the regularity of generalized Drazin invertible operators in $\B(X)$.
Initial-Trace Insufficiency and Entropy-Accounting Separation in Finite-Volume Coarse Graining
Antonis Polemitis; Nicholas Christakis; Dimitris Drikakis

Coarse finite-volume information does not automatically define an exact pathwise closure for the restricted evolution of a fine-grid realization. We study two one-step information boundaries that are distinct from recursive predictive memory. First, we show that parent averages together with complete initial parent-interface trace pairs are sufficient for one forward-Euler finite-volume transition with a deterministic two-state numerical flux, but they do not generally determine a completed second-order strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta, equivalently Heun, transition. An explicit scalar upwind collision shows that hidden interior data can affect later stage traces and hence the completed parent update, even when initial traces and parent averages agree. Second, we show that exact conservative one-step closure is not the same as entropy-accounting closure. A parent entropy balance obtained from a cellwise numerical entropy balance contains a subcell Jensen gap, a realized entropy-flux difference, and residual dissipation. For a declared Burgers-Rusanov conservative flux and a declared Rusanov-type numerical entropy flux, we construct a sign-indexed finite family in which all branches have identical parent averages, identical conservative interface registers, and identical next parent averages, while the entropy-interface register distinguishes every branch. Under the uniform branch law, the conservative channel leaves nonzero deterministic squared-error floors for both the raw entropy register and its cyclic divergence. The results give a concise finite-volume information-sufficiency test for multistage interface data and entropy-side accounting.
Balance in Inequality: Testing the Physical Equilibrium, Precession, and Structural Stability of Magic Gems

A magic square exemplifies balance in inequality: its $n^2$ entries $\{1,\dots,n^2\}$ are distinct, yet every row, column, and main diagonal sums to $μ_n=n(n^2+1)/2$. Lifting centred grid cells into $\mathbb{R}^3$ as radial vectors $\mathbf{p}_{ij}(λ)=(x_j,y_i,λz_{ij})$ and taking their convex hull---the Magic Gem $\mathcal{G}_λ(S)$---asks: when does line-sum equality suffice for equilibrium in 3D, and when a nonlinear realization breaks balance, how can an opposing inequality restore it? We test this across all $880$ order-$4$ magic squares in four regimes. For radial spokes from $O$, natural lengths balance identically, while unit spokes break equilibrium on all $832$ non-associative squares in 3D and on all squares in 2D, where the ring-radius ratio $r_2/r_1=\sqrt{5}$ bounds the resultant below by the Pell convergent $9/4\approx\sqrt{5}$. By length--weight duality, balance is restored via tip weights $\mathbf{w}^*>\mathbf{0}$ on $S^2$ or power-law spoke scaling ($r^{α^*}$ in 2D and $(\mathbf{V}_3)_z=0$ in 3D). In 3D rotation, equal point masses make every semi-magic square an axisymmetric top with spherical-top transition $λ_{\mathrm{iso}}=(n^2+1)^{-1/2}$, whereas entry masses $m_{ij}=s_{ij}$ expose the quadrupole $Q_{xy}=\sum z_{ij}x_jy_i$, triggering $180^\circ$ Dzhanibekov flips on $824$ squares. Passing to the uniform solid hull $\mathcal{G}_0(S)$ shifts the centroid off $O$ on $829$ squares; re-engaging the opposing core $\mathcal{G}_1(S)$ restores balance via two-density inclusions, nested wireframes, or the $K_{n^2}$ strut network, while all $880$ hulls unfold into non-overlapping nets with $f_0-1$ glue tabs. Finally, $λ=1/5$ stabilizes $74.5\%$ of facets on a table, and alternating $\mathcal{G}_λ(S)$ with its mirror twin $\mathcal{G}_λ(r^2\overline{S})=-\mathcal{G}_λ(S)$ locks chiral blocks into a vertical tower.
Binomial Artin-Schelter Regular Algebras and Twisted Monoid Algebras

We study four-dimensional binomial Artin-Schelter regular algebras and their connection with twisted monoid algebras. Starting with $23$ examples up to permutation of generators, we investigate the associated monoids of I-type and the structure of their groups of fractions. We determine the corresponding finite permutation groups and compute the second group cohomology $H^2(G(M),k^\times)$. These computations allow us to construct explicit families of four-dimensional Koszul Artin-Schelter regular algebras through cocycle twists. We illustrate this construction for some of these algebras.
On the optimality of truncation among binary linear sketches
Robinson D. H. Cung; Adway Girish; Emre Telatar

We study statistical inference and function evaluation problems in which the input binary vector is available only through a binary linear sketch, i.e., a fixed number of parity measurements. We show that under a certain monotonicity condition, simply truncating the input by retaining a subset of its coordinates is optimal among all linear sketches of the same size. In particular, this applies to distributed testing of correlations of binary vectors when they are of opposite signs and evaluating unate Boolean functions on uniformly random inputs. Additionally, given that truncation is optimal, we immediately have lower bounds for arbitrary binary linear sketches. To illustrate this application, we consider the one-way communication complexity of a distributional graph connectivity problem on $n$ vertices and show that truncation, and hence all binary linear sketches, requires $Θ(n \log n)$ bits to achieve constant error, while a nonlinear protocol only requires $O(\log n)$ bits.
The first non-trivial Fučík curve for the sublinear Dirichlet Laplacian
Elie Alhelou; Gisella Croce; Giovanni Pisante

Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a bounded open connected set, and let $q\in(1,2)$. We consider the sublinear $q$-eigenvalue problem for the Dirichlet Laplacian $-Δu=λ\|u\|_{L^q(Ω)}^{2-q}|u|^{q-2}u$, $u\in H^1_0(Ω)\setminus\{0\}$, whose first eigenvalue $λ_1(Ω)$ is simple, with eigenfunctions of constant sign. The definition of a second eigenvalue is not unique. Following the approach introduced by Molle and Passaseo for the linear Laplacian, we construct the first non-trivial curve of the corresponding Fučík spectrum, and show that it has a unique diagonal point $(γ(Ω),γ(Ω))$. The Fučík-selected second value $λ_2^F(Ω)=2^{1-\frac{2}{q}}γ(Ω)$ is strictly larger than $λ_1(Ω)$, admits a two-phase variational characterisation, and satisfies a sharp Hong-Krahn-Szegő inequality: among sets of given measure it is minimised by the union of two equal balls. The selected solution at the diagonal point is a classical $(2,q)$-eigenfunction exactly when its nodal $L^q$-masses are balanced. We finally show that on balls in dimensions $N\geq2$ every Fučík-selected solution is foliated Schwarz symmetric.
Rings in which every semiprime left ideal is an intersection of prime left ideals

We study rings over which every semiprime submodule of every module is an intersection of prime submodules. This holds if semiprime two-sided ideals satisfy ACC, if principal two-sided ideals are finitely generated as left ideals, or if the ring is PI. Over Jacobson PI rings, every finitely generated module is Jacobson: its prime submodules are intersections of maximal submodules. For affine PI algebras this extends the Amitsur-Procesi theorem to modules.
 In every ring with involution, real two-sided ideals are intersections of real prime two-sided ideals. The same holds for real submodules of modules over PI rings and hereditary Noetherian prime rings, but can fail for real left ideals in Noetherian domains. Formally real affine PI algebras need not be real Jacobson: their real prime two-sided ideals need not be intersections of real primitive ideals. We give a sufficient positivity criterion. Over real Jacobson PI rings, finitely generated modules are real Jacobson: their real prime submodules are intersections of real maximal submodules.
 Over finitely generated free associative algebras, every finitely generated semiprime submodule of a finite free module is a finite intersection of finitely generated prime submodules and an intersection of maximal submodules of finite codimension. Semiprime hulls of finitely generated submodules are finitely generated. Evaluation at finite-dimensional irreducible representations and nonzero vector tuples gives a Hilbert Nullstellensatz over arbitrary fields. For free algebras with involution, the corresponding real results are known over the real or complex numbers when the involution permutes the generators. We extend real prime decomposition to arbitrary fields and involutions, and give new algebraic proofs of the real Nullstellensatz and finite generation of real radicals, without the GNS construction or Groebner bases.
Invariant random subgroups of the finitary special linear group over a finite field

An invariant random subgroup of a discrete group is a conjugation-invariant probability measure on the space of its subgroups. We confirm a conjecture of Simon Thomas and classify the invariant random subgroups of the finitary special and general linear groups over a finite field. These are shown to be stabilizers of random tuples of vectors and functionals. The classification uses the character theory of the finitary special linear group established by Skudlarek and the theory of the invariant random subgroups of the finitary permutation group established by Vershik. In addition, we classify the invariant probability measures for several natural actions of these finitary groups.
Mixing Time of the Random-Pair Monte Shuffle

In the random-pair Monte shuffle on $n$ cards, each step chooses two positions independently and uniformly and exchanges their cards with probability $1/2$. The chosen positions are public; the decisions to exchange cards remain hidden. We prove that the mixing time in expected conditional total variation distance is $2n\log n+O(n)$, with an exact leading constant and an $O(n)$ cutoff window. To our knowledge, this is the first public-schedule Monte shuffle whose full-permutation mixing time has been determined up to an additive $O(n)$ term.
 The upper bound follows by comparing two executions with the same public schedule to a classical random-transposition walk. For the lower bound, we construct a schedule-dependent test function and estimate its variance using a matrix-averaging operator. Combined with the depth bound of Czumaj and Lingas, the mixing estimate gives public switching networks with at most $2n\log n+O(n)$ switches and $O(\log n)$ depth for fixed error and failure probabilities.
 The author obtained this result through interaction with GPT-6 Astra.
Well-Covered Powers: Cartesian Products and Cayley Graphs
Haobo Ma; Thanh Vu; Wenlin Zhang

We study graphs whose powers are well-covered, with an emphasis on Cartesian products and Cayley graphs. We first establish necessary conditions and sufficient criteria for Cartesian products, provide examples showing that a factor need not be well-covered and that two noncomplete factors can have the well-covered powers property, and classify several structured product families. In particular, we construct graphs satisfying the well-covered powers property for arbitrarily large diameters. We then show that the Cartesian square of a connected abelian Cayley graph is well-covered exactly when the graph is complete. We classify the well-covered-power graphs among connected circulant graphs of degree at most four. For Cartesian products of any number of complete graphs, we also prove that the recursive alphabet-size inequalities in the final conjecture are sufficient for all powers to be well-covered, prove partial converses for arbitrarily many factors, and give explicit obstructions for every binary prefix followed by one complete factor.
Discontinuities in optimal transport between nonconvex domains

We develop a new approach to studying discontinuity sets of measure-preserving convex gradient maps between nonconvex domains. Such maps optimize the Euclidean distance squared. Our idea is to introduce a new `phantom' optimal transport problem, that transports the missing mass from the convex hull of the target to the `excess' Monge--Ampère measure of the minimal convex extension of the Brenier potential. We show that the closure of the discontinuity set of the original map contains the support of this phantom target. Moreover, inside a planar source domain these two sets actually coincide; on $n$-dimensional domains they coincide $\mathcal{H}^{n-1}$-a.e. The Hausdorff exponent $n-1$ is sharp in every dimension $n\geq3$. For planar polygonal targets, we establish a quantitative global length bound for the closure of the discontinuity set depending only on the target geometry, valid for bounded positive densities.
The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
Argyrios Deligkas; Michail Fasoulakis; Stavros D. Ioannidis

Computing a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) point of a quadratic polynomial over the unit hypercube is known to be $CLS$-complete, when the coefficients of the polynomial are encoded in binary. We prove that the problem remains $CLS$-complete even when the coefficients are encoded in unary. This is the first problem proven to remain $CLS$-hard when the input is given in unary.
Classification of torsion of elliptic curves over sextic fields

We determine all the groups that appear as the torsion group of an elliptic curve over a number field of degree $6$. Apart from the $44$ groups that occur infinitely often, which were determined by Derickx and Sutherland, exactly four groups occur: $\mathbb{Z}/25\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$, $\mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/12\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$. The first three were known to occur, while the group $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is new. We also show that, up to isomorphism, each of the groups $\mathbb{Z}/37\mathbb{Z}$ and $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}\times\mathbb{Z}/24\mathbb{Z}$ is the torsion group of a single elliptic curve over a single sextic field. The methods build on those developed by Derickx and Najman for quartic fields and by the author for quintic fields. Among the new ingredients are a formal immersion criterion at the prime $2$ which uses the Cartier operator, and arguments with several diamond operators and with cuspidal divisor classes on quotients of modular curves.
Markovian Lifts and Multifactor Approximations for Weighted Sub-fractional Brownian Motion

We construct a Hilbert-space Markovian lift of weighted sub-fractional Brownian motion for $0<b<2$, including the logarithmic case $b=1$. A Laplace factorization represents the process as the boundary value of a forward curve. In the weighted Sobolev space with derivative weight $r^γ/(1+r)^2$, $0<γ<1$, right translation is strongly continuous and the noise operator is Hilbert--Schmidt if and only if $b+γ>1$. The state norm bounds the total variation of initial curves on compact intervals. For locally bounded deterministic temporal weights, this bound allows the driven scalar equation to be restarted from every lifted state. Under spatial Lipschitz assumptions, with additional time and derivative regularity in the Young case, the solution and forward curve form a time-inhomogeneous Markov process with $C_b$-Feller transitions; both coefficients may have linear growth. Discretization of the Laplace variable gives independent Ornstein--Uhlenbeck factors coupled to the original process through the same Gaussian noise. The nonlinear approximations converge uniformly in time in every finite $L^p$. For uniform spectral partitions with balanced cutoffs, the solution rate is $M^{-(b-1)/3}$ for $1<b<2$, while the uniform driver rate is $M^{-b/4}\sqrt{\log(2+M)}$ for $0<b\le1$. Under stronger coefficient assumptions, we derive error bounds for Young solutions and for the fully discrete scheme, retaining the dependence on the spectral cutoff and specifying joint mesh conditions.
A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $ζ$-function

By a theorem of Bagchi, the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) holds if and only if $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})ζ(s)/s$, $k \geq 2$, in the Hardy space $H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2})$, where $\mathbb{C}_α$ is the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s) > α$. The formal Möbius expansion $E = \sum_{k \geq 2} μ(k) G_k$ diverges on the critical line, by a theorem of Báez-Duarte. We study it in the scale of spaces $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$, where its convergence forces $ζ$ to be zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_α$. We prove that the partial sums $S_n$ converge to $E$ in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_α)$ for every $α> 1$, and that a single zero of $ζ$ in $\mathbb{C}_α$ keeps the best-approximation error $d_n(α)^2$ uniformly away from zero. We express the Möbius error $s_n(α) = \|S_n - E\|^2_α$ as a series with elementary terms, free of $ζ$, and compute it for $n \leq 10^6$: $s_n(1/2)$ oscillates without decaying, whereas for $α> 1/2$ it decays at a rate close to $n^{1-2α}$, much faster than the bound known under RH. On the critical line, $d_n(1/2)^2$ behaves like $0.046/\log n$ for $100 \leq n \leq 5120$, in agreement with earlier computations by Báez-Duarte, Balazard, Landreau and Saias.
The finite basis problem for varieties modulo x^3=0
Elena Kireeva; Alexei Krasilnikov; Vladimir Shchigolev

We prove that any variety of associative algebras over a Noetherian commutative ring with unity satisfying the identity x^3=0 is finitely based. This property has been known for the varieties satisfying the identity x^2=0. On the other hand, there are varieties satisfying the identity x^6=0 that are not finitely based.
Rényi mixing bounds for kinetic samplers via $L^2$ hypocoercivity

We study convergence in Rényi divergence of order two for underdamped Langevin dynamics, the bouncy particle sampler, and the Zigzag sampler, for a target $e^{-U}$ on $\mathbb R^d$ that satisfies a logarithmic Sobolev inequality, with $\nabla^2U$ bounded below by a possibly negative constant and, for the Zigzag sampler, also bounded above. For initial laws whose Rényi divergence from equilibrium is at most $R$, we show that it decays exponentially, at a rate that depends on $R$. With the friction or refreshment rate chosen according to $R$, the time needed to reach a fixed accuracy in total variation or in Rényi divergence is of order $\sqrt{R\log R}$ at fixed dimension and target parameters, improving the linear dependence obtained by directly converting exponential $L^2$ decay. The key idea is to use the logarithmic Sobolev inequality for the position target in place of the usual spatial spectral-gap estimate in the $L^2$ hypocoercivity argument. For the bouncy particle and Zigzag samplers, this order is sharp for the Rényi divergence on a one-dimensional Gaussian target, uniformly in the refreshment rate. For the Zigzag sampler in dimension at least two, Gaussian examples show that the mixing-time bound is sharp up to logarithmic factors in the worst case over strongly convex targets, in both the initial divergence and the upper Hessian bound; in particular, strong convexity alone does not give a uniform mixing bound.
Exact penalty methods with adaptive discretization for nonsmooth semi-infinite optimization

The paper considers a nonsmooth semi-infinite optimization problem in which the constraints are reformulated through a value function. Stationary points of the cutting surface approximations are studied, showing that stationarity is preserved in the limit under boundedness of the associated sequence of multipliers. Building on these results, an algorithm that combines the cutting surface approximations with a penalty scheme is devised, together with some proximal variants. An exact penalty result is established under suitable global conditions, and numerical results are reported to compare the methods with existing exact penalty and cutting surface algorithms.
A probabilistic score estimation using the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula
Jiatong Sun; Long Nguyen; Ning Jiang; Weiqi Chu; Yao Li

Score-learning methods generally lack pointwise supervision, which affects the training accuracy, particularly in regions where SDE trajectories are rare. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel method called \emph{BEL anchors}, which uses Monte Carlo score estimates at user-selected space-time query points. By combining a Feynman--Kac representation of the Fokker--Planck equation with the Bismut--Elworthy--Li formula, our estimator requires neither closed-form transition densities, spatial discretization, nor derivatives of the initial density. We derive its asymptotic variance and use the anchors as sparse supervised targets for existing score-learning objectives. Experiments show that BEL anchors improve implicit score matching in poorly sampled regions, prevent score-PINN collapse, and enable accurate sample regeneration in several numerical examples.
The Askey-Wilson Function is the Laplace Transform of a Positive Measure

The Askey-Wilson function $φ(x, γ)$ is a meromorphic continuation of the Askey-Wilson polynomials in their spectral variable off the lattice $γ= \tilde{a} q^m, m \in \mathbb{Z}_+$. We show that the analytic part of the Askey-Wilson function $φ^{an}(x, \tilde{a} q^γ)$ is the Laplace transform of a positive measure of total measure $φ^{an}(x, s_0) < \infty$, under certain conditions on the parameters governing the function. We deduce log-convexity of this function, as well as positive-definiteness and an integral formula for a certain intertwining operator associated with the Askey-Wilson operator $L$. This offers a $q$-analogue of several results, in the trigonometric limit due to Sahi-McSwiggen, and in the rational (i.e. Dunkl) limit due to Rösler.
Proper Conflict-Free Coloring on Structured Graph Classes: Bounds, Exact Algorithms, and Hardness

A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper vertex coloring in which every non-isolated vertex has a neighbor whose color appears exactly once in its open neighborhood. We study this coloring on chordal and ordered bipartite graph classes. For well-partitioned chordal graphs, we prove the tight bound $ω(G)\leq\pcf(G)\leqω(G)+1$ and give an $O(n^2)$ construction from a partition tree. Every assignment of lists of at least $ω(G)+1$ colors also admits a PCF coloring that respects the lists. Deciding whether $ω(G)$ colors suffice is NP-complete, even when the partition tree is a star. This also proves NP-completeness on chordal graphs when the number of colors is part of the input. For interval graphs, we prove that lists of size $ω(G)+1$ always suffice, improving the previous ordinary-coloring bound of $ω(G)+2$. We use matchings to characterize when $ω(G)$ colors suffice and give an endpoint algorithm taking $2^{O(ω(G)^2)}n^{O(1)}$ time. We also characterize the exact value when the clique number is at most three and give a linear-time algorithm from sorted interval endpoints. For biconvex graphs, we prove a tight five-color bound and give a direct exact algorithm taking $O(n^{33})$ time. For bipartite permutation graphs, a smaller dynamic program gives an exact $O(n^{17})$ algorithm. Finally, if a bipartite graph is convex over an ordered shore $X$, we prove the sharp bound $\pcf(G)\leq\lceil\log_2(|X|+1)\rceil+3$ and construct a coloring in linear time from the order.
Large time dynamics for non-autonomous weakly damped KdV-Burgers equations on the real line
Cung The Anh; Nesibe Ayhan; Bao Quoc Tang; Ingo Witt

The large time dynamics of the weakly damped non-autonomous Korteweg-de Vries-Burgers equation \begin{equation*} u_t + u_{xxx}+ uu_x + λu - μu_{xx} = g(x,t) \end{equation*} in the phase space $L^2(\mathbb R)$ is investigated. Due to the low regularity of the initial data, the framework of Bourgain spaces is employed. We first obtain the existence of a unique pullback attractor $\{\mathcal A_μ(t)\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ in $L^2(\mathbb R)$ for each $μ\ge 0$. Then we show an optimal asymptotic smoothing effect of the equation, namely the pullback attractor is compact in $H^3(\mathbb R)$. These results are proved by using an energy equation method, splitting solutions into parts with low and high frequencies and exploiting a dispersive regularization. Furthermore, the attractors are shown to be upper semicontinuous as $μ\to 0$ and have finite fractal dimensions in $H^1(\mathbb R)$.
Small Hankel operators on weighted Besov spaces

We characterize bounded small Hankel operators from $B_p(\om)$ to $\overline{B_q(\om)}$ on the polydisc for $0<p,q<\infty$, under explicit conditions relating the kernel parameter to the weight. When $q<p$, boundedness is equivalent to a weighted Besov condition on the symbol; when $p\le q$, it is equivalent to a weighted supremum condition on a shifted radial derivative. In particular, the diagonal case is characterized by the product Bloch space. The proof combines weighted Bergman duality and atomic factorization with local kernel estimates and randomized atomic tests.

We study min-plus Bruhat cells $B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$, where $B_{trop}^{(n)}$ denotes the set of all upper-triangular matrices over $\RR \cup \{\infty\}$, and $p$ is a permutation. It is proved that $\dim (B_{trop}^{(n)} \odot p \odot B_{trop}^{(n)})= \frac{n(n+1)}{2} + l(p)$, where $l(p)$ is the length of $p$ in Coxeter generators. Also we provide an explicit description of the cell $B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR) \odot p_0\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}(\RR)$ (up to a subset of dimension less than $n^2$) for the highest in Bruhat order permutation $p_0$. Finally, it is shown that for a tropically non-singular matrix $A$ for at most one permutation $p_A$ it can hold $A\in B_{trop}^{(n)}\odot p_A\odot B_{trop}^{(n)}$.

We introduce a one-parameter family of continuous distributions on the unit interval whose cumulative distribution functions are given by the odd-height power towers \(x\uparrow\uparrow n\) (\(n=1,3,5,\dots\)). The associated densities admit a simple recursive formula obtained by logarithmic differentiation. We prove that every such density is strictly positive on \((0,1)\) and integrates to one, thereby establishing that the construction yields a genuine probability distribution. Numerical investigation reveals a characteristic peak--dip--rise shape: a sharp mode lying just below \(e^{-e}\) for all examined heights, followed by a trough and a gradual recovery toward density value~1 at the right endpoint. We then identify the limiting distribution as the height tends to infinity through odd integers.
Indu Bala; Preeti Parashar; Swapan Rana

The algebraic and environmental characteristics of mixed unitary quantum operations are investigated. It is established that the composition of two uniformly n-mixed unitary channels is itself n-noisy, and this n-noisy property is shown to be an invariant under unitary equivalence. Furthermore, by utilizing majorization and the divisibility of Kraus rank-four unital qubit channels, we demonstrate that any unital qubit channel can be physically simulated using a three-dimensional maximally mixed environment. Together, these results advance the classification and physical realization of noisy quantum channels.
On silting theory for complete path algebras
Maximilian Kaipel; Daniel Labardini-Fragoso; Håvard Utne Terland

Let $Q$ be a finite quiver and let $Λ$ be the complete path algebra of $Q$ with respect to the arrow ideal. We study the mutation of silting objects in the bounded homotopy category of projective $Λ$-modules and characterise in which cases the mutation theories of silting complexes and 2-term silting complexes of $Λ$ are determined by those of a finite dimensional quotient $Λ/I$. This characterisation is closely related to a characterisation of 2-term silting finite quotient algebras.
Weighted Randomized Kaczmarz for Sparsely Corrupted Linear Systems
Jessie Chen; Ziyu Cheng; Yunhui He; Alona Kryshchenko; Jocelyn T. Chi; Anna Ma; Jamie Haddock

In this paper, we introduce a generalized weighted randomized Kaczmarz framework to approximate solutions to overdetermined linear systems whose measurements are perturbed by sparse, additive corruptions. The proposed framework samples equations with probabilities proportional to a user-defined weighting function of their corresponding residual magnitudes. Our work focuses on weighting functions that will reduce the influence of potentially corrupted equations, and provides analyses for a general class of non-increasing weighting functions. We derive one-step expected squared error bounds that separate progress on uncorrupted equations from the contribution of corrupted equations, and provide sufficient conditions for geometric convergence under one specific family of weighting functions -- threshold weighting. We also investigate adaptive exponential weights scaled by the median or median absolute deviation of residual magnitudes, requiring no prior knowledge of the corruption fraction or magnitudes. Lastly, we consider a family of inverse residual weighting functions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefit of such a generalized framework in its flexibility in developing approaches for settings in which information about the corruptions is known or unknown.
On the Geometric Structure of Hyperbolic Clifford Bundles and Associated Spin Groups

In this paper, we present the spinor structure associated with the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra of a real $n$-dimensional vector space $V$, which is denoted by $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$. Unlike the standard Clifford algebra, the Hyperbolic Clifford algebra $\mathcal{C}l(H_V)$ simultaneously accommodates both multiforms and multivectors in a single algebraic structure, making it the natural framework---known as the ``mother algebra''---for the study of superfields in theoretical physics and for generalizing the Clifford bundle formalism to hyperbolic structures arising in gravitational theories. The orthogonal groups and orthogonal transformations associated to the hyperbolic space $H_{V}$ are presented. The Clifford--Lipschitz group and the Pin and Spin groups associated with $\mathcal{C}l\left(H_{V}\right)$ are defined. Then, the frame bundle and spinor structure associated to Hyperbolic Clifford algebra is derived.
Timely Ground-Station Status Delivery via UAV-Assisted Data Collection and Hierarchical RL
Xiangjian Gao; Mohammad Moltafet; Hamid R. Sadjadpour

We consider a UAV-assisted status-update system in which a rotary-wing unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) collects updates from multiple sensors, stores the newest update of each sensor, and forwards selected buffered updates to a ground station (GS). We minimize a weighted sum of the time-average GS-side age of information (AoI) and UAV energy consumption over a finite horizon. The optimization is subject to half-duplex operation, sensor and UAV energy-causality constraints, transmission-rate and power limits, and a terminal-location constraint. Because collection changes the information age at the UAV but does not reduce the GS-side AoI until the buffered update is forwarded, mobility, collection, and forwarding decisions are coupled over time. We use a hierarchical AoI-energy actor-critic (HAE-AC) controller in which a coarse-timescale actor selects return-feasible UAV movements, while a deterministic per-slot scheduler constructs feasible collection or forwarding sets and assigns the minimum transmit power required for each scheduled transmission. In a 100-sensor deployment, HAE-AC reduces the average GS-side AoI by about 22% relative to an adaptive staleness-gated benchmark. Compared with forward-upon-collection, selective buffered forwarding reduces the number of downlink bursts by roughly 30% while increasing the number of collections per sensor by more than 23%.
A holomorphic Lie-Trotter product formula for nonlinear local semigroup

We prove a new, holomorphic version of the Lie-Trotter product formula for nonlinear local semigroups with a parameter. We show that the product converges to the solutions of a nonlinear evolutions equation with a parameter. The solution is holomorphic in time on a centered at zero conic set in the complex plane and depends continuously on the parameter, and analytically on the initial data.
Lemmas and Conjectures in Spectral Graph Theory

The corpus of Elie Duhamel and Tristan Cazenave~\cite{dc} contains $305{,}755$ automatically generated conjectures relating spectral and metric invariants of connected graphs. A pipeline generated with Claude Code (numerical refutation, proof by the SMT solver \textsf{z3} from a library of lemmas, discovery of new lemmas, formalisation in \lean~4/Mathlib) refuted $162{,}964$ conjectures and proved $117{,}390$ without any unproved hypothesis, of which $79{,}505$ are verified end to end in \lean{} for every connected graph. This document collects, with proofs written for mathematicians, the most interesting lemmas that were discovered and proved, the ten most useful lemmas, the ten hardest theorems, simpler proofs of known results (Bollobás--Erdős, Yang--Lu), and the unrefuted conjectures that we find most interesting. All the proofs are gathered in an archive
On the lower- and upper bounds of three-colored anti-Ramsey numbers

In this paper we study a relatively new Ramsey type graph parameter introduced by my Bachelor's thesis supervisor Nóra Almási, and her Master's thesis supervisor Maria Axenovich. The parameter $ξ(G)$ denotes the largest natural number $n$, such that there is a red-blue-green edge coloring of $K_n$, such that in the edge coloring all copies of $G$ represent all three colors. After a brief recap on Ramsey numbers, we precisely define $ξ(G)$, and take a look at its relations to the Ramsey numbers. In the third chapter we establish lower bounds on $ξ(G)$, in the cases $G=K_5$ and $G=K_6$, namely $ξ(K_5)\ge 19$ and $ξ(K_6)\ge 31$.
Learning Almost Complex and Complex Structures
Edward Hirst; Tancredi Schettini Gherardini; Tomás S. R. Silva; Jakob Stein

We study the numerical constructions of almost complex and complex structures on spheres and products of spheres up to real dimension six. Our general set-up parametrises almost complex structures via a global matrix field in an ambient Euclidean space, compressed by the tangent projector. The projector's algebraic residual measures the almost complex condition, while its Nijenhuis tensor is evaluated in the intrinsic norm of the round product metric. Polynomial features and neural networks are trained without prescribed targets to perform general searches for these structures. The almost complex search passes numerical admissibility checks on all nine examples that admit such structures and rejects $S^4$, where a topological obstruction is known. A matrix correction then enforces the almost complex identity, subject to a novel uniform admissibility condition. For integrability, a free polynomial representation with Levenberg-Marquardt optimisation learns the complex structures on $S^2\times S^2$, $S^3\times S^1$, $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^5\times S^1$, with the largest Nijenhuis norms found by adversarial search all below $10^{-9}$. These general searches were unsuccessful on $S^6$, $S^4\times S^2$ and $S^4\times T^2$. Therefore, for these three cases direct numerical reconstructions were built in torus-fibred coordinates. They are integrable by construction, satisfy their compatibility conditions to better than $10^{-11}$, and corroborate the recent constructions on $S^6$ and $S^4\times S^2$.
Survival-Time Risk Beyond Low-Order Channel Models: Identifiability and Scheduling
Ruifeng Zheng; Zhihan Xu; Pit Hofmann; Frank H. P. Fitzek

This paper investigates whether low-order packet-loss statistics suffice to assess survival-time risk under bursty packet losses, i.e., the probability that no update succeeds for a prescribed number of consecutive slots. Conventional models, such as the Gilbert model, characterize packet losses using the loss rate and mean burst length, but channels sharing these statistics may exhibit substantially different failure risks. We characterize the Markov channels one order above a given low-order fit that share its statistics and analyze their risks under acknowledgment-based scheduling with transmission budgets. We show that, with dense transmission attempts, risk is primarily governed by loss persistence beyond the modeled memory, and the worst-case channel need not be the most persistent one. Under limited budgets, retry spacing makes loss relapse probabilities important and can reverse the risk ordering of compatible channels. Numerical and measurement results show that low-order models can substantially underestimate the risk, highlighting the need for scheduling-dependent channel statistics.
Curve-Supported Concentrations of Vortices and Screw Dislocations Subject to Confinement

We study the concentration of logarithmically interacting defects, such as Ginzburg--Landau vortices and screw dislocations, on closed curves in two dimensions, subject to a confining field. We prove that a measure supported on a smooth closed curve solves the mean-field transport equation exactly when, in Lagrangian labels, the curve moves with the negative induced velocity and each label keeps its mass. This contour law is a gradient flow of the mean-field energy. We prove that the gradient of the energy on a curve has a leading term proportional to the operator $|D|$ with Fourier symbol $|k|$, which prevents every smooth equilibrium curve from being a local minimizer, in a gradient-flow analogue of the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability of vortex sheets. In a radially symmetric case with quadratic confinement, we find an explicit circular equilibrium whose linearization is diagonal in Fourier modes, and we show that, as $N\rightarrow \infty $, the linear spectrum of the regular $N$-gon converges, mode by mode, to that of the circle. Finally, we compute a critical point on two concentric circles with lower energy than the single circle, indicating a rich family of multi-circle equilibria.
Stationary distribution of active Brownian particles in a bounded domain
Alexandra Tzella; Daniel Loghin; David J. Needham; Jacques Vanneste

Self-propelled particles such as swimming micro-organisms often accumulate at boundaries. Active Brownian particles (ABPs), that is, particles moving at constant speed with an orientation undergoing rotational diffusion, provide a simple model. ABPs have a finite probability to be on the boundary. Their probability density therefore includes both regular bulk and singular boundary components. Exchanges between these represent capture at the boundary and re-entry into the bulk.
 We examine the distribution of ABPs in the stationary regime. We first obtain a similarity solution that describes the probability density near the turning points, where orientation is tangential to the boundary and particles re-enter the bulk. This shows that the bulk density is singular and the boundary density is non-differentiable. We then add spatial diffusion to the ABP model and investigate the limit $\eps \to 0$ of small spatial diffusivity. We use matched asymptotics to describe the regularising effect of a finite $\eps$, focusing on the vicinity of the turning points. We assess our predictions against numerical simulations using both lattice Markov chain and finite-element discretisations.
Statistical Stability and Linear Response for Suspension Measures under Base and Roof Perturbations

We study the dependence of canonical invariant probability measures of suspension semiflows on simultaneous perturbations of the invariant base density and the roof function. We compare two natural representations of the suspension measure: physical-height coordinates, in which the support depends on the roof function, and normalised-height coordinates, in which all measures are defined on a fixed cylinder.
 In physical-height coordinates, we obtain an exact fibrewise formula for the $L^1$ discrepancy between suspension densities and derive quantitative total-variation estimates. In normalised-height coordinates, we establish corresponding stability estimates through the product of the base density and the roof function. These results transfer quantitative statistical-stability estimates for the base densities to the associated suspension measures.
 For one-parameter families whose base densities are differentiable in $L^1$ and whose roof functions are differentiable in $L^\infty$, we derive an $L^1$ linear-response formula on the fixed cylinder and a bounded-Lipschitz first-variation formula in physical height. The latter contains a signed measure supported on the graph of the unperturbed roof. We further compute the exact first-order total-variation speed and prove that total-variation differentiability holds if and only if the first-order roof velocity vanishes almost everywhere with respect to the unperturbed fibre density. The results are measure-theoretic and do not require spectral or mixing assumptions on the suspension semiflow.
Sharp Weighted Hardy-Type Inequalities for Homogeneous Magnetic Potentials

We prove a sharp magnetic improvement of the family of weighted inequalities on the upper half-space $\mathbb{R}^{N+1}_+$ that interpolate between the Hardy inequality and the trace Hardy inequality. The magnetic potentials are of Aharonov-Bohm type, $\mathbf{A}(x)=|x|^{-1}\boldsymbol{a}(x/|x|)$, where the tangential field $\boldsymbol{a}$ may be singular on a closed subset of the sphere. We compute the sharp constant explicitly: it is given by the constant of the corresponding nonmagnetic inequality, evaluated in a virtual dimension that depends on the first eigenvalue of the magnetic Laplacian on the sphere. In particular, the magnetic trace Hardy constant strictly exceeds its Euclidean value whenever this eigenvalue is positive. The proof rests on a ground state representation of the deficit, which also shows that the sharp constant is not attained in the energy space.
 As a consequence, we obtain the sharp Hardy inequality for the fractional powers $(-Δ_{\mathbf{A}})^σ$, $0<σ<1$, of the magnetic Laplacian: the constant is the same on smooth functions supported away from the singular set and on the form domain of $(-Δ_{\mathbf{A}})^σ$, and it is not attained. Examples include the planar Aharonov-Bohm potential with nonintegral flux and, in dimension three, the Aharonov-Bohm potential and the Dirac monopole.
Factorized approximate inverse preconditioners in the tensor train format
Pau Torrente Badia; Daniel Pérez García; Artur Garcia-Saez; Stefano Carignano

We present a preconditioning pipeline that accelerates Tensor Train (TT) linear solvers for symmetric positive-definite problems. Extending the Factorized Sparse Approximate Inverse framework to tensor networks, we construct a preconditioner as the product of a TT operator and its transpose. This formulation is positive semidefinite for any bond dimension and truncation, and definite whenever the factor is non-singular, satisfying the mathematical requirements of the Conjugate Gradient method. We detail the construction of this preconditioner and its integration into Density Matrix Renormalization Group (DMRG)-like linear solvers. Performance evaluations show consistent iteration reductions for anisotropic diffusion and Poisson problems across various configurations, leading to net speedups of up to 25% in ill-conditioned settings of time stepping schemes that can reuse the approximate inverses. These benchmarks were performed with the open-source Julia library DifferenTT.jl, which we also introduce in this work to provide out-of-the-box access to these preconditioned pipelines.
Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz for the Toda chain from inverse scattering transform

The Thermodynamic Bethe Ansatz (TBA) procedure developed by Yang-Yang provides the free energy functional to be minimized via a variational problem. Their result not only gives the correct thermodynamics, but it also sets the framework for Generalized Hydrodynamics. Originally developed for quantum systems, this procedure has been recently successfully applied to (integrable) classical particle systems. However, this has never been done for classical field theories: no classical derivation has consistently accounted for solitons, breathers, radiation (dispersive modes), and their mutual interactions. We here derive the TBA equations for the Toda chain directly from its inverse scattering transform. This results in solitonic modes interacting with radiation, extending the soliton gas picture. We provide numerical verification of our equations against well established TBA equations in terms of particle modes. We expect the same procedure should apply to KdV, and pure radiative models as defocusing NLS and Sinh-Gordon, while we discuss current limitations in other models such as focusing NLS (and Ablowitz-Ladik) and Sine-Gordon.
On uniqueness of probability solutions to one-dimensional Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations
Vladimir I. Bogachev; Stanislav V. Shaposhnikov
We give new sufficient conditions for uniqueness of probability solutions to one-dimensional Fokker-Planck-Kolmogorov equations in the case where the drift coefficient depends on time.
A surface-group action on real-hyperbolic space with no Cannon--Thurston map

We present discrete, faithful and purely loxodromic representations of a closed surface group of genus 431, and of a free group, into the group of isometries of a finite-dimensional real-hyperbolic space for which no Cannon--Thurston map exists. The construction combines three ingredients: the small-cancellation strategy employed by Baker--Riley to construct a subgroup of an ambient hyperbolic group with no Cannon--Thurston map, the realization of these groups by octagon complexes, and a theorem of Desgroseilliers--Haglund that supplies a convex cocompact faithful representation of the ambient hyperbolic group on a real-hyperbolic space.
 These examples admit ray Cannon--Thurston maps, as defined by Halder, Mahan Mj and Sardar.
Combination Theorems and the Farrell--Jones Conjecture for Graph Products of Pairs

We study the Farrell--Jones conjecture for graph products of pairs and for fundamental groups of polyhedral products. We introduce a pair-deletion decomposition and a local notion of FJ-admissibility, and prove a vertexwise combination theorem for graph products of pairs. The criterion applies, in particular, to ordinary graph products, free-factor pairs, suitable normal pairs, and classes controlled by acylindrical Bass--Serre actions.
 For polyhedral products, we combine these results with their description by relative graph products and graph products of pairs. We also obtain bounds and exact computations for amenable category, together with applications to simplicial volume and Borel rigidity of closed aspherical polyhedral-product manifolds.
The Iterated Local Transitivity Model for oriented graphs
Anthony Bonato; MacKenzie Carr; Ketan Chaudhary; Trent G. Marbach; Teddy Mishura

Transitivity in social and other complex networks describes the tendency for two nodes with a common neighbor to become adjacent. We propose a new model for complex networks based on transitivity, called the Iterated Local Transitivity Model for Oriented Graphs (ILTO). The model generalizes the Iterated Local Model for Tournaments (ILMT). As in ILMT, oriented graphs are generated iteratively by cloning nodes and their adjacencies, with arcs between clones oriented either as the corresponding arcs between their parents or in the reverse direction. This process produces dense oriented graphs and, under suitable conditions, graphs with high connectivity and small diameter.
 We analyze the universality properties of ILTO, showing that, for generating sequences with infinite support, the base oriented graph determines which oriented graphs appear as induced subgraphs, unlike in ILMT. We study motifs in ILTO and show that when the base graph is a tournament and the generating sequence has infinite support, the model generates quasirandom tournament sequences. Finally, we study domination numbers, the cop number, and the dichromatic number. We bound the cop number in terms of the independence number of the base graph and show that, for each fixed base graph, the dichromatic number is $Θ(2^t)$ after $2t$ consecutive 0-steps.
Solutions of the space-fractional heat equation with polynomial growth: Liouville theorems and Schauder estimates
Serena Dipierro; Ovidiu Savin; Enrico Valdinoci; Riccardo Villa

With the aim of extending to parabolic equations the framework developed by the first three authors in [Dipierro, Savin, and Valdinoci, Rev. Mat. Iberoam. (2019)], we introduce a notion of (viscosity) solutions for the space-fractional heat equation modulo $k$. In turn, we are able to define $s$-caloric functions with polynomial growth at infinity, showing also related Schauder estimates, a Liouville-type result, and a stability property with respect to the $L^\infty_{\rm{loc}}$-convergence.
Ziad Ismaili Alaoui; Oded Lachish; Nikhil S. Mande

A tournament is an orientation of a complete graph. A vertex $v$ controls a vertex $u\neq v$ if there is a directed path of length at most two from $v$ to $u$, and a $δ$-king is one that controls at least $δ(n-1)$ vertices. In the query complexity model, each query reveals the orientation of an edge. Shen, Sheng and Wu [SICOMP'03] established an $Ω(n^{4/3})$ lower bound on the deterministic query complexity of finding a $1$-king, and a non-matching upper bound of $O(n^{3/2})$. Neither bound has been improved in over two decades, despite substantial progress on variants of the problem.
 For $δ$-kings with $δ< 1$, Biswas, Jayapaul, Raman and Satti [Discrete Applied Mathematics'22] showed that $O(n^{4/3})$ queries suffice to find a $\frac12$-king. Lachish, Reidl and Trehan [FSTTCS'22] improved this guarantee to $\frac12+\frac{2}{17}$ using $\widetilde{O}(n^{4/3})$ queries, and asked whether a larger fraction could be achieved within the same query bound.
 We answer this question affirmatively for every fixed fraction below one: for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, we give a deterministic algorithm that finds a $(1-\varepsilon)$-king using $O(n^{4/3})$ queries.
 The design of our algorithm is informed by a structural analysis combining a sparse regularity lemma due to Allen, Kohayakawa, Mota and Parente [Electronic Journal of Combinatorics'14] with a new sampling argument based on a reachability theorem of Afek, Gafni and Linial [arXiv'19].
One-Sided Hardy--Littlewood Maximal Operators on Variable Lebesgue Spaces Beyond Log-Hölder Continuity

We study the boundedness of the right-sided Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on variable Lebesgue spaces over the real line. Motivated by the $K_0$ condition for the classical Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator, we introduce a directional condition $K_0^+$ adapted to the geometry of the one-sided maximal operator.
 We characterize $K_0^+$ in terms of the uniform boundedness of a family of one-sided averaging operators and prove that it is a necessary condition for the boundedness of $M^+$ on $L^{p(\cdot)}(\mathbb{R})$. We also establish one-sided analogues of the modular and reverse Hölder estimates associated with the classical $K_0$ condition. These estimates constitute the main local ingredients in the proof of boundedness of $M^+$ under the combined assumptions $K_0^+$ and $N_\infty$.
Bayesian Filters via the Stochastic Category

We extend the categorical treatment of Bayesian filters to models with feedback, whose transitions and observations may depend on the past observations. We work in the stochastic category, whose objects are measurable spaces and whose morphisms are Markov kernels, which we refer to as stochastic morphisms. We systematically parameterize stochastic morphisms by a measurable space, and develop the calculus of conditioning in a notation intuitively compatible with classical probability theory, requiring neither string diagrams nor densities. A stochastic morphism into a product space is regarded as a parameterized family of joint laws, and its conditional law is again a stochastic morphism, so that the rules of conditioning become equalities of stochastic morphisms. We define the Bayesian inverse with respect to a parameterized prior and prove Bayesian coherence. A model with feedback is then a model whose parameter space grows with the observations, and we derive the Bayesian filter, prediction and smoothing for such models, with standard Borel hidden states and countably generated observation spaces. The affine Gaussian stochastic morphisms parameterized by a measurable space form a family strictly larger than the Markov category $\mathbf{Gauss}$, closed under composition and Bayesian inversion, in which we obtain the Kalman filter and the Rauch-Tung-Striebel smoother with feedback.
Conjugate radius and parabolicity along the Ricci flow

We study the behaviour of the conjugate radius under the Ricci flow on complete noncompact manifolds. We show that if $(M^n,g(t))_{t\in[0,T]}$ is a complete Ricci flow with nonnegative scalar curvature at $t=0$, the initial metric is parabolic and not Ricci-flat, and the Einstein tensor $\mathrm{Ric}-\tfrac12 Rg$ is bounded above, then parabolicity is preserved along the flow and the conjugate radius of $g(t)$ is finite for every $t\in(0,T]$. As an application, we prove that a complete noncompact gradient shrinking Ricci soliton whose volume growth is subquadratic, in the sense that $\liminf_{r\to\infty}\Vol(B(p,r))/r^2=0$, has finite conjugate radius.
Foad Sohrabi; Harish Viswanathan; Sivarama Venkatesan; Jinfeng Du; Aliye Özge Kaya; Navin Hathiramani; Pavan Koteshwar Srinath

The surge in global mobile traffic, driven by 5G adoption and emerging applications, necessitates new spectrum allocations for 6G systems. With most major swaths of spectrum below 15 GHz already allocated to other services, co-existence between cellular and incumbent services such as satellite or radar systems is critical to make such spectrum accessible for 6G. At the same time, the advent of artificial intelligence offers a new opportunity for designing more efficient spectrum sharing techniques. This paper presents four novel data-driven spectrum access techniques to enable efficient use of spectrum for the 6G era: 1) co-existence technique for efficient protection of fixed incumbent receivers within an established protection area; 2) data-driven approach for protecting satellite receivers via control of radiated power above the horizon; 3) spectrum sensing-based fast-time-scale physical resource block blanking; and 4) base station-based spectrum occupancy detection to enable fast-time-scale spectrum sharing with satellite and non-terrestrial network incumbents. These techniques leverage artificial intelligence and extreme multiple-input multiple-output capabilities to enable efficient spectrum co-existence/sharing while maintaining cellular network performance.
Seshadri constants of singular loci of line arrangements with at most twelve lines
Marcin Dumnicki; Łucja Farnik; Krishna Hanumanthu; Brian Harbourne; Piotr Pokora; Joaquim Roé; Halszka Tutaj-Gasińska

Let ${\mathcal L}$ be an arrangement of $d$ lines in the complex projective plane and let $Z={\operatorname{Sing}}({\mathcal L})$. A question of Pokora asks whether the multipoint Seshadri constant of ${\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{P}^2}(1)$ at $Z$ is always computed by a line of the arrangement containing the largest number of points of $Z$. We prove that the answer is affirmative for every arrangement of at most twelve lines. The proof uses a Bézout-type covering criterion, elementary restrictions on the intersection lattice, and a detailed analysis of the two extremal combinatorial types that can occur for twelve lines. One type is the Hesse arrangement; it is handled using a net of quartics through its twelve double points. The other type would yield a uniquely determined incidence structure on thirteen lines. We show that this incidence structure is not realizable over any field.
A generalization of the Dirichlet approximation theorem for affine actions on the real line

We study quantitative density of orbits of the free semigroup $Γ$ generated by two maps of $(0,\infty)$. For the Möbius pair $x\mapsto 1/x$, $x\mapsto x+1$ we show that every orbit is $O(n^{-1})$-dense in $[0,\infty)$, that every irrational number $u$ is approached at a rate governed by the continued fraction of $u$ (at least $n^{-2}$, exponential when $u$ has bounded partial quotients, and $\exp(-cn/\log n)$ for almost every $u$), and that for rational $u$ and rational starting points the rate $n^{-1}$ is optimal. For the affine pair $T_0(x)=x/a$, $T_1(x)=bx+1$ with $a,b>1$, which was studied by Bergelson, Misiurewicz and Senti, we prove that for every $x>0$ and $u\ge 0$ there are infinitely many $γ\inΓ$ with \[ |γ(x)-u|<C\,λ^{-|γ|},\qquad λ=\exp\!\Big(\frac{\log a\,\log\frac{a}{a-1}}{\log\frac{a^2b}{a-1}}\Big)>1, \] where $|γ|$ is the word length of $γ$ and $C$ is independent of $γ$. This exponential rate holds whether or not $\log_a b$ is rational, and the exponential order cannot be improved for almost every $u$. We also give a corrected version of the Kronecker-type estimate $|γ(x)-u|<(u+1)(t^{1/|γ|}-1)$. Finally, we discuss the approximation of real numbers by ratios of primes and by ratios of logarithms of primes, updated in light of recent results on gaps between primes.
Maxime Egéa; Hanyue Gu; Daniel Rudolf; Björn Sprungk

We study the multi-modal Laplace approximation, given by a weighted Gaussian mixture centred at the local minima of the negative log-density, for sampling from probability measures that concentrate around finitely many modes as an inverse-temperature parameter $n$ grows. Such distributions occur in Bayesian inference in the small noise or large data regime. We derive explicit, non-asymptotic bounds on the Hellinger distance between the multi-modal Laplace approximation and the concentrating posterior. The bound decays like $n^{-1/2}$ with $n$ and the constants depend only polynomially on the dimension $d$.
