Hongyu Chen; Li Ma; Li Sheng

On every unit-volume flat complex three-torus, we construct a solution of the volume-preserving conformal Chern--Calabi flow with a finite-time Chern Type-I singularity at any prescribed point. The full spatial supremum has an exact asymptotic coefficient, and prescribed rescalings converge to a complete nonflat radial shrinking solution. The positive part of Chern scalar curvature can remain arbitrarily small throughout the flow, as can each prescribed subcritical spatial curvature norm. We determine the punctured terminal metric, its one-point completion and unique nonflat tangent cone, and the terminal energy asymptotics. We also exclude Chern Type-II under a logarithmically improved critical weak $L^3$ bound on Chern scalar curvature, and prove a separate scale-invariant integral criterion involving first Chern--Ricci curvature. The constructed singular solutions satisfy both criteria.

Let $A$ be a ring such that the formal power series ring $A[[t]]$ is a unique factorization domain. Bayart's problem asks whether the formal power series ring in two variables $A[[x,t]]$ must also be a UFD. Equivalently, is every irreducible element $f\in A[[x,t]]$ prime? We prove that the answer is yes whenever the constant term of $f$ is an associate of $p^m$, for any prime $p \in A$ and $1\leq m\leq3$, and for $m=4$ if $A$ contains $\Q$. We also prove the following reduction: To prove a positive answer to Bayart's problem, it suffices to prove that $A[x][[t]]$ is a UFD whenever $A[[t]]$ is.
A Clifford-index approach connecting boundary Dirac fermions to sigma-model topological terms in the periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors

The periodic table of topological insulators and superconductors emerges from two distinct approaches: boundary Anderson localization and momentum-space K-theory. Connecting these approaches physically requires deriving the boundary sigma-model topological terms from the underlying fermion theories. We develop an index-theoretic framework for minimal massless boundary Dirac models in the eight real Altland--Zirnbauer classes. Its central ingredients are an elliptic cylinder operator interpolating between two sigma-field textures, a quotient index defined by the cylinder's graded Clifford symmetry algebra, and an index theorem identifying its protected zero-mode index with the relative homotopy class of the endpoint textures. To establish this correspondence, we deform the cylinder texture while preserving the kernel's index class and localize the obstruction to a Clifford defect. An exact oscillator-kernel calculation fixes the generator normalization. A field-independent congruence and a common regularization provide a real antisymmetric Pfaffian representative whose sign transport is related to the cylinder mod-two index by Witten's spectral-flow argument. This yields the nontrivial $\mathbb{Z}_2$ theta weight for one minimal physical module. Combining complex-parent anomalies with physical Clifford multiplicities and real-target periods also gives the real-class Wess--Zumino terms with unit spherical level. The framework thus provides an operator-level connection between boundary Dirac theories and the sigma-model topological terms associated with the periodic table.
Haagerup vertex operator algebras at central charge eight

Evans and Gannon showed that a positive vertex operator algebra of central charge eight whose representation category is the Drinfeld center $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$ of the Haagerup fusion category has one of two character vectors, with six or nineteen currents. Call such an algebra, if strongly rational, a Haagerup algebra. We prove that a Haagerup algebra $U$ has six currents, that $U_1 \cong \mathfrak{sl}_2 \oplus \mathfrak{sl}_2$ embeds into $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$ in one of two explicit ways, with levels $(1,39)$ or $(3,13)$, and we determine the lowest weight spaces of its modules and $U_2$ as $U_1$-modules. For the levels $(3,13)$, $U_2$ is one of four Galois conjugate subspaces, and the algebra it generates is unitary, $C_2$-cofinite and isomorphic to the algebra constructed by Jiao; for the levels $(1,39)$, $U$ contains the algebra announced by Riesen. The associated lattice of $U$ is that of the form $x^2+xy+10y^2$, resp. $3x^2+3xy+4y^2$, the two classes of the principal genus of discriminant $-39$. Exchanging them in the decomposition of $U$ over its Heisenberg commutant gives a Haagerup algebra $U^\natural$ of the other levels, and $U \mapsto U^\natural$ is a bijection between the isomorphism classes of the two cases. Consequently, if either explicit algebra of Jiao or Riesen is positive and strongly rational with representation category braided equivalent to $Z(\mathcal{H}_3)$, there are exactly two Haagerup algebras up to isomorphism, forming a single hyperbolic genus. The explicit algebras of Jiao and Riesen have rational forms. The proofs combine exact trace relations given by vector-valued modular forms, exact computations in a model of $V_{E_6 \oplus A_2}$, and genera of vertex operator algebras.
Mean Field Game Problem with Kantorovich Potential Coupling: An Attrition model
Avetik Arakelyan; Davit Alaverdyan; Naira Hovakimyan; Isaac Kaminer; Tigran Bakaryan

In this work we address a class of Mean-Field Game (MFG) systems on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{d}$ in which individual agent incentives arise from macroscopic, distribution-dependent objectives governed by the Wasserstein-2 ($W_{2}$) distance. Taking the first variation (Lions derivative) of the Wasserstein-based macroscopic functional yields a coupled forward-backward system of Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) and Fokker--Planck (FP) equations featuring a nonlocal coupling driven by the Kantorovich optimal transport potential. As a primary case study, we formulate a large-scale attacker-defender attrition model aimed at protecting High-Value Units (HVUs). By defining population-wise attrition rates via the $W_{2}$ metric and casting the defense strategy as a Pareto-optimal McKean--Vlasov control problem, we derive a concrete HJB--FP system with a Kantorovich potential coupling. We prove the local-in-time existence of classical solutions for this system using Schauder's fixed-point theorem. Finally, we compute the MFG dynamics by combining the Sinkhorn algorithm with ResNet-based Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and simulate two-dimensional attacker-defender engagements across diverse attrition parameters, control costs, and multi-HVU configurations.
Logarithmic Sobolev and exponential inequalities for submanifolds in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds

We establish a logarithmic Sobolev inequality for complete $C^{1,1}$ immersed submanifolds of dimension $m\ge2$ in Cartan--Hadamard manifolds with sectional curvature at most $-b^2$. The inequality retains the Euclidean sharp constant after subtraction of $(m-1)^2b^2$ from the Fisher and mean-curvature energy; this coefficient is maximal for a lower bound uniform over $b\ge0$. For immersed surfaces, we prove both a finite-domain critical exponential inequality and a global Ruf-type inequality with a positive $L^2$ term. Both have potential $|H|^2-b^2$, exponent $16π$ and an absolute multiplicative constant, and follow from one geometric heat-kernel comparison. The exponent and curvature coefficient are optimal. We classify Gaussian equality in the logarithmic inequality and geometric equality in the higher-dimensional Nash consequence. All inequality constants are independent of the codimension.
The inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition for the Suzuki and Ree groups
In this paper, we give verifications of the inductive Navarro-Alperin weight condition in [8] for the Suzuki and Ree groups at all primes.
Cutoff and a Gaussian-shift profile for the Rudvalis shuffle

The Rudvalis shuffle removes the top card and reinserts it uniformly at random in one of the bottom two positions. Hildebrand proved the classical upper bound $O(n^3\log n)$, and Wilson later proved the sharp lower coefficient $1/(8π^2)$, establishing the correct order but leaving the leading upper constant, cutoff, and the cutoff profile open. We prove that the full labelled shuffle has total-variation cutoff at \[
 \frac{n^3\log n}{8π^2} \] with a window of order $n^3$.
 The upper bound is obtained by writing one deterministic rotation of the shuffle as a nonnormal sweep of adjacent averaging projections, comparing that sweep to a weighted interchange generator, and controlling the entire regular-representation heat trace. The key sharp-window ingredients are heat-kernel smoothing through the Octopus Inequality, zero extension of deletion-harmonic ordered-tuple functions, a representation-theoretic multiplicity payment, and a sectorwise entrance estimate that disposes of all large Young-diagram deficits. For the profile, an exact complex one-card eigenfunction yields a deck statistic whose surviving first Fourier mode converges to a Gaussian shift. A matching full-deck $L^2$ bound then shows that this one-dimensional Gaussian likelihood ratio asymptotically exhausts all remaining information, giving the exact total-variation profile.
Orbital stability for the equivariant Chern--Simons gauged Landau--Lifshitz equation in $\mathbb{R}^2$
Guanghui Jin; Jinmyoung Seok; Jianjun Yuan

We study the equivariant Chern--Simons gauged Landau--Lifshitz equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For equivariance index $m\ge2$ and a potential $V\in C^{3,1}([0,2])$ satisfying $V(0)=V'(0)=0$, we first establish local well-posedness for the Cauchy problem at the $H^2$ level, with the sphere constraint written in the natural affine space $u-\vec n\in H^2$. For nonnegative $V$ we then consider an $m$--equivariant ground state of $H_ω=E+ωM$, $ω>0$. Under a constrained nondegeneracy condition for the polar Hessian, the conserved energy and mass give orbital stability in $H^1$. A Gustafson--Shatah type continuation argument, in which the Chern--Simons feedback is treated as a tame nonlocal zeroth-order perturbation, upgrades this conditional stability to global $H^2$ existence for all $H^2$ initial data sufficiently close to the ground state orbit in $H^1$. For the quadratic potential we also verify the nondegeneracy condition in a nonempty interior near-BPS regime approaching the self-dual point $(κ,ω)=(1,0)$. This yields a concrete family of globally defined orbitally stable ground states.
Energy-Dissipative, High-Order BDF Schemes for Simulating Geometric Flows via Energy Increments
Zhiqing Pan; Wei Jiang; Jiwei Jia

We propose energy-dissipative backward differentiation formula (BDF) methods for geometric flows in the Barrett--Garcke--Nürnberg (BGN) parametric finite element framework. Starting from a Lagrange-multiplier formulation, we replace the multistep approximation of the energy derivative by an energy-increment equation while retaining the BDF geometric equations. The Simpson quadrature and two interleaved time grids provide third- and fourth-order constructions. The positive quadrature weights ensure stepwise decay of the original discrete geometric energy for every nondegenerate solution of the nonlinear system. We establish an explicit conditional consistency bound for the scalar energy equation and a regularity criterion for the Newton system of curve-shortening flows. Then, the proposed schemes extend to simulating curve diffusion, mean curvature flow, and surface diffusion. Finally, numerical experiments demonstrate geometric accuracy, energy decay, good mesh distribution, and high performance of the proposed schemes.
Feynman--Kac Representation for Parabolic Equations with Memory: A New Class of BSDEs
Hanxiao Wang; Jiongmin Yong; Qi Zhang

This paper is concerned with the connection between parabolic equations with memory (MPEs, for short) and backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs, for short). To provide a probabilistic representation of MPEs, we introduce a new class of BSDEs, called BSDEs with memory (MBSDEs, for short). The main feature of MBSDEs is that, at the current time $s$, the generator depends not only on the current value $Y^{t,x}(s)\equiv Y^{s,X^{t,x}(s)}(s)$ but also on the future path $r\mapsto Y^{r,X^{t,x}(s)}(r)$, $r\in[s,T]$. This structure reveals a fundamental difference from classical BSDEs: in the classical setting, the time and space variables are coupled and inseparable, whereas in MBSDEs they are completely independent. We prove the well-posedness of these MBSDEs and show that their adapted solutions provide a probabilistic representation for the solutions of MPEs. Furthermore, under a monotonicity condition, we establish a comparison principle for one-dimensional MBSDEs, which enables us to develop a viscosity solution theory for MPEs. This generalizes the celebrated nonlinear Feynman--Kac formula of Peng [25] and Pardoux--Peng [22] to the case with memory, in both the classical and viscosity solution senses.
6G Uplink Waveform and Rank Selection under Distributed Reception
Yewen Cao; Fen Hou; Yulin Shao

The development of 6G uplink is expanding waveform and spatial transmission options, while distributed reception makes their relative merits depend on the spatial and frequency structure of the aggregate channel. We study the joint selection of cyclic prefix orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing and discrete Fourier transform spread OFDM at rank 1 and noncoherent rank 2 under common user equipment power constraints and centralized linear minimum mean-square error reception. We derive waveform switching thresholds at both ranks and a rank selection margin, establishing conditions for selecting among the four modes based on available transmit power, DFT despreading loss, and spatial multiplexing gain. We then characterize how port gains and correlations at individual access points (APs) form aggregate spatial separation and influence mode selection. At fixed port gains and available transmit powers, improving spatial separation without reducing it on any subcarrier increases the rank selection margin, while its effect on the preferred waveform within rank 2 depends on the frequency distribution of the improvement. Numerical results show that different AP deployments can favor different waveforms and ranks, even with the same receive antenna budget and comparable aggregate channel gains, including waveform switches at a fixed preferred rank.
Topping's diameter conjecture for immersed surfaces

We resolve Topping's diameter conjecture for closed immersed surfaces in Euclidean three-space, building on his recent result for embedded surfaces. More generally, we establish sharp diameter and mean-width estimates for compact connected immersed surfaces, possibly with boundary. As a consequence, we confirm the codimension-one case of the sharp length--diameter conjecture for immersed minimal surfaces.

We study the 2-connected subgraphs of minimally 3-connected graphs whose contraction preserves 3-connectedness. We show that every minimally 3-connected graph that is not a wheel or a complete bipartite graph $K_{3,n}$ contains a contractable 2-connected induced subgraph that is a cycle, a fan, a $K_{2,n}$ or a $K_{3,n}$. In addition, these subgraphs satisfy certain degree restrictions. We show that none of these four families can be discarded since for each one of the four families, there exists a minimally 3-connected graph containing a contractable induced 2-connected subgraph in that family and none in the other three families. Reversing the contraction process gives a new construction for 3-connected graphs using edge addition, expansions into prescribed 2-connected subgraphs and $Y$-sum.
Boundary Harnack principle for abstract supersolutions on uniform domains

We develop an axiomatic approach to the boundary Harnack principle on diameter-uniform domains in proper doubling metric measure spaces. Under critical-density and upper-contraction assumptions, we establish a scale-invariant one-sided boundary comparison between nonnegative supersolutions and positive solutions and Hölder continuity of quotients of positive solutions. Our framework does not require linearity or rectifiable curves. Applications include classical elliptic equations, spectral fractional Laplacians, harmonic functions on fractals, and Pucci operators.
Smoothed analysis of stability radii for the assignment problem

Every linear program can tolerate small changes to its costs and still yield a solution of the original problem. The size of this tolerance measures how robust an optimal decision is to noise or numerical error, and how much regularization the problem can support. Classical sensitivity analysis can determine this tolerance only from an optimal solution. This paper provides a priori lower bounds on two measures of this tolerance -- the optimality gap and the $\infty$-norm stability radius -- for the $n$-by-$n$ linear assignment problem over the Birkhoff polytope. The bounds derive from a smoothed analysis, which adds Gaussian noise with standard deviation of at least $σ$ in every direction to an arbitrary base cost. At every fixed confidence level, uniformly over the base cost, both quantities are at least of order $σ/(n\sqrt{\log n})$. The radius bound is asymptotically sharp. Under isotropic noise, the worst case occurs when every assignment has equal cost, and in this case, a scaled stability radius converges in distribution to a standard exponential variable.
Second-Order Asymptotics for the Scalar Gaussian Broadcast Channel

This paper characterizes the second-order coding region of the scalar Gaussian broadcast channel along the curved boundary of its capacity region. The characterization holds under both average and maximal error criteria and allows correlation between the receiver noises. At each interior point of this boundary, the second-order region is a halfspace, as in the work of Scarlett and the author on Gaussian multiple-access channels with degraded message sets. Achievability follows from spherical superposition coding with a blocklength-dependent power allocation. The main innovation lies in the converse. Using Ornstein--Uhlenbeck entropy dissipation and Gaussian functional inequalities, we construct an auxiliary observation through an additive Gaussian noise channel and establish quantitative relative entropy bounds for the channel output distributions conditioned on this observation. The strong functional representation lemma of Li and El Gamal then allows us to select a realization of its independent random seed to obtain a deterministic partition of the retained receiver-1 message set. The component label plays a role analogous to the auxiliary random variable in the capacity characterization, while providing the distributional control needed at the second-order scale. These properties guide the construction of auxiliary output measures whose likelihood ratios admit the cancellations and normal approximation needed to evaluate an information spectrum converse.
Spontaneous Geometric Structures in 2D MHD Flows

Under suitable spatial decay assumptions on the initial data, we establish precise asymptotic expansions of the velocity and magnetic fields for two-dimensional incompressible MHD flows at each positive time. We identify in the far-field profile the hexagonal pattern previously discovered for the 2D Navier-Stokes equations by L. Brandolese \cite{Bra22}, characterized by six equally spaced directions of faster decay for each component of $u(x,t)-u_0(x)$. Surprisingly, the corresponding contribution to the magnetic field vanishes identically, owing to an exact cancellation associated with the antisymmetric structure of the magnetic nonlinearity. Thus, at order $|x|^{-3}$, the hexagonal structure appears only in the velocity field.
Sharp Bounds for Edge Mappings of Graphs

The study of extremal problems for set mappings was initiated by Erdős and Hajnal in 1958. Alon and Caro, and later Caro, Patkós, Tuza and Vizer, studied related problems for edge mappings of graphs. For a graph $G$ with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges, let $g_0(G)$ be the minimum integer $N$ such that every mapping $f:E(K_N)\to E(K_N)$ satisfying $f(e)\cap e=\varnothing$ for every $e\in E(K_N)$ admits a copy $G^*$ of $G$ in $K_N$ with $f(e)\notin E(G^*)$ for every $e\in E(G^*)$. Gishboliner, Jin and Sudakov conjectured that $g_0(G)=O(n+m/\sqrt n)$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by constructing a family of graphs. We then prove that $g_0(G)=O(n+m^{3/4})$. Furthermore, for every $n\ge2$ and $m$ satisfying $\lceil n/2 \rceil\leq m\leq \binom{n}{2}$, there exists a graph $G_*$ with $n$ vertices, $m$ edges and no isolated vertices satisfying $g_0(G_*)=Ω(n+m^{3/4})$. Thus the upper bound is best possible in terms of $n$ and $m$.
1-Genericity Is Not Weihrauch Reducible to the Finite Intersection Principle

This paper shows that the problem of producing a Cohen $1$-generic real relative to a given oracle is not Weihrauch reducible to the finite intersection principle (FIP). More strongly, no nontrivial computable FIP instance admits a single Turing functional that produces an absolute $1$-generic real from every enumeration of every maximal centered set of indices. The argument combines a $1$-generic real that computes no perfect tree all of whose paths are $1$-generic with local constancy and a parametrization of maximal centered sets. This answers Question~9.10.25 of Dzhafarov and Mummert.
Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling

We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -Δu+u=λu\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<λ<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.
$\mathsf{RCA}_0$ Proves the Collapse of the Intersection Principles Hierarchy

This paper shows that the pairwise intersection principle ($2\mathrm{IP}$) implies, over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$, the existence of a Cohen $1$-generic real relative to every given set. Together with the known implications, this yields the equivalence over $\mathsf{RCA}_0$ of the finite intersection principle (FIP), $2\mathrm{IP}$, and $1$-GEN. In fact, FIP is equivalent to $n\mathrm{IP}$ for every fixed $n\geq 2$. These results give affirmative answers to Questions~1 and~2 of Cholak, Downey, and Igusa, and to Question~9.10.26 of Dzhafarov and Mummert. The proof uses cumulative, nested supports satisfying a finite Helly property and a decoding argument based on a least selected label. Neither $Σ^0_2$ induction nor $Σ^0_2$ bounding is required.
A sphere-product counterexample to the additivity of homology nilpotency

Homology nilpotency need not increase under a product with a sphere. We construct a simply connected, closed smooth manifold $M$ of dimension $53$, rationally elliptic with $\dim_{\mathbb Q}\bigl(π_*(M)\otimes\mathbb Q\bigr)=7$, such that $cat_0(M)=10$ and $Hnil(M\times S^2)=Hnil(M)=11$. The inequality $Hnil(X\times Y)\leq Hnil(X)+Hnil(Y)$ can therefore be strict even for a product of a closed manifold with $S^2$ as the second factor.
A log-concavity criterion for finite nonnegative linearization

In a 2005 survey, R. Szwarc asked for criteria, stated in the recurrence coefficients, for nonnegative linearization (property (P)) of finite orthogonal polynomial systems such as the Krawtchouk polynomials. For a finite three-term recurrence normalized to have row sums one, whose diagonal and downward coefficients have a constant nonnegative ratio, we prove that property (P) holds for every product, including products beyond the terminal degree, whenever the Newton coefficients of the profile $d_i=b_i+c_i$ are log-concave without internal zeros. The criterion contains the full positive Krawtchouk range and the dual $q$-Krawtchouk arrays, and through a quadratic decomposition of symmetric finite systems it covers Szwarc's quadratic system $Q_n$ in its sharp range $0<p_0\leq1/2$. As a limit to any such criterion, property (P) fails at coefficient distance $O((1-r^2)^N)$ from the Krawtchouk array of size $N$ with fixed ratio $c_i/d_i=r<1$. All theorems, corollaries and propositions are formalized in Lean 4.
Distributionally Robust Optimization over Incomparable Spaces
Junyu Chen; Jieling Shi; Yong Sheng Soh

Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) provides a principled framework for making decisions under uncertainty when the underlying distribution may be incorrectly specified. A widely used approach builds on ideas from optimal transport (OT) as a means of measuring differences between distributions. However, this depends on these distributions residing in the same space. In certain settings, the reference data distribution we have and the space on which we make our decision may be different, which renders classical OT techniques impossible. In this paper, we provide a new DRO formulation in which ambiguity sets are defined through the Gromov-Wasserstein distance, which is an extension of OT to pairs of distributions residing in incomparable spaces. We show that several seemingly unrelated optimization formulations, including conditional value-at-risk minimization, group distributionally robust optimization, robust graph $k$-median, and $k$-median with outliers, can be recovered as special cases of our formulation. We describe the computational aspects of solving the proposed formulation based on the doubly-nonnegative relaxation. Last, we illustrate the framework through experiments on clustering over incomparable spaces and stochastic graph $k$-median.
Counting Nilpotent Galois extensions with prescribed genus number

Let $G$ be a nontrivial finite nilpotent group. In this paper, we study the distribution of genus numbers of Galois extensions of $\Q$ with Galois group isomorphic to $G$, ordered by absolute discriminant. We show that the proportion of fields with any prescribed genus number tends to zero, and obtain a quantitative bound for this proportion. Moreover, if every element of order $\ell$ in $G$ is central, where $\ell$ is the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, we determine the orders of magnitude of the average genus number and its higher moments.
Short Paper No. 1: Relation between integer sequence A319433 and the maximum degrees of finite linear Jaco graphs

This short paper presents the interesting relation between integer sequence A319433 in https://oeis.org and the maximum degrees of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs $J_n(x)$ where $n = 1,2,3,\dots$. The result first appeared as a conjecture. Subsequently, a proof through AI-assisted mathematical reasoning came to the fore. Appropriate clarity remarks follow in the main text. It appears that $\textit{Golden ratio}$-like floor function plays an important role in the analysis of the graph structural properties of the family of finite linear Jaco graphs.
Wilker property, function spaces and hyperspaces

The Wilker property requires that a compact set covered by two open sets admit compact covering pieces inside those open sets. We study this property through products, compact-open function spaces and hyperspaces. We construct countable compact Fréchet--Urysohn $T_1$ hereditarily Wilker spaces with non-Wilker products and squares. For spaces whose compact subsets are closed, Wilker-ness is equivalent to every compact subspace being Hausdorff; this yields a positive product theorem when one Wilker factor has closed compact subsets. For an irreducible subset system $H$, we characterize preservation of $H$-sobriety by compact-open function spaces in terms of $H$-supercompactness of compact subsets of the domain, and show that Wilker spaces satisfy this criterion. The Hoare hyperspace of a space is Wilker exactly when binary union on the Scott space of its open-set lattice is jointly continuous for the ordinary product topology. Consequently, the Hoare construction preserves and reflects Wilker-ness on consonant bases, although preservation fails in general. We also identify core-compactness of the base with local compactness of its Hoare hyperspace and prove that the Smyth construction reflects Wilker-ness.
MDS Algebraic Geometry Codes of Square-Root Length on Hyperelliptic Curves

For every fixed genus $g\geq2$ and every $0<ρ<1$, we construct maximum distance separable (MDS) algebraic geometry codes over $\F_q$ for all sufficiently large odd squares $q$. Their parameters are $\bigl[n,\lfloorρn\rfloor,n-\lfloorρn\rfloor+1\bigr]_q$ with $n=\sqrt q+1+O_g(q^{1/4})$. The codes use full Riemann--Roch spaces on genus-$g$ hyperelliptic curves. They are not monomially equivalent to generalized Reed--Solomon (GRS) codes when $q$ is sufficiently large. An infinite subfamily has exact length $n=\sqrt q+2gq^{1/4}+1$.
Idempotent Ultrafilters and Closed Images of Complete Semilattices

We prove that every continuous homomorphism from a complete topologized semilattice to a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice has closed image, answering a question of Banakh and Bardyla. The main step is the convergence of idempotent ultrafilters on complete semitopological semilattices. We also prove that, for every complete subsemilattice $X$ of a Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $Y$, the natural order of $X$ is closed in $Y\times Y$. In particular, the natural order of every complete Hausdorff semitopological semilattice $X$ is closed in $X\times X$.
Secrecy Sum-Rate Maximization for RSMA-Enabled Pinching-Antenna Systems
Code Kebe; Saeid Pakravan; Wessam Ajib

This paper investigates secrecy sum-rate (SSR) maximization in a downlink rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA)-enabled single-waveguide pinching-antenna system (PASS) with an external eavesdropper. The RSMA power allocation, secure common-rate allocation, and pinching-antenna (PA) positions are jointly optimized subject to transmit-power, per-user secrecy-rate, and PA-placement constraints. To tackle the resulting nonconvex problem, an alternating-optimization framework is developed, combining successive convex approximation for RSMA resource allocation with feasibility-preserving projected gradient ascent for PA-position optimization. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently outperforms the considered benchmarks in terms of average SSR, demonstrating the benefits of joint RSMA resource and PA-position optimization for secure PASS transmission.
Rank-Optimal Sample Complexity of Riemannian Gauss-Newton for Low-Rank Matrix Recovery
Xunmeng Wu; Jian-Feng Cai; Zongben Xu; Zai Yang

In this paper, we study the recovery of an unknown rank-$r$ matrix $\boldsymbol{X}_\star \in \mathbb{R}^{n_1\times n_2}$ from Gaussian linear measurements using the Riemannian Gauss-Newton (RGN) algorithm. Each iteration of RGN solves the RGN equation followed by a fixed-rank retraction. We prove that, with high probability, RGN with spectral initialization converges quadratically to $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$ using $\mathcal{O} ( r(n_1+n_2)κ^2 )$ measurements, where $κ$ is the condition number of $\boldsymbol{X}_\star$. This is the first result to simultaneously achieve rank-optimal sample complexity and quadratic convergence for Gaussian low-rank matrix sensing. The key to the proof is a sharp spectral-norm analysis of the iterates, which requires controlling the inverse operator arising from the RGN equation. Our analysis develops an exact finite Neumann expansion of this inverse operator and combines it with a virtual-sequence decoupling argument and the restricted isometry property. Extensive numerical experiments support our theoretical findings and demonstrate the advantages of RGN.
Strong convergence of a slowly damped primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling, Tikhonov regularization and implicit Hessian damping
Yixuan Ma; Honglu Li; Yibin Xiao

This paper proposes a novel mixed-order inertial primal-dual dynamical system with general time-scaling and Tikhonov regularization coefficients, together with implicit Hessian damping, for solving convex optimization problems with linear equality constraints in Hilbert spaces. The proposed dynamical system incorporates slowly vanishing viscous damping and is developed based on a time-dependent Tikhonov-regularized Lagrangian. Under suitable assumptions, we establish fast convergence rates for the objective residual, the feasibility violation, and the primal-dual gap using a Lyapunov analysis. Moreover, we prove that the generated primal-dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm primal-dual solution. Numerical experiments illustrate the theoretical results and indicate improved convergence performance relative to the comparison dynamical systems.
A rigidity theorem for edge-connectivity under non-negative Bakry--Émery curvature
Kaizhe Chen; Shiping Liu; Haotian Yang

The edge-connectivity $κ(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of edges whose removal disconnects $G$, and it is bounded above by the minimum degree $δ(G)$. We classify all connected locally finite simple graphs with nonnegative Bakry--Émery curvature satisfying $κ(G)<δ(G)$. All such graphs are infinite. Consequently, every finite connected simple graph with nonnegative Bakry--Émery curvature satisfies $κ(G)=δ(G)$, confirming a conjecture of Chen, Koolen, and Liu.
The massive phase of the two-dimensional Heisenberg model is stable under small anisotropy

Polyakov predicted that the classical Heisenberg model on $\mathbb{Z}^2$ has exponentially decaying correlations at every temperature, and a proof of this has recently been posted. We show that the massive phase survives small anisotropy. For every inverse temperature $β$ there is $δ(β)>0$ such that the $S^2$-valued model with couplings $\sum_iJ^iσ_x^iσ_y^i$ has exponentially decaying spin two-point functions, uniformly in finite subgraphs with free boundary conditions and in edge strengths up to $β$, whenever $|J^i-1|\leδ(β)$ for $i=1,2,3$. For the easy-plane model with couplings $σ^xσ^x+σ^yσ^y+λσ^zσ^z$ this shows that the onset of the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless phase, proved by Garban and de Montgolfier for every $λ\in(-1,1)$, moves to zero temperature as $λ\uparrow1$: in free-boundary limits, correlations decay exponentially for every $β\le c |\log(1-λ)|^{1/2}$. The physical prediction is of order $|\log(1-λ)|$. The same holds for aligned single-ion anisotropy, which includes a confining potential $\varepsilon\sum(σ^z)^2$, and for nearly isotropic $O(n)$ models with $n\ge3$. The proof keeps the sign-cluster argument of the isotropic proof, using Ginibre's correlation inequality for anisotropic planar energies, and uses the rotation symmetry only on one finite annulus, where the anisotropy is a bounded perturbation of the Hamiltonian.
Xiaoquan Xu; Fengshuo Xu; Haitao Ji; Dong Qiu

Kernel retracts of co-sober spaces need not be co-sober, even when the ambient space is countably infinite and compact. We construct a co-sober $T_0$-space $Y$ and a continuous idempotent map $k\colon Y\to Y$ satisfying $k(y)\leq_Y y$ in the specialization order, whose image with the subspace topology is not co-sober. The construction starts from a countable compact $T_1$ KC anti-Hausdorff space of van Douwen type and adjoins an infinite chain. We classify the $k$-irreducible compact saturated subsets of the extension and show that each is a point saturation. The kernel operator collapses the added chain to a distinguished point while fixing the original space, thereby recovering the non-co-sober seed as its image. This answers negatively two questions of Xu and Zhao, concerning continuous kernel operators and arbitrary retracts, and contrasts with the known preservation of co-sobriety by continuous closure operators.
Mayur S. Gowda; Srinivasa Pranav; Shreyas Chaudhari; José M. F. Moura

Homogeneous gradient functions have widespread significance, including applications in maximum energy subspace selection and retrieval problems. Euler's homogeneous function theorem specifies how the potential associated with a positively k-homogeneous gradient field can be recovered directly from the field itself. We use Euler's theorem to build on GradNets and propose a homogeneous gradient network architecture that is guaranteed to correspond to the gradient of a homogeneous function. Then, we describe how monotone homogeneous GradNets universally approximate the gradients of k-homogeneous convex functions. The inductive bias of homogeneous GradNets enables them to outperform baseline ICNNs by up to 7dB in our max energy subspace projection experiment and by up to 13% higher accuracy, 98% fewer parameters, and 70% fewer FLOPS in our amortized inner product search experiment.
The most singular loci of twisted character varieties

For any simply connected almost simple group $G$ and any compact Riemann surface of genus $g>1$, we study the singular locus of the character variety which parametrises fundamental group representations with a twist by a central element $z$ of $G$. While for $z=1$ the most singular representations have values in a maximal torus (and are invariant for the Weyl group action) and for generic $z$ every $z$-twisted representation is irreducible, for a general $z$ we find that the most singular representations have values in a particular Levi subgroup $L_z$ up to conjugation. From the explicit Lie-theoretic description of $L_z$, we determine the structure of the maximal stabiliser groups, and prove that the most singular loci is a disjoint union of generic type $A$ character varieties.
Robust preconditioners for finite element approximations of control-state constrained optimal control problems governed by elliptic equations
Juan Zhang; Liang Ge; Jianwei Zhou

The goal of this paper is to derive robust preconditioners for integral control-state constrained optimal control problems governed by the second order partial differential equations with linear finite element approximations. We give corresponding discretized systems of the first order necessary and sufficient optimality conditions, and get six linear algebraic systems with saddle point schemes. Furthermore, we propose efficient block preconditioners to solve the corresponding linearized algebraic systems. With respect to both mesh sizes and inherent parameters, the robustness of proposed preconditioners is proved with explicit eigenvalues of minimal polynomials. Meanwhile, we design two algorithms and choose the incomplete $LU$ factorizations to deduce the computations. Two numerical experiments are given to depict the efficiency of our proposed preconditioners.
From Ghost SICs to SIC-POVMs: A Galois Reduction of Zauner's Conjecture

Symmetric informationally complete positive operator-valued measures (SIC-POVMs, or SICs) are optimal minimal measurements for quantum state tomography. Problem~1 of Horodecki, Rudnicki and Życzkowski's open problems in quantum information asks for SICs in infinitely many dimensions. By work of Appleby--Flammia--Kopp and Radchenko--Wheeler, ghost SICs, which satisfy the SIC equations with Hermiticity up to parity, exist unconditionally for $d\ge4$. We study the passage from ghosts to SICs. We compute all isolated points of the complexified SIC variety for $d=4,5,6$; exactly half are SICs. We prove that no symmetry of the SIC equations maps a ghost to a SIC, so the step is purely arithmetic, and that a SIC exists in dimension $d$ whenever the ghost overlap units satisfy a place law: each Galois conjugate is real or unimodular according to the infinite place of the real quadratic field $F$ below it. If the unit field is abelian over $F$, the place law is the Stark relation $c_-=κ$; equivalently, a Galois conjugate of an associated near-group fusion category is unitary exactly when it is pseudo-unitary. For $d$ a power of a prime $p\equiv5\pmod 6$ or of $3$, an infinite family, we prove that under the algebraic part of Stark's conjecture $c_-=κ$ is equivalent to the triviality of $κ$ on the Hilbert-class-field part of the unit field. That condition involves no complex conjugation, and it follows from a sign-free multiplet hypothesis. We state an explicit $GL_2$ reciprocity law for the squared ghost overlaps that implies $c_-=κ$, and we prove it for the computed algebraic overlaps in $d=5,7,11,15$ by Artin reciprocity and a check in every ray class. Zauner's conjecture remains open: the algebraic part of Stark's conjecture and the multiplet hypothesis are not proved here.
Variance Reduction Note 3: The Convergence of PAGE

The probabilistic gradient estimator (PAGE) alternates randomly between an accurate gradient refresh and a cheap recursive correction. This third expository note on recursive variance reduction explains the algorithm and gives a self-contained convergence proof for smooth nonconvex optimization. A Lyapunov function combines objective decrease with estimation error, turning the refresh probability into an explicit contraction parameter. The resulting expected oracle complexity is $O(n+\sqrt n\,ε^{-2})$ for finite sums and $O(ε^{-3})$ for online problems, with the other problem parameters fixed. Initialization, refreshes, and both evaluations in each gradient difference are counted. The presentation is pedagogical and makes no claim of a new algorithm or convergence rate.
Smooth numbers in simultaneous arithmetic progressions

We prove a mean value theorem on the distribution of smooth numbers in two simultaneous arithmetic progressions, with generalizing a result of Drappeau. Let $\varepsilon>0$ and $(\log x)^C<y<x^{1/C}$ for a sufficiently large $C$. Our result implies that $y$-smooth numbers are well-distributed in the residue classes of a fixed integer $a$ on average over moduli $\leq x^{5/9-\varepsilon}$ for each $|a|\leq x$, which improves Drappeau's range $\leq x^{6/11-\varepsilon}$. As an application, we show that a positive proportion of $y$-smooth numbers $n\leq x$ satisfy $\min(P^+(n-1), P^+(n+1))>x^{407/720}$.
Near-Optimal Learning of Quantum Many-Body Systems from Gibbs and Thermal Metastable States via the Stationarity Test

We study the problem of learning a finite-range quantum Hamiltonian on an $n$-qubit $D$-dimensional lattice from copies of its Gibbs states at a known inverse temperature $β$ or its thermal metastable states. Existing efficient algorithms at arbitrary temperature have sample guarantees with an $e^{\poly(β)}$ dependence, leaving open whether the exponent can be made linear in $β$. We achieve this improvement: for $β\ge1$, our algorithm learns all Hamiltonian coefficients to $\ell_\infty$-error $ε$ with probability at least $1-δ$ using $\tO\bigl(e^{O(β)}ε^{-2}\log(n/δ)\bigr)$ copies and total time $\tO\bigl(n e^{O(β)}ε^{-2}\log(n/δ)\bigr)$. The measurements act on individual copies and are supported on balls of radius $O\bigl(β^2+β\log(1/ε)\bigr)$. Our sample complexity achieves the optimal exponential order in $β$, with optimal $ε^{-2}$ dependence up to logarithmic factors.
 Building on the stationarity-test framework \citep{Bergamaschi2026Stationarity}, we prove a unified Fisher-information coercivity bound showing that errors in the candidate Hamiltonian produce a detectable signal with only an $e^{-O(β)}$ loss in sensitivity. The key is a smooth frequency filter whose bandwidth remains independent of temperature, together with sharper estimates relating this signal to the Hamiltonian coefficients. For thermal metastable states, the guarantee holds under local drift $ζ\le e^{-Cβ^{2D+1}}$, for a geometry-dependent constant $C>0$, and above an accuracy floor $\tO(e^{O(β)}ζ)$. The argument applies to both Gibbs and thermal metastable states and, combined with local measurements and projected stochastic gradient descent (SGD), yields both learning guarantees.

In this paper, we focus on well-filtered spaces. By using the Rudin sets and WD sets, we obtain the following results: (1) The product of arbitrary many Scott well-filtered dcpos is still well-filtered with respect to the Scott topology. Thus we give positive answers for two questions proposed by Xu and Zhao; (2) Let P be a dcpo with ΣK(P) being well-filtered and Q a RB-domain. Then ΣK(P\times Q) is well- filtered if K(P\times Q) is a dcpo; (3) A intrinsic characterization of the WD sets is given by using Scott open filters.
A co-sober Alexandrov space whose Scott power space is not co-sober

We show that the Scott power construction does not preserve co-sobriety. For a dcpo $P$, let $\operatorname{Fin}(P)$ be the poset of nonempty finitely generated upper sets ordered by reverse inclusion. We prove that co-sobriety of $Σ\operatorname{Fin}(P)$ implies co-sobriety of $ΣP$. The proof adapts the point-saturation and union argument used for full compact saturated power posets; the finite step follows from a result of Heckmann and Keimel. Applying this transfer to a dcpo with a non-co-sober Scott space yields a co-sober Alexandrov space whose Scott power space is not co-sober. We also construct a countable example for which the Smyth power poset is countable. In the countable example, the same poset is co-sober under the upper Vietoris topology but not under the Scott topology.
Every $k$-Quasi-Planar Graph Has Linearly Many Edges

For every fixed integer $k\ge2$, we prove that every simple graph on $n$ vertices drawn in the plane with no $k$ pairwise crossing edges has at most $C_kn$ edges, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. We allow any finite number of proper crossings between two edges, including edges with a common endpoint. For $n\ge3$, removing a small disk around each vertex turns the drawing into a family of arcs on a sphere with $n$ boundary circles. Each arc joins two different boundary circles, and different edges have different unordered pairs of endpoint circles. The arcs are therefore essential and pairwise nonhomotopic, with endpoints allowed to move along their boundary circles during a homotopy. Any family of pairwise intersecting lifts to the universal cover projects to distinct graph edges that cross pairwise. Its size is consequently at most $k-1$. Beeker and Lazarovich's theorem on surface patterns then bounds the number of arcs. Their estimate is linear in the size of a triangulation, and an explicit triangulation of the $n$-holed sphere has linearly many edges and triangles.
Du Bois cohomology of noncommutative spaces and the Hodge numbers invariance conjecture for singular varieties

We extend the definition of cdh-sheafified Hochschild homology from varieties to stable categories linear over a field of characteristic zero, thereby proving its Morita-invariance. The dimensions of its homology groups give meaningful numerical invariants of a category; we combine them with invariants coming from topological K-theory and Poincaré duality to prove equality of mixed Hodge numbers for singular complex projective Fourier--Mukai partners in several classes in dimensions two, three, and four, including normal surfaces and threefolds with rational singularities and equal irregularity.
 Beyond these applications, we construct Du Bois versions of topological cyclic homology of stable categories together with appropriate multiplicative structures, prove a Geller--Weibel-type result for the variants of negative cyclic homology we introduce, and give categorical characterizations of cohomological purity of proper varieties and the $\mathbb{Q}$-factoriality defect of complex projective threefolds with rational singularities.
On Emergent Geometry of the Generalized BGW Theory

We present a systematic study of the mathematical theory of the generalized Brézin-Gross-Witten (BGW) theory using methods from statistical physics. We prove the multidifferentials of the generalized BGW theory are given by the Eynard-Orantin topological recursion in a generic background with general coupling constants. Furthermore, we characterize the transition between the Witten-Kontsevich model and the generalized BGW theory. This approach yields a new proof of the Okuyama-Sakai conjecture, further elucidating the deep structural connections between these two fundamental models.
Nearby Lagrangians in the cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle
Yuan Gao; Weiwei Wu; Tianyu Yuan

We prove the nearby Lagrangian conjecture for the Klein bottle: every closed connected embedded exact Lagrangian submanifold of its cotangent bundle is Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section by a compactly supported isotopy. The proof passes to the torus double cover and builds on the theorem of Dimitroglou Rizell, Goodman, and Ivrii for the two-dimensional torus. The main step is to construct an isotopy compatible with the covering involution. We achieve this using holomorphic sphere rulings in $S^2\times S^2$ adapted to the zero section, allowing the construction to descend to the Klein bottle.
Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity

We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors, with alternating small differences, then lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for countable DSS families and uniform nuclear tails for norm-compact DSS families, together with common Hilbert-space factors and arbitrarily small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. The main equality is a candidate real-field proof; no complex-field equality is asserted.
A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus

We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

Order-invariant cluster first-order logic (CFO) and local-order-invariant first-order logic are two fragments of order-invariant first-order logic, both motivated by the study of invariant logics on classes of bounded degree. Our main result is that order-invariant CFO contains local-order-invariant FO on arbitrary classes of finite structures, settling the conjecture of Ghasemi and Grange that order-invariant CFO contains plain FO. By combining this with a collapse result of Ghasemi and Grange, we obtain the equivalence of FO, local-order-invariant FO, and order-invariant CFO on classes of finite colored graphs of bounded degree. The proof makes use of Gaifman normal form, which allows our translation from local-order-invariant FO to order-invariant CFO to be effective. Combined with the fixed-parameter tractability of model-checking for order-invariant CFO on bounded-degree colored graph classes, this shows that model-checking for local-order-invariant FO on bounded-degree colored graph classes is fixed-parameter tractable. To generalize our collapse and model-checking results beyond colored graphs, we use a method based on first-order interpretations which also yields a collapse of order-invariant FO to FO when restricted to graph classes of bounded shrub-depth. Finally, we give an application to the database-motivated frozen-witness logic of Abiteboul, Simon, and Vianu by showing that local-order-invariant FO contains deterministic frozen-witness FO, and thus that deterministic frozen-witness FO collapses to FO on classes of finite structures of bounded degree.
Eynard-Orantin Topological Recursions for Higher Weil-Petersson Volumes on Moduli Spaces of Super Riemann Surfaces

We derive an Eynard-Orantin topological recursion for intersection numbers involving Norbury's $Θ$-class together with $ψ$-classes and higher $κ$-classes. These intersection numbers encode higher Weil-Petersson volumes of moduli spaces of super Riemann surfaces. The resulting recursion is a higher-$κ$ deformation of the topological recursion associated with the Bessel curve, which encodes the Brézin-Gross-Witten model.
A Counterexample to Wooley's $L^1$ Question for Beatty Sequences

For real numbers $α$ and $β$, let $\mathcal{B}(α,β)=\{\lfloorαm+β\rfloor:m\in\mathbb{N}\}$. Wooley asked whether the exponential sum over $\mathcal{B}(α,β)\cap[1,N]$ always has $L^1$ norm $O_{α,β}(\log N)$. We give a negative answer. We construct fixed $α>1$ and $β$, with $1/α$ of finite Diophantine type, such that the $L^1$ norm is $\gg(\log N)^2$ for infinitely many $N$. Wooley also proved that this $L^1$ norm is $O_{α,β}((\log(2N))^2)$ when $1/α$ has finite Diophantine type. Our example shows that his upper bound is sharp.
Purity maxima, absolute separability, and spectral volumes of absolutely PPT states

For $m\otimes n$ systems with $n\ge m\ge3$, we determine the exact maximum purity of absolutely positive partial transpose (APPT) states and the unique maximizing ordered spectrum when $n\ge2m^2-4$ for even $m$ or $n\ge2m^2-m-4$ for odd $m$. Under these dimension assumptions, absolutely separable states have the same maximum purity, attained at the same unique ordered spectrum. The proof uses an outer polytope defined by two linear head--tail inequalities, each comparing a sum of the largest eigenvalues with a sum of the smallest.
 Under explicit multiplicity assumptions, we derive an exact matrix criterion for APPT membership of full-rank spectra with three distinct eigenvalues. For every $m\ge10$, this criterion gives explicit APPT boundary spectra at $n=4m-2$ and $n=4m$ that disprove both cases of the maximum purity conjecture of Ahiable, Kothakonda, and Winter.
 We also determine the exact completely absolutely separable (CAS) purity maximum and its unique maximizing ordered spectrum in every bipartite dimension. We prove that the inner APPT polytope consists entirely of absolutely separable spectra. The resulting linear sufficient condition for absolute separability strictly improves the reduction-map and eigenvalue-ratio tests. Finally, we compute the exact relative volumes of the CAS set and an outer polytope defined by a single head--tail inequality. Under the uniform measure on spectra, the CAS, absolutely separable, and APPT volumes have the same asymptotic order $\sqrt n\,e^{-κ_m n}$ for every fixed $m\ge2$, with explicit $κ_m>0$.
No infinite cluster at criticality for long-range percolation with fast-decaying interactions

We consider independent long-range bond percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ in which $x$ and $y$ are joined with probability $1-e^{-βJ(x-y)}$. Let $d\ge2$ and let $J$ be invariant under coordinate permutations and sign changes, positive on nearest-neighbour pairs, and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty} n^d\sum_{\|x\|>n}J(x)=0$. We prove that there is no infinite cluster at the critical parameter. Together with Berger's theorem for heavy tails, this gives continuity of the phase transition for $J(x)\asymp\|x\|^{-d-α}$ for every $α>0$ except $α=d$, in every dimension $d\ge2$, and for every exponentially decaying kernel satisfying these hypotheses. Previously the fast-decaying case was known for nearest-neighbour and uniform finite-range kernels, in $d=2$ for finite-range and exponential kernels, and in high dimension for sufficiently spread-out kernels. The proof adapts a recent renormalization argument for nearest-neighbour percolation on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ that is driven by a gluing inequality conjectured by Kozma and Nitzan. Long edges enter in two places: they can jump over the surfaces that a nearest-neighbour path must cross, and they let a cluster outside a box enter it from far away. We control the first with thick outer faces and the tail condition, and the second by measuring entrances through the total edge weight between a cluster and a box rather than through the number of boundary vertices.
Sequential convergence in the lower topology and co-sobriety of Scott spaces

We investigate how order structure controls sequential convergence in the lower topology of a poset and how this, in turn, governs topological duality and co-sobriety of Scott spaces. We first give a purely order-theoretic characterization of lower convergence. For complete lattices this yields a lower-limsup formula, and on complete chains the lower limsup coincides with the usual lattice limsup. We also characterize first countability of the lower topology at a point by the existence of a countable coinitial subset outside its principal ideal. We prove that every compact saturated subset of a Scott space is sequentially closed in the lower topology and deduce that, for every poset, the lower topology and the co-compact (de Groot dual) topology of its Scott space have exactly the same convergent sequences and limits. For coherent Scott spaces we identify the lower closure of a $k$-irreducible compact saturated set with its double-cone closure and obtain an infimum criterion for co-sobriety. Consequently, every bounded-complete dcpo with sequential lower topology has a co-sober Scott space. In particular, every countable bounded-complete dcpo, and hence every countable complete lattice, has a co-sober Scott space.
The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces

Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avilés, Japón, Lennard, Martínez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avilés et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.
Global straightening of solution manifolds for state-dependent delay equations

Let $U$ be an arbitrary open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be continuously differentiable. Suppose that each derivative $Df(φ)$, $φ\in U$, admits a continuous linear extension $D_ef(φ):C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)\to\mathbb R^n$, such that $D_ef(φ)χ$ depends jointly continuously on $φ\in U$ and $χ\in C([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$. We construct a $C^1$ diffeomorphism of $U$ onto an open subset of $C^1([-h,0],\mathbb R^n)$ which maps the solution manifold of $x'(t)=f(x_t)$ onto an open subset of the closed subspace defined by $φ'(0)=0$. This resolves an open problem posed by Walther concerning regularization of the entire solution manifold. The diffeomorphism preserves the value at zero and agrees with the original history on $[-h,-τ]$ for any prescribed $τ\in(0,h)$, and is uniformly arbitrarily close to the identity in the supremum norm. It is connected to the identity by a jointly $C^1$ family of diffeomorphisms. The same conclusions hold under the weaker assumption that the finite signed measures representing the derivatives of $f$ have no atom at zero. We also establish a corresponding theorem for separable real Hilbert-valued histories.
Linear-exponent bounds for the automatic complexity of rational diagonals modulo prime powers

Let $p$ be a prime and let $G$ be the diagonal of $N/Q$ in $m$ variables over the $p$-adic integers, with $Q(0)$ a unit. We prove that the $p$-kernel of the coefficients of $G$ modulo $p^α$ has size $K_α(G)\le p^{(|J|+1)α-1}+(p^α-1)/(p-1)$, where $J$ is an explicit finite support set determined by the Newton polytopes of $N$ and $Q$, and $|J|\le\prod_i(h_i+1)$ for $h_i=\max(°_{z_i}N,°_{z_i}Q)$. Thus the minimal automaton has $p^{O(α)}$ states for fixed input and prime. The general upper bounds of Rowland and Yassawi have exponents that are cubic in $α$ for Furstenberg series and of order $α^{m+1}$ for diagonals in $m$ variables. The proof combines a $δ$-decomposition with synchronous Cartier sections and a count of compatible histories; it requires no smoothness or ordinarity assumption. We give explicit transitions and derive bounds for Furstenberg series. For the Furstenberg series $F$ of $bx^2y^2+(1+ax+dx^2)y+cx^2$ with odd $a,b,c,d\in\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove $K_α(F)\ge9\cdot8^α/(64α-32)$ and $\lim_{α\to\infty}α^{-1}\log_2K_α(F)=3$. This exponent result rests on primitive reachability, parameter-independent normalized window frames, and an overlap estimate certified in a finite quotient of a rational Cartier lattice. An appendix also proves that the zero orbit in the Rowland-Yassawi automaton for $x^2y^2+(1+x+x^2)y+x^2$ has exactly $2^{α+1}+α+1$ states, resolving their orbit-size conjecture.
A solution to the Erdős-Sárközy product-density problem

Color each positive integer red or blue, and call an integer a same-color product if it is the product of two red numbers or of two blue numbers. Does there exist a universal constant $c > 0$ such that: For each fixed coloring, and for all sufficiently large $M$ (where "sufficiently large" may depend on the coloring), at least $cM$ of the integers among $1$, $2$, $\ldots$, $M$ are same-colored products (allowing for equal factors, and where each distinct product is counted once)? This problem was given (in an equivalent way) in Guy's famous text on unsolved problems in number theory, and was posed (in equivalent ways) by Erdős and Sárközy in 1990, in the proceedings of the 1988 Banff number theory conference, and 1993 [Colloq. Math.], and this problem seems to have remained open. We succeed in solving this problem, by proving that no such universal constant exists.
Long-time behavior of first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space

We establish the long-time behavior of solutions $U$ to first-order Hamilton-Jacobi equations in the Wasserstein space $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$. For a class of Hamiltonians with quadratic growth, including non-convex ones, we prove that there exist a unique ergodic constant $λ$ and a solution $V$ of the associated ergodic problem such that $U(t,m)-λt$ converges to $V(m)$, uniformly on $\mathcal{P}_2(\mathbb T^d)$, as $t\to+\infty$. Finally, we provide applications to mean field control problems and zero-sum differential games.
Robust Appointment Scheduling with Heterogeneous Costs

Designing simple appointment systems that under uncertainty in service times, try to achieve both high utilization of expensive medical equipment and personnel as well as short waiting time for patients, has long been an interesting and challenging problem in health care. We consider a robust version of the appointment scheduling problem, introduced by Mittal et al.\ (2014), with the goal of finding simple and easy-to-use algorithms. Previous work focused on the special case where per-unit costs due to under-utilization of equipment/personnel are homogeneous i.e., costs are linear and identical. We consider the heterogeneous case and devise an LP that has a simple closed-form solution. This solution yields the first constant-factor approximation for the problem. We also find special cases beyond homogeneous costs where the LP leads to closed form optimal schedules. Our approach and results extend more generally to convex piece-wise linear costs.
 For the case where the order of patients is changeable, we focus on linear costs and show that the problem is strongly NP-hard when the under-utilization costs are heterogeneous. For changeable order with homogeneous under-utilization costs, it was previously shown that an EPTAS exists. We instead find an extremely simple, ratio-based ordering that is 1.0604 approximate.
Spectral gaps near one quarter for Weil--Petersson random surfaces with growing cusp number

We prove that the spectral gap of a Weil--Petersson random hyperbolic surface of genus $g$ with $n=n(g)\ge1$ labelled cusps converges in probability to $1/4$ as $g\to\infty$, for every sequence $n=o(\sqrt g)$. More precisely, for each fixed $0<\varepsilon<1/4$, there are constants $C_\varepsilon\ge2$ and $g_\varepsilon\ge3$, independent of $n$, such that the expected number of nonzero $L^2$ eigenvalues in $(0,1/4-\varepsilon]$, counted with multiplicity and including residual eigenvalues, is at most $C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2/g$ whenever $g\ge g_\varepsilon$ and $g\ge C_\varepsilon(n+1)^2$. This proves a conjecture of Shen and Wu. A matching lower bound shows that the count estimate is optimal up to constants for each fixed $\varepsilon$, and that $n=o(\sqrt g)$ is necessary for convergence of the gap to $1/4$. The proof combines volume estimates uniform in the cusp count with polynomial approximation and a positive trace on truncated surfaces.

We study polynuclear growth (PNG) on the half-line with Poisson nucleations in the bulk and at the boundary. For every nonnegative boundary nucleation rate, we construct stationary measures and jointly stationary couplings under a common graphical environment, with profiles pinned at the origin. We realize these couplings as a measurable stationary PNG horizon and prove convergence to the half-space stationary horizon under Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling. The horizon convergence includes its base profile and positive representing measure, together with joint profile convergence at every prescribed finite parameter list. We also prove convergence of the height evolution from general upper-semicontinuous initial profiles to the half-space KPZ fixed point. The associated passage field converges locally uniformly to the half-space directed landscape, jointly with evolutions from finitely many initial profiles driven by the same environment. The convergence results cover the critical boundary window and every fixed subcritical boundary rate, including zero. All fixed subcritical rates produce the same limiting laws.
Almost global solutions of 2-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains without the second null condition

For 3-D quadratic quasilinear wave equations in exterior domains with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions and small initial data of size $\varepsilon>0$, the authors of two papers [M. Keel, H. Smith, C.D. Sogge, Amer. J. Math. 122 (2000), no. 4, 805-842; J. Amer. Math. Soc. 17 (2004), no. 1, 109-153] have shown that the lifespan ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}$ of smooth solutions satisfies ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}=\infty$ or ${\bar T}_{\varepsilon}\ge e^{C/\varepsilon}$, depending on whether the null condition holds or not, respectively. Moreover, our series of results for quasilinear wave equations in 2-D exterior domains are consistent with the corresponding results for the classical Cauchy problem.
Extremal permutations of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ with many good slopes and applications to quantum Latin squares

For $n\ge2$, a good slope of a permutation $f$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n=\mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is an element $m\in\mathbb{Z}_n$ for which $x\mapsto f(x)+mx$ is a permutation. We classify and count the equality cases for prime powers and products of two distinct odd primes. Non-affine equality cases exist for every composite $n\ge6$. We also prove the sharp bound $p_0-1$ for the size of a set of good slopes with invertible differences between distinct elements, where $p_0$ is the least prime divisor of $n$. Finally, we establish gap results below $\varphi(n)$ and apply our bounds to a construction of quantum Latin squares due to Ball and Simoens.
Adelic Galois representations are maximal for almost all Drinfeld modules

Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, let $q$ be an odd prime power, and set $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $F=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$. We study the Galois representations associated with rank $r$ Drinfeld modules of the form $φ_T=T+g_1τ+\cdots+g_rτ^r$, where $g_i\in A$ and $g_r\neq 0$. As a further consequence, we establish the existence of rank $r$ Drinfeld modules with surjective adelic Galois representations for every $r\geq 3$, extending previous existence results which were known for prime values of $r$.

We prove a splitting theorem for cosmological spacetimes which admit a globally $p$-harmonic Cauchy temporal function for some $p < 1$, without making any use of timelike lines. In Bartnik's context of cosmological and timelike geodesically complete spacetimes, we establish a Liouville-type unboundedness result which shows that globally $p$-harmonic temporal functions, $p < 1$, are necessarily Cauchy temporal. Moreover, using the theory of elliptic PDEs, we show that locally Lipschitz $p$-harmonic temporal functions with $p < 1$ are in fact smooth. Altogether, our work reduces the resolution of Bartnik's cosmological splitting conjecture to the global weak solvability of the $p$-d'Alembert equation for some $p < 1$ in the class of locally Lipschitz temporal functions.
Local Limit Theorem for Branching Processes in Varying Environments

Let $Z_{i,n}$ be the population at time $n$ descended from one particle at time $i$ in a branching process in a varying environment. Under two-sided bounds on products of offspring means, an integrable uniform second-moment tail condition, and nondegeneracy and unit positive-support gcd of all weak limits, we prove $\mathbb{P}(Z_{i,n}=k)\le C(n-i+1)^{-2}$ uniformly in $0\le i<n$ and $k\ge1$, and obtain a local limit theorem as $n-i,k\to\infty$ with $k\le L_0(n-i)$, without third-moment assumptions. These results extend the classical local probability estimates for critical Galton--Watson processes to varying environments.
An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws

For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$.
 Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circΦ^{-1}$.
 For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $Λ_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+Φ(-b_p))=\varphi(b_p)$.
 We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern.
 An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$.
 Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.
Improved first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions

We study the smoothed first moments of primitive quartic and sextic Dirichlet $L$-functions for which every nontrivial power of the character remains primitive. Assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis for the Dirichlet and finite order Hecke $L$-functions occurring in the proof, we obtain asymptotic formulas with errors $O(Q^{\frac{49}{58}+\eps})$ and $O(Q^{\frac{23}{26}+\eps})$, respectively. We follow the double Dirichlet series approach of Gao and Zhao. The main ingredient is a joint estimate for the two sums arising from the removal of rational prime divisors, with the Möbius coefficients retained. This gives a quotient of Dirichlet $L$-functions. Under GRH, we bound both the Dirichlet $L$-functions and their reciprocals. Combining the joint estimate with estimates for the generating series of Gauss sums gives larger regions of meromorphic continuation. These regions do not separate the possible secondary terms.
A secondary term in the first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet L-functions

P. Gao and L. Zhao obtained an asymptotic formula for the smoothed first moment of primitive cubic Dirichlet $L$-functions over $Q$ with conductors coprime to $3$, with a main term of order $Q$ and error \(O\left(Q^{\frac{7}{8}+\eps}\right)\) under the generalized Lindelöf hypothesis. Building on their double Dirichlet series, we assume the generalized Riemann hypothesis and separate an explicit secondary term of order $Q^{\frac{5}{6}}$, with error $O\left(Q^{\frac{23}{28}+\eps}\right)$.
Fully Discrete Error Analysis of the CSLDG Scheme with Numerical Characteristic Tracing and Spline Reconstruction

A semi-Lagrangian discontinuous finite element scheme based on the characteristic Galerkin method (CSLDG) is investigated.The scheme directly discretizes an integral invariant model derived from the coupling of the transport equation and its adjoint equation.we have established, for the first time, error estimates for the fully discrete CSLDG scheme over a general domain Ωin \mathbb{R}^d.The error is decomposed into three parts: the ideal numerical solution error (the difference between the exact solution and the spatial discretization), the time-dependent test function error (the deviation of the test function caused by the numerical characteristic backtracking via an ODE solver), and the upstream region approximation error (the integration region deviation induced by numerical characteristic backtracking and spline boundary reconstruction).Under either compact-support boundary conditions or periodic boundary conditions with the velocity field and the solution sharing the same spatial periodicity, without requiring incompressibility,and assuming the standard CFL condition (Δt=O(h)) linking the time step and the mesh size, the following results are proved:Using piecewise P^K polynomial spaces, the L^2 error of the ideal numerical solution attains a suboptimal order O(h^K); If the ODE solver order satisfies D \ge 2K+2+d, the overall error retains the suboptimal order even after incorporating the time-dependent test function error;When the upstream region approximation error is further taken into account, for d \ge 2 the overall error remains suboptimal O(h^K) provided the spline reconstruction degree satisfies r \ge \max(K+1+d, d+2);
Irreducibility of Full Multivariate Partial-Twuality Polynomials

For each nonempty finite simple graph, we study five full multivariate partial-twuality polynomials defined using matrix ranks and coranks over $\mathbb{F}_2$. Over an arbitrary coefficient field $K$, we give a necessary and sufficient criterion for nontrivial factorization in the Laurent polynomial ring by additive separation of the exponent function across a nontrivial vertex partition. For $\bullet\in\{τ,δτ,τδ,δτδ\}$, the full multivariate partial-$\langle\bullet\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z^{\pm1},\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected. For $δ$, we characterize the connected graphs whose polynomials are reducible by a condition on the parities of vertex degrees and of the numbers of common neighbors, and determine their irreducible factors. For each operation, the corresponding polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and at least one state has zero $z$-exponent. In particular, the full multivariate partial-$\langleδ\rangle$ polynomial is irreducible in $K[z,\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}]$ if and only if the graph is connected and bipartite.
Generating the liftable outer automorphism groups of regular cyclic covers

Let $R_n = \bigvee_{i=1}^{n} S^1$ be a finite connected one-dimensional CW complex with $n \geq 2$, and let $\mathrm{Out}(F_n)$ be the outer automorphism group of the free group $F_n$, where $π_1(R_n)\cong F_n$. Let $\mathcal{C}$ be the infinite chain of roses, and let $q_n:\mathcal{C}\longrightarrow R_n$ be the standard infinite-sheeted cover induced by $\langle τ\rangle$, where $τ$ is the unit translation on $\mathcal{C}$. In this paper, we establish $p$-Wasserstein bounds and Cramér-type moderate deviations for the multi-dimensional elephant random walk in the diffusive and critical regimes. Using a Gaussian convolution estimate with random covariance and the recursions for the conditional covariance, we obtain $W_{p,2}(\mathcal L(\widehat T_n),N(0,I_d))\le C_{a,d}pL_n$, where $\widehat T_n$ is normalized by its exact covariance and \[ L_n\asymp \begin{cases} n^{-1/2}\log n,&a\le1/3,\\ n^{-3(1/2-a)},&1/3<a<1/2,\\ (\log n)^{-3/2},&a=1/2. \end{cases} \] Consequently, we obtain radial Cramér-type moderate deviations for $x=o(L_n^{-1/3})$.
