For finite-rank $\R$-buildings whose Euclidean metric factor has finite linear image, we obtain an all-type local-to-global theorem, including the nondiscrete $\widetilde G_2$ case, with an explicit gap and without metric completeness; the linear-image restriction can be removed from the fixed-point conclusion when the Euclidean factor has dimension at most three. A tangent-cone criterion characterizes the gap and yields a cubical bound with optimal asymptotic growth $d/π$ in dimension $d$. For Hadamard manifolds, the gap is equivalent to uniformly bounded finite stabilizers in the isometry image, with stabilizer bounds of optimal polynomial growth in the gap constant.

An anti-quadratic nearly associative algebra $(A, \bullet, ω)$ is a nearly associative algebra equipped with a non-degenerate skew-symmetric bilinear form $ω$ satisfying the anti-associativity condition $ω(u \bullet v, w) = -ω(u, v \bullet w)$ for all $u, v, w \in A.$ In this paper, we investigate the structural properties and extension theory of these algebras. We prove that any anti-quadratic nearly associative algebra is inherently nilpotent of index at most $6$. Furthermore, we introduce a novel $T T^*$-extension method and show that every anti-quadratic nearly associative algebra arises from this construction. We also introduce the notion of a double extension and prove that every such algebra can be constructed by iterated double extensions. Finally, as an application, we give a complete classification of anti-quadratic nearly associative algebras of dimension at most $4$.
Fock Projections between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Spaces: Full-Range Boundedness and Compactness

The Fock--Bargmann projection \(P_t\) is initially an orthogonal projection on a Gaussian Hilbert space. We characterize the boundedness and compactness of \[ P_t:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal F_β^{p_2,q_2} \] and of its associated maximal projection \[ P_t^+:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow L_β^{p_2,q_2} \] for all \(t,α,β>0\) and \(0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2\le\infty\). Set \[ Δ(t;α,β):=t^2-2βt+αβ, \qquad d(p,q):=\frac1q-\frac1p. \] For both operators, boundedness holds exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with \[ q_1\le q_2, \qquad d(p_2,q_2)\le d(p_1,q_1). \] Both operators are compact exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with both of the above boundary inequalities strict. Thus boundedness forces the source exponents into the Banach range, whereas when \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), every target exponent is admissible, including quasi-Banach ones. Annular discretization reduces the problem to drifted Gaussian sequence operators, whose comparison with diagonal sequence operators yields the endpoint criteria and quantitative tail estimates. A dilation--multiplier transfer gives corresponding results for Gaussian-twisted Fock operators, including Berezin transforms.
Irrationality of values of $L$-functions for real Dirichlet characters

Let $χ$ be a non-trivial real Dirichlet character and $s$ be a sufficiently large integer. In this paper, we prove that among the first $s$ non-critical special values of the Dirichlet $L$-function associated with $χ$ at least $c\sqrt{\frac{s}{\log s}}$ are irrational, where $c$ is a constant independent of $s$. This is a substantial improvement on work of Fischler when $4$ divides the conductor of $χ$. Otherwise, our constant improves on work of Mistiaen. The proof adapts some techniques of Lai and Yu for odd zeta values to the case of $L$-functions. The lack of positivity arguments is overcome by applying an irrationality criterion by Lai and Sprang originating from the $p$-adic setting.
Improving the Optimization Landscape of Matrix Completion with $ε$-close Surrogates

Non-convex optimization is central to machine learning and AI, yet unlike its convex counterpart, it still lacks a general and principled framework. In this work, we try to highlight the importance of combining noisy perturbations with over-parametrization mathematically under the classic setting of matrix completion (MC). Matrix completion is an important non-convex recovery problem in which only a subset of a matrix's entries is observed, and the remaining entries must be recovered using low-rank constraints. This problem is notoriously difficult because observations are limited. However, we show that by injecting $ε$-level perturbations into the nullspace of the observation mask, we can construct noisy matrix sensing surrogates whose solutions remain $\mathcal{O}(ε)$-close to the ground truth with valid restricted isometry property (RIP) constants. The existence of RIP further enables powerful tensor frameworks to be applied with theoretical guarantees. This approach reflects a broader empirical trend in which stochasticity or noise improves the curvature of the optimization landscape, allowing over-parameterized (a.k.a large) models to better separate signal from noise. Assuming each matrix entry is observed independently, we establish quantitative recovery guarantees without explicit requirements on sampling rate or incoherence, and discuss how such assumptions can further strengthen our results.
The regular set of Ricci limit spaces

Let $(X,d,p)$ be a nontrivial pointed Gromov--Hausdorff limit of complete connected Riemannian $n$-manifolds satisfying $\operatorname{Ric}\geq-(n-1)g$. For $1\leq j\leq n$, set \[ \mathcal{R}_j(X) = \bigl\{x\in X:\text{ every tangent cone at } x \text{ is isometric to } \mathbb{R}^j\bigr\}, \qquad \mathcal{R}(X)=\bigsqcup_{j=1}^n\mathcal{R}_j(X). \] We prove that there is a unique $k$ such that $\mathcal{R}(X)=\mathcal{R}_k(X)$, answering the pointwise regular-dimension question originating in Cheeger and Colding's work~\cite[p408]{CC97}. We construct a volume-corrected heat entropy on RCD space and identify the distributional logarithmic-density defect $\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{Hess} f)-Δf$ by Green-volume regularization.
In this paper, we introduce and study the notion of 2-nil hyperideals of multiplicative hyperring.

This paper develops methods for simultaneous inference on component functions in additive models. We first propose bias-corrected smooth backfitting estimators inspired by least squares linear regression and establish their asymptotic properties. We then show that the distributions of the uniform errors of these estimators converge to a Gumbel-type distribution. Based on this distributional approximation, we construct simultaneous confidence bands and develop a practical residual-based procedure for testing the additive components. Simulation studies and empirical data analyses demonstrate that the proposed estimators reduce bias and improve estimation accuracy compared with several existing estimators. Moreover, the empirical coverage probabilities of the proposed simultaneous confidence bands are found to be comparable to those of their oracle counterparts.
LEO Constellation Analysis for Satellite IoT: An Analysis of Coverage Gaps and Retransmissions
Lowie Rombouts; Jeroen Famaey; Roger Sanchez-Vital

Low Earth Orbit (LEO) constellations are a promising way to connect Internet of Things (IoT) devices beyond terrestrial coverage, yet the intermittent visibility of their satellites imposes hard constraints on system and protocol design. Coverage probability and other snapshot statistics, which are often computed without accounting for the terminal's latitude, are insufficient for this purpose. Designers also need the temporal structure of coverage: the rate of coverage gaps, their duration distribution and mean, and quantities such as the probability that a retransmission succeeds after an initial transmission has failed. We develop an ergodic framework for Walker Star constellations in which these quantities reduce to spatial integrals over a two-dimensional torus that can be evaluated efficiently. We validate the framework against a seven-day Simplified General Perturbations 4 (SGP4) simulation of the Iridium NEXT constellation and find close agreement for the coverage probability, the revisit-time distribution, and the retransmission success probability. A comparison of Walker Star configurations further shows that constellations with similar satellite counts can yield substantially different packet-delivery probabilities with at most one retransmission, depending on the number of orbital planes. The results show that the ergodic model accurately gives the long-run values that finite time-domain simulations can only approximate, providing researchers with a tractable basis for the analytical modelling of IoT connectivity over non-terrestrial networks (NTN).
Stability of ideal Nash equilibrium points in generalized multi-criteria games, interval-valued games, and existence in single-leader--multi-follower problems
Urairat Deepan; Poom Kumam; Parin Chaipunya

We study the stability of ideal Nash equilibria in generalized multi-criteria games, in which each player's vector-valued payoff is ordered by a closed cone and the feasible strategy sets depend on the other players' strategies. Under compactness and continuity assumptions, the ideal Nash equilibrium correspondence is upper semicontinuous on the class of games admitting an ideal equilibrium. Our main result does not require the ordering cones to be convex or pointed. In fact, the ideal equilibria are exactly the common equilibria of associated scalar games when all the cones are convex. As consequences of our results, the stability of interval-valued games is derived and existence theorems for single-leader-multi-follower problems are proved for both optimistic and pessimistic sense.
Root-of-unity limit of the $A_{n-1}$ lens elliptic gamma function solution of the star-star relation

We study the root-of-unity limit of the multi-component spin solution of the star-star relation whose Boltzmann weights are products of lens elliptic gamma functions, and whose spins take values in $\mathbb{R}^{n-1}\times(\mathbb{Z}_r)^{n-1}$. When one of the elliptic nomes tends to a primitive $2rN$-th root of unity, the quasi-classical expansion gives at leading order the classical star-star relation of the Bazhanov-Sergeev multi-spin model; at the next order, under the standard assumptions on the saddle points, a $(\mathbb{Z}_{rN})^{n-1}$-state solution of the star-star relation, which depends on $r$ and $N$ only through $rN$. Real $\mathbb{Z}_n$-symmetric configurations of the continuous spins give elliptic $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ Kashiwara-Miwa type models labeled by $n$-torsion points. Extended to general primitive torsion points, these include the broken $\mathbb{Z}_{rN}$ model of Quano and Fujii, for which the star-star relation follows from their Yang-Baxter equation when $\gcd(n,rN)=1$. In the trigonometric limit the saddle point equations single out the spectral curve of the $\mathfrak{sl}(n)$ chiral Potts model of Bazhanov, Kashaev, Mangazeev and Stroganov, and the Boltzmann weights become those of that model.

We revisit the relation between discrete- and continuous-time stationary dynamic optimization, using both the Bellman and Hamiltonian descriptions. We study the problem of embedding discrete Bellman--Lax--Oleinik operators and the associated Hamiltonian cascades into continuous-time dynamics. Rather subtle obstructions to such embeddings emerge even under the most natural assumptions.
Let $K$ be a field which is strongly stable, that is, stable and strongly dependent. Then $K$ is finite or algebraically closed. This answers a question of Shelah.
Physically Constrained Kinematic Calibration for High-Precision Robotic Needle Guidance
Prabhu Nithin Gollapudi; Andreas Maier; Franziska Mathis-Ullrich; Water Zhao; Jia Wang; Siming Bayer

Percutaneous needle insertion is a common practice in minimally invasive procedures whose clinical success depends on accurate needle placement. However, achieving the necessary precision is a challenge for manual operators. Robotic assistance can improve targeting accuracy and reduce operator dependence, but residual millimeter-scale errors persist because nominal kinematic models do not fully represent the physical manipulator. This paper presents a robust bound-constrained kinematic calibration method designed to improve positional accuracy for a 6-Degree-of-Freedom (6-DoF) robotic needle-guidance manipulator. The approach uses physically plausible parameter ranges to regularize a compact 19-parameter geometric identification model. By treating these bounds as active optimization constraints rather than mere numerical safeguards, the framework effectively mitigates parameter coupling and overfitting, ensuring highly stable parameter identification. In simulation, the proposed method reduced end-effector Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) from 3.422 mm to 0.690 mm (a 79.8% improvement). In benchtop hardware experiments, the calibrated model achieved sub-millimeter validation accuracy, including 0.865 mm RMSE in experimental trajectory validation and 0.610 mm RMSE in a coordinate-lattice verification task. These results demonstrate that physically constrained kinematic calibration can enhance robotic needle-targeting accuracy, establishing a high-precision foundation for future clinical applications.

We consider probability measures whose distribution functions solve conjugate equations between two compatible systems of increasing maps on the unit interval. We give sufficient conditions for Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity in terms of finite compositions of the source maps and a lower mass estimate which holds at Lebesgue almost every point. Our result substantially extends a regularity theorem of Mantica and Totik by allowing nonlinear target maps and replacing their assumptions on convexity, concavity, and displacement near fixed points. The proof uses the mass criterion of Stahl and Totik from logarithmic potential theory. We give further sufficient conditions involving uniform mesh bounds, sets where derivatives equal one, and endpoint drift. Examples distinguish these conditions and show that the uniform version of the lower mass estimate can fail for regular conjugacy measures.
IRA Rigidity and boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras
Tattwamasi Amrutam; Yair Glasner; Yair Hartman; Yongle Jiang

We introduce the notion of Boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras and study their general properties. We show that every Boomerang subalgebra of $L(Γ)$ is the group von Neumann algebra of a Boomerang subgroup when $Γ$ is a countable $C^*$-simple acylindrically hyperbolic group or a finite product of such groups. Consequently, every such group is invariant random algebra (IRA) rigid: every IRA arises as the pushforward of an invariant random subgroup (IRS) under the group von Neumann algebra construction. We also establish IRA rigidity for adjoint $K$-split higher rank $S$-arithmetic groups, as well as for all countable mixed identity-free (MIF) groups and their finite products. Consequently, IRA rigidity holds for countable groups admitting a topologically free minimal extremely proximal action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points. The same conclusion holds for countable groups admitting a faithful minimal action of general type on a tree whose induced boundary action is topologically free, and for finite products of groups admitting either of these actions.
Tracy Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration

We study sample covariance matrices formed from i.i.d., centered, isotropic random vectors $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \mathbb{R}^M$, whose coordinates are allowed to be dependent. We assume the random vectors satisfy a concentration bound for their quadratic forms $q_i^T A q_i$. Under this assumption, we establish edge universality and obtain the Tracy--Widom law for the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix after appropriate centering and scaling. In particular, our result removes the unconditionality assumption in existing edge universality results for log-concave ensembles~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.
Beamfocusing Beyond the Near Field: Frequency Diverse Arrays for OFDM-ISAC Systems
Arda Akyazi; Ahmed Hussain; Asmaa Abdallah; Ahmed M. Eltawil; Abdulkadir Celik

Traditional phased arrays (PAs) achieve near-field (NF) beamfocusing through spherical wavefront curvature, but lose this range selectivity in the far field (FF). Frequency diverse arrays (FDAs) instead introduce frequency offsets across antenna elements. These offsets synthesize a range-dependent beam whose beamdepth is governed by the aggregate frequency-offset span rather than the physical aperture, thereby extending finite beamdepth into the FF. Although FDAs have been extensively studied for radar, their broader potential for wireless communications remains largely unexplored. Accordingly, this article examines how this capability can support wireless communications and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). We compare PA and FDA focusing mechanisms, explain FDA coupling and periodicities, and assess coexistence with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM). Integer-multiple offsets preserve alignment with the OFDM subcarrier grid and avoid offset-induced intercarrier interference under ideal synchronization, but require suitable symbol mapping and receiver processing. We also distinguish FDA beamdepth from waveform-based radar range resolution and discuss their complementary roles in sensing. For the configurations studied, FDAs offer no additional single-user spatial degrees of freedom. Interestingly, their principal benefit is multiuser separation through location division multiple access (LDMA). Numerical case studies under an idealized FDA channel model show that FDA-LDMA achieves higher sum-rates than PA-based schemes for users with small angular separation in the FF, even after accounting for the bandwidth reserved for frequency offsets.
Infeasible Momentum Orthogonalized Methods for Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold
Yuxuan Zeng; Qi Deng; Dongdong Ge; Yinyu Ye

We study deterministic and stochastic optimization over the Stiefel manifold, explicitly allowing iterates to deviate from the manifold rather than enforcing feasibility via retraction at each step. We introduce Landom, a Landing-type method that constructs momentum in the relative-gradient direction, maps this update to its compact polar factor, and combines the resulting tangential step with a step along the negative gradient of the orthogonality penalty to improve feasibility. Under operator-to-nuclear smoothness, Landom achieves an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the averaged nuclear norm of the relative gradient with exact gradients, and an $O(T^{-1/4})$ bound in expectation with stochastic momentum, bounded variance, and a fixed batch size. Our analysis also provides explicit pathwise bounds on the orthogonality residual, including its dependence on the step size and initial infeasibility. To address the coupling between objective and feasibility correction in Landom, we further propose Landom+, a two-timescale variant in which the tangential and normal step sizes are decoupled. By keeping the normal step size fixed, Landom+ achieves tighter control over the orthogonality residual following an initial transient while maintaining the respective convergence rates for stationarity. Numerical experiments across a range of applications illustrate that the proposed algorithms remain competitive with established manifold optimization approaches.
A Dual-Guided Column-Generation-Based Matheuristic for Integrated Railroad Blocking
Yida Xu; Zhengzhong Ricky You; Baichuan Mo

Integrated railroad blocking is a central planning problem in freight railway operations, which requires coordinated decisions on block design, blocking sequences, and block routing. We propose a dual-guided column-generation-based matheuristic (DG-CGM) that uses linear programming (LP) dual information to identify promising transportation paths and incorporates them into restricted mixed-integer programs to improve feasible solutions. Starting from an initial plan built by construction, DG-CGM alternates destroy and local repair with path generation, which uses dual prices from restricted LPs of a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation to identify promising transportation paths. When local improvements continue to stagnate, we further apply joint repair to combine alternatives across demand groups. To address the coupling between logical and physical path pricing, we introduce a joint reduced cost that eliminates path-specific dual variables from pricing, enabling more efficient column identification through exact labeling algorithms. We evaluate the performance of DG-CGM on both generated instances and real-world cases. On 150 generated instances with 50-150 nodes, DG-CGM achieves the optimal cost on 89 of the 91 instances solved to proven optimality by Gurobi, with a geometric mean runtime equal to 5.2% of that for Gurobi and a mean relative cost reduction of 3.4%. On six full-scale scenarios derived from the 2026 INFORMS Railway Applications Section competition data, each with 47,193 nodes, DG-CGM obtains feasible solutions within two hours that serve 95.9%-99.6% of the requested freight volume, providing practical blocking plans for large-scale railway operations. The code, instances, and computational results are publicly available at https://github.com/Zhengzhong-You/IRBP.
Strong well-posedness for cyclic catalytic reaction--diffusion SPDEs with mutation and immigration

We study cyclic catalytic stochastic reaction-diffusion systems with mutation and immigration. The equations have square-root catalytic coefficients and spatially colored noise. Under a condition requiring the cyclic inward drift to dominate the corresponding noise covariance, we establish global strong well-posedness for nonnegative initial states. Our approach combines positivity-preserving approximations, uniform energy estimates, and a concave power entropy that controls the occupation of states near zero. These boundary estimates allow us to derive a Hellinger stability inequality for two synchronized weak variational solutions, yielding pathwise uniqueness directly in this solution class. We then use joint compactness of the approximating solutions and their driving noise, together with martingale identification and the Gyongy-Krylov criterion, to construct a probabilistically strong solution on the prescribed Wiener space.
Twisted second moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions with applications to weighted one-level density

We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.
The lattice of antichains of intervals: Dyck paths, level sets, and sweep dimension

The Clarke-Cormack-Burkowski lattice $\mathcal{E}_n$ is the lattice of antichains of intervals of the chain $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, the algebraic structure underlying minimal-interval semantics, a query semantics used in information retrieval. We give an explicit, elementary anti-isomorphism between $\mathcal{E}_n$ minus its top element and the Stanley lattice of Dyck words of semilength $n+1$ (an anti-isomorphism whose existence is implicit in work of Ferrari and Munarini), under which the rank of an antichain is $\binom{n+1}{2}$ minus the area of the associated Dyck word. Hence the rank generating function of $\mathcal{E}_n\setminus\{\top\}$ is the reverse of the Carlitz-Riordan $q$-Catalan polynomial. Using a local limit theorem for the area of random-walk excursions, we confirm unconditionally an asymptotic formula of Takács: the size $λ_n$ of the largest level set of $\mathcal{E}_n$ satisfies $λ_n\simκ\,4^{n+1}/(n+1)^3$, where $κ\approx1.0807$. Finally, for the antichains of intervals of an arbitrary finite poset $P$ we study the sweep dimension, the minimum number of linear orders needed to separate every interval from every element outside it. It equals the Dushnik-Miller dimension of the lattice of convex subsets of $P$, it is the least $k$ for which $P$ maps into $\mathbb{R}^k$ so that every interval is the preimage of an upper orthant, and it lies between $\max(2,w)$ and $2w$, where $w$ is the width of $P$, both bounds being tight. Antichains of intervals embed, preserving joins, into $k$-dimensional staircase regions.
Riemannian Optimization on Unknown Manifolds via Stochastic Proximal Refinement
Ruixiang Wu; Jiahao Ai; Tinko Sebastian Bartels; Xuanzhuo Liu; Yifei Wu; Yu Mao; Tongxin Li; Costas Courcoubetis

We study Riemannian optimization on an unknown manifold accessed only through feasible samples. The central challenge is to turn feasible samples into optimization steps, i.e., the samples are drawn from the unknown feasible manifold, but do not directly provide the tangent spaces, projections, or retractions required by classic Riemannian methods. Moreover, regions with low objective values may be sparsely represented in the data, so directly sampling from a distribution fitted to these observations can require many draws to find better feasible solutions. We introduce Proximal Refinement on Implicit Smooth Manifolds (PRISM), which turns feasible-sample access into an iterative optimization procedure by repeatedly sampling an objective-aware proximal distribution conditioned on the current iterate. Theoretically, we show that PRISM recovers the effect of Riemannian-gradient refinement, leading to provable objective descent, feasibility (manifold adherence), and convergence toward first-order stationarity. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through synthetic experiments illustrating its geometric properties and applications to data-driven building control and diverse real world optimization tasks, highlighting its potential as a general framework for data-driven optimization across scientific and engineering domains.
New results on openly disjoint cycles in regular digraphs
Bin Chen; Wenshen Wu; Meishaung Chen

Given a digraph \(D\), let \(c(D)\) be the largest size of a collection of openly disjoint directed cycles through a common vertex, and let \(c_r\) be the minimum of \(c(D)\) over all \(r\)-regular digraphs \(D\). In 2005, Seymour asked whether every \(r\)-regular digraph satisfies \(c(D)=r\). Mader answered Seymour's problem negatively for every \(r\ge 8\), but conjectured that nevertheless \(\lim_{r\to\infty}c_r=\infty\). Recently, Steiner confirmed this conjecture by proving \[ \left\lceil \frac{3r}{22}\right\rceil \le c_r \le 7\left\lceil \frac{r}{8}\right\rceil. \] In this paper, we first answer Seymour's problem negatively for $r\in \{6,7\}$, and then improve Steiner's bound to \[ \left\lceil \frac{r}{6}\right\rceil \le c_r \le 5\left\lceil \frac{r}{6}\right\rceil.\]
Hanzhi Bai; Fuhong Ma; Jin Yan

Fix an integer $r\ge 3$. Let $K_r$ denote the complete graph on $r$ vertices and $t_{r-1}(n)$ the Turán number for $K_r$. For each integer $k$ satisfying $0\le k \le \binom{n}{2}-t_{r-1}(n)$, $\rev{ϕ_r(n,k)}$ denotes the minimum, over all $n$-vertex graphs with $t_{r-1}(n)+k$ edges, of the maximum size of a $K_r$-packing \rev{(a family of edge-disjoint copies of $K_r$)} in the graph. The problem of characterizing the behavior of $ϕ_r(n,k)$ has a long history and dates back to Erdős for the case $r=3$. \rev{Győri} proved that $ϕ_r(n,k)=(1-o(1))k$ whenever $k=o(n^2)$. We characterize the range of $k$ for which $ϕ_r(n,k)=(1-o(1))k$, showing that this equality holds if and only if $k=o(n^2)$. Moreover, we obtain an \rev{asymptotic} upper bound (which falls below $1$) for $ϕ_r(n,k)/k$ whenever $k/n^2$ converges to a constant $δ$ satisfying $0 < δ\le \frac{1}{2(r-1)}$.
Two-coloring the points of a projective plane
Aart Blokhuis; Ádám Markó; Tamás Szőnyi; Zsuzsa Weiner

Let us color the points of a projective plane of odd order $n$ with two colors, say red and blue. Erdős asked the question of determining the maximum number of balanced lines (that have the same number of red and blue points). The answer is $n^2$, and in the corresponding trivial coloring the unbalanced lines go through a point. In this paper, we consider the Galois plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,q)$ and determine the number of unbalanced lines for a non-trivial coloring. The problem can also be generalized to $(r,b)$-colored lines (see Definition 1.1) and in many cases we extend the results to the generalized problem. Our strongest result for Galois planes of prime order $p$ describes all 2-colorings with at most $\max\{3p+1,4p-22\}$ not $(r,b)$-colored lines (see Theorem 5.13). Finally, in case of the generalized problem, we allow even more not $(r,b)$-colored lines if $r$ is small and the order is prime (for more details, see Theorem 5.18).
Primes and the Möbius function over quadratic polynomials
Lasse Grimmelt; Jori Merikoski; Mayank Pandey; Alexandru Pascadi

We prove an asymptotic formula for the number of primes $p\leq X$ of the form $n^2+h$ for almost all $h \leq X^{1/2-o(1)}$. We prove that, for almost all $h \leq X^{2/5}$, the number of primes satisfies a correct-order lower bound. We also show cancellation of the Möbius function over $n^2+h$ for almost all $h < X^{1/2-o(1)}$.
Separating hash families with large universe II

For fixed integers $t,k\ge 2$, put $N=(t-1)(k-1)+1$. We prove that the maximum universe size of a $t$-perfect hash family of length $N$ over an alphabet of size $q$ satisfies $ p_t(N,q)\ge q^{k-o(1)}$. Together with monotonicity in the length, this gives a positive answer to a question of Blackburn, Etzion, Stinson and Zaverucha for every choice of feasible parameters. Our proof combines the Nash--Williams--Tutte theorem, a graph-theoretic elimination argument, and a solution-free-set theorem established in our previous work.
Cutoff for random Cayley graphs of finite groups

We study the random walk on a Cayley graph of a finite group whose generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random. We show that, for every finite group, the walk exhibits cutoff with high probability whenever the number of generators is at least a constant multiple of the logarithm of the order of the group and small compared with every positive power of it. This holds for both undirected and directed Cayley graphs, in discrete and continuous time, and the lower bound on the number of generators is best possible, up to the value of the constant. The cutoff time is the time at which the expected entropy of the walk comes close to its maximum, and in general it depends on the structure of the group. This settles a conjecture of Aldous and Diaconis.
Strong law of large numbers for random semigroups in norm topology

This paper studies the strong law of large numbers for products of random uniformly continuous semigroups in Banach spaces. We propose a novel approach by treating the product of semigroups as a solution to an integral equation and establish a version of the SLLN in norm topology for arbitrary Banach spaces.
On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (II): strong uniqueness
Yu Li; Longhuan Yan; Wenjia Zhang

We prove strong uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of a closed Ricci flow when one tangent flow is generated by a complete smooth asymptotically conical Ricci shrinker. The modified flow converges to this shrinker in a fixed gauge, with quantitative estimates on expanding domains. The main ingredients are a Łojasiewicz-Simon inequality for Perelman's entropy, based on the global weighted divergence-free gauge constructed in the preceding paper, and estimates controlling the geometric radius under Ricci flow.
Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions

This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits. The proof is an extension of Nordskova's argument to families, using semilinear autoequivalences and absolute Galois actions on geometric generic fibers to permute mutually orthogonal spherical objects. Then, we specialize the separation to closed fibers. In our examples, the spherical objects are constructed from rigid rational curves or spinor bundles on quadrics.
Yulin Chang; Jie Han; Patrick Morris; Lin Sun

In this paper we establish the following result for clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs when the cliques are large enough. For integers $k \geq 3$ and $t\geq t_0(k)$, we show that for every $α> 0$, there exists $C>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n\in(t+1)\mathbb{N}$, the union of a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum codegree at least $αn$ and a binomial random $k$-uniform hypergraph $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with $p\geq Cn^{-{t/\binom{t+1}{k}}}$ on the same vertex set contains a $K_{t+1}^{(k)}$-factor asymptotically almost surely. The bound on $p$ is asymptotically best possible and extends the graph case, resolved by Balogh, Treglown and Wagner. In particular, we have $t_0(3)=3$, which implies that our result applies to every $t\ge 3$ for $3$-uniform hypergraphs. Together with the previously established result for perfect matchings, this covers all possible clique sizes for $3$-uniform hypergraphs.
Kloosterman Sums and Plücker Height Zeta Functions
Li Cai; Jingsong Chai; Yadi Liu; Mingyu Yang

We establish nontrivial bounds for Kloosterman sums over $p$-adic fields associated with the longest Weyl element on arbitrary split reductive groups, at arbitrary level. As an application, we obtain the regularity of Bessel distributions (of Whittaker models) for all such groups.
Region-Preserving Accelerated Gradient Methods for Geodesically Convex Optimization

Accelerated Riemannian optimization methods often require a priori assumptions that their iterates remain in a region where geometric bounds hold. We develop a parameterized inertial dynamical system and an explicit accelerated gradient method for smooth geodesically convex optimization on Riemannian manifolds with locally bounded sectional curvature. Our setting allows both positive and negative curvature without requiring completeness of the ambient manifold. Starting from a curvature-corrected continuous model, we construct the discrete updates by eliminating indefinite cross terms in the Lyapunov energy difference and derive verifiable conditions for a fixed step size. The resulting energy analysis establishes preservation of the initial geodesic ball without assuming iterate containment in advance. We further establish accelerated convergence rates for both geodesically convex and strongly geodesically convex objectives, without requiring restarts.
Integral Harnack-type estimates and the rate of extinction for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations

We establish local boundedness and integral Harnack-type inequalities for locally nonnegative weak solutions to nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the fast diffusion range by combining refined energy estimates with a careful treatment of the nonlocal terms. As an application, quantitative decay estimates for both the local mass and the local supremum of weak solutions are derived near the extinction time. Furthermore, we study the extinction phenomenon for bounded nonnegative weak solutions to the Cauchy--Dirichlet problem and obtain quantitative upper bounds for the extinction time.
Exponential stability of port-Hamiltonian systems with unstructured, measurable Hamiltonian densities

For first-order port-Hamiltonian systems in the dissipative setting considered here, we characterise exponential stability without any further regularity or block-structure assumption on the Hamiltonian density, thus closing a gap persisting in the literature. The proof requires revisiting the computation of the adjoint generator of the port-Hamiltonian semigroup. Finally, we provide both examples and non-examples showcasing the inconclusiveness of known conditions on the Hamiltonian densities necessary for the application of characterisation results in the literature.
A reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and its extensions

We study reciprocal moments of the critical points of a polynomial with a simple zero at the origin. A positive similarity transforms a reciprocal derivative companion into a complex symmetric matrix. This gives a short proof of the reciprocal Schoenberg inequality and a refinement for every elementary symmetric function. We determine the optimal constants in the corresponding inequalities for every positive exponent, including the sublinear range, and extend the results to arbitrary positive charges. We also characterize the normal powers of the companion and of its symmetric representative. The resulting criterion gives the complete equality cases in two quartic inequalities and explains the appearance of noncollinear equality configurations at higher orders. We also obtain a closed generating determinant and a quantitative collinearity estimate.
RapidDOC: Riccati-Preconditioned Implicit Differentiation for Differentiable Optimal Control under Operator Mismatch
Xiangda Zhu; Yuankun Chen; Zifei Nie; Yi Chang

Differentiable optimal control embeds constrained optimization problems in data-driven pipelines by differentiating their optimality conditions and propagating task-loss gradients to model or objective parameters. A key observation is that forward optimization and backward sensitivity computation involve related stage-structured linear systems, making reuse of forward factorization information natural. However, direct reuse is generally invalid, because differences in linearization, barrier terms, regularization, and curvature can create a mismatch between the retained forward operator and the target operator defining the derivative. We therefore propose RapidDOC, a factorization-reuse method that leaves the target adjoint equation unchanged. The retained cache produces a candidate adjoint and, when its target residual exceeds the prescribed tolerance, serves as a fixed right preconditioner for GMRES. A cache-action error operator characterizes directional exactness, the preconditioned iteration, and the relation between target residual and outer-gradient error. An ablation on three constrained robotic OCPs shows that the proposed method achieves lower backward time than both target-system refactorization and a no-reuse iterative method, demonstrating the computational benefit of reusing the retained forward factorizations. Across open- and closed-loop parameter-learning experiments, the proposed method achieves learning performance comparable to the baselines, while yielding the lowest open-loop backward time on all three tasks and reducing total closed-loop solver-call time by 40.5-83.1% relative to the fastest competing method. Finally, deploying the learned controller on a physical vehicle reduces the median figure-eight tracking RMSE from 22.75 to 6.09 cm, demonstrating its potential for hardware deployment.
Existence, Equivalence, and Convergence of Unbalanced Optimal Transport

We study an unbalanced optimal transport problem with a spatially independent signed source. The target density is continuous on a bounded domain or continuous and integrable on $\mathbb R^n$. We establish sequential weak lower semicontinuity at the critical Sobolev regularity $W^{1,n}$ and existence of minimizers under prescribed distortion and Jacobian mass bounds, provided a finite-energy admissible pair exists. For domain-preserving, uniformly bi-Lipschitz affine flows, we prove an energy-preserving static-dynamic correspondence and stability of the reconstruction. Within this class, sequential $Γ$-convergence identifies the strong source-penalty limit as transport minimization among pairs of minimum source cost. This yields optimal-cost asymptotics and subsequential convergence of minimizers and their reconstructed paths. When a constant source is admissible, optimal sources converge strongly in $L^2$ to the constant determined by the endpoint mass difference. We establish local constant-source feasibility for Hölder endpoint densities near a fixed reference pair and give a quantitative obstruction showing that constant-source feasibility may fail even when admissible pairs exist.
Sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding algorithm for sparse optimization problems
Zhong-Feng Sun; Nan Meng; Yun-Bin Zhao

In this paper, we propose a sparse descent direction derived from the Newton direction within a low-dimensional subspace for sparse optimization problems. Building upon this direction and incorporating hard thresholding and orthogonal projection, we develop a novel algorithm termed the sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding (SDSNT) algorithm. We further establish its global convergence under the restricted isometry property $δ_{3k}\leq \sqrt{3/20}$ of the measurement matrix. Numerical experiments on random sparse vector recovery and audio signal reconstruction reveal that SDSNT achieves comparable performance to several state-of-the-art algorithms. Notably, relative to most of them, it delivers superior recovery at high sparsity levels and improved efficiency at low sparsity levels.
A Model for Fast Mining Blockchains
Rhys Bowden; Cengiz Gazi; Jan de Gier; Peter Taylor

We study a Markovian model for a blockchain mining process. In the limit where there is an infinite number of miners, the model satisfies a functional law of large numbers due to Barbour and Luczac (2008), leading to an infinite set of coupled ODEs characterising the blockchain heights. We show that the sequence of solutions to this system converges uniformly, to a limiting profile in an appropriate comoving frame. Utilising asymptotic arguments inspired by Brunet and Derrida (1997), we derive an explicit expression for the position of the travelling front, which exhibits a leading order logarithmic Bramson correction in time. For a finite number of miners, we further derive a correction to the travelling speed which is logarithmic in the number of miners. Finally, by application of a computation due to Ablowitz and Zeppetella (1979), we identify that, for a specific choice of the travelling speed, the Painlevé integrable, travelling wave solution of the Fisher-KPP equation with drift accurately matches our limiting profile. Our results are supported by numerical simulations.
Product Pitt inequalities and signed Boas equivalences for general monotone functions

We prove product-weight Pitt inequalities for real or complex functions on $\mathbb R^d$ whose full mixed Vitali variation satisfies an exterior-tail general monotonicity condition. A two-parameter condition gives spatial weights with different powers near the coordinate hyperplanes and at infinity. For the classical parameters, a reverse estimate yields a Boas norm equivalence without sign, parity or separability assumptions. The equivalence holds for finite spatial norm and, for $L^1$ data, characterizes finiteness of either norm; the unrestricted nonintegrable converse remains open. We also prove an equivalence under primitive control, give explicit examples, and establish sharpness of the Fourier-side exponent range.
Pebbling Numbers and Generator Reinforcement of Cayley Graphs
Yuan Yang; Bocheng Li; Qingzhong Ji

We study inverse-closed generator additions of minimum size that make the optimal pebbling number of a finite Cayley graph at most three while preserving its specified regular action. A weighted vertex-cover formulation on inverse orbits yields an $O(|Γ|^2)$ algorithm for abelian groups in the explicit multiplication-table model. We derive formulas for central involutions and cubelike graphs, with an inverse-closure correction determined by square roots in the uncovered set. The exact thresholds are $2^{d-1}-d$ for hypercubes ($d\ge1$), and $3$ for standard Keller graphs when $d=2$ and $2^{d-1}$ when $d\ge3$. Every admissible augmentation of either family has ordinary pebbling number equal to its order.
Feature-preserving interface reconstruction using piecewise circles and cusps
Jerry Liu; Kenneth Weiss; Jin Yao

We present a geometric interface reconstruction method for Volume-of-Fluid (VOF) simulations that captures both curved interfaces and sharp features using only volume fraction data. We represent interfaces with linear facets, circular arcs, and corner facets formed by two lines or arcs joined within a single cell. We first propagate local orientation constraints through a graph and merge cells to resolve ambiguities, treating topological consistency as a first-class constraint. An optional conservative refinement improves $C^0$ continuity while preserving local volume constraints. Users can independently enable circular facets, corner facets, cell merging, and continuity refinement to balance accuracy and computational cost. In its simplest configuration, our method provides a fast local line-fitting scheme competitive with state-of-the-art PLIC methods. On standard static benchmarks, the full configuration reconstructs identifiable lines, circles, and sufficiently resolved corners to numerical precision on coarse, perturbed Cartesian meshes. On varying-curvature interfaces, it achieves third-order convergence in facet-gap error and approximately first-order convergence in curvature error. These results demonstrate global volume conservation and accurate reconstruction of curved and corner features.
Scaled-Gradient Hard Thresholding Algorithms for Sparse Signal Recovery

Thresholding methods provide a simple iterative framework for sparse signal recovery by combining a search direction with a thresholding operation. Gradient-based search directions are computationally efficient because they require only first-order information for the error metric. We incorporate componentwise gradient scaling into this framework by preserving large-magnitude components and attenuating the remaining components of the gradient of error metric. Combining this strategy with hard thresholding yields scaled-gradient hard thresholding (SGHT) and its pursuit variant SGHTP. Under suitable restricted isometry conditions, we establish recovery error bounds for both methods that account for measurement noise and deviations from exact sparsity. Numerical experiments indicate that SGHTP achieves recovery performance comparable to established pursuit methods on the tested ECG signals.
Stochastic dynamics generation of directed percolation using a two-channel convolutional neural network
Feng Gao; Jianmin Shen; Wei Li

Neural networks provide a promising approach to learning and generating the stochastic dynamics of nonequilibrium systems. In this study, we propose a stochastic dynamics generative method based on a two-channel convolutional neural network, using the (1+1)-dimensional directed bond percolation model to investigate its ability to learn local stochastic transition rules and reproduce stochastic dynamics across different system sizes. The proposed method takes the current particle configuration and the control parameter as inputs, learns the conditional activation probabilities at the next time step through local convolutions, and generates stochastic temporal evolution through iterative Bernoulli sampling. The results show that the network-generated dynamics agree well with Monte Carlo simulations across different control parameters. Furthermore, applying the trained network to a substantially larger system with $L=10000$ yields an estimated critical probability of $p_c=0.643$ and an effective density decay exponent of $δ\approx0.1592$, close to the established theoretical values. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method can reproduce the stochastic dynamics of directed percolation and capture its macroscopic dynamical and statistical properties across different spatial sizes.

We introduce a version of the Katok-Sarnak formula linking twisted traces of scalar valued Maass cusp forms for $Γ_0(N)$ with $N$ square-free to Fourier coefficients of vector valued Maass cusp forms for the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and the Weil representation associated to a lattice of signature $(2,1)$. We prove this by computing the Fourier coefficients of the vector valued Siegel and Millson theta lift of a scalar valued newform by two different methods and comparing the results.
Rigidity in sharp eigenvalue estimates for differential forms
Tsz-Kiu Aaron Chow; James Koh; Sen Yuk Wu

For $1\leq p\leq n/2$, we derive sharp eigenvalue estimates for the Hodge Laplacian on differential $p$-forms under the curvature condition introduced by Petersen and Wink, and study their equality cases. Equality recovers the stronger curvature operator lower bound and, in the closed case, leaves only round or Sasakian metrics on the universal cover. For manifolds with boundary, weak $p$-convexity of the boundary makes the unit hemisphere the only equality case for the absolute boundary problem.
Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials

We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(μ)$ associated to a partition $μ=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ \sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for signatures \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]
On the Turán number for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle and a tree
Ya-Hong Chen; Yong Lu; Quan Sun; Qi Wu; Long-Tu Yuan

Let $T$ be a fixed tree on at least two vertices. We determine the Turán number and all extremal graphs for the Cartesian product of an odd cycle $C_{2m+1}$ and $T$, for every fixed integer $m\ge1$ and all sufficiently large $n$, in terms of its decomposition family. Every extremal graph is the join of an independent set and an extremal graph for that family. The proof combines the Erdős--Sós theorem with weak stability and progressive induction.
Truthful and Admissible Principal--Agent Testing with Nuisance Parameters

Statistical contracts reward experimenters according to the evidence produced by a costly study, so the reward rule influences both who participates and what they report. Principal--agent testing theory explains how to prevent ineffective proposals from being profitable. We ask when such contracts can also elicit honest parameter reports if the decision concerns a mean effect but the variance or distributional shape is unknown. Under risk neutrality and a fixed participation cost, we construct menus of e-values --- nonnegative normalized rewards with expected value at most one under every null --- such that (i) agents who know they are null have no incentive to participate, (ii) every alternative type earns positive expected profit and is thus incentivized to participate, (iii) truthful reporting uniquely maximizes expected their reward, (iv) and each contract is admissible: its payouts cannot be pointwise improved while retaining null validity. For Gaussian observations, we treat separately agents who know both mean and variance and agents who know only their mean; in the latter case, truthfulness holds at every variance without requiring a nuisance prior. Multi-sample extensions preserve these incentives and can reward accumulating evidence. Beyond Gaussian models, we show that two independent nonnegative observations suffice to elicit any finite mean above a positive null threshold, without any further distributional knowledge, but one observation cannot combine strict mean elicitation with individual admissibility on this class. Finally, we distinguish the existence of useful tests from the identification needed for truthful contracts. Boundedness is not required, and finitely many null constraints do not by themselves guarantee admissible elicitation.
Beomjoon Kim; Donghwa Ji; Kabgyun Jeong

Quantifying correlations is important for understanding how quantum states and channels support information processing. Quantum umlaut information $U$ connects such correlations to reliability in hypothesis testing and certain communication settings, but its known formulas require classical descriptions of the underlying states. To estimate correlations without these descriptions, we introduce measured quantum umlaut information $U^M$ by replacing Umegaki relative entropy with measured relative entropy. Its variational formulation leads to a quantum generative adversarial framework for estimating $U^M$ from measurement statistics of unknown bipartite states and classical-quantum channels. This framework optimizes reference states and measurements without reconstructing the target states or channel outputs. For classical-quantum channels, it also optimizes the input probabilities. We further analyze the relation between $U^M$ and $U$, deriving a state-dependent gap bound and characterizing equality for full-rank bipartite states. Numerical simulations show trained estimates close on average to independently computed numerical references for $U^M$ across the tested states and channels. These estimates could help assess how well quantum memories preserve correlations and how noise or drift affects input-output dependence in quantum transmitters and state-preparation devices.
Coordination three heals, coordination four is hard: the antiferromagnetic Potts model with a costly third state
Jeehoon Choi; Suhwan Yoo; Chaeyeon Kim; Hee Young Kwon; Changyeon Won

We study the ground states of the antiferromagnetic three-state Potts model in which the third state carries a single-ion energy cost $D_3$, on arbitrary lattices, and show that the difficulty of the ground-state problem is controlled by the maximum coordination $Δ$ alone; on planar lattices with $Δ\le5$ it is classified completely. On lattices with coordination at most three the third state heals frustrated bonds one for one: every graph of maximum degree three other than $K_4$ has an independent set of sites that meets every odd cycle and whose size equals the number $\operatorname{fr}$ of frustrated bonds of the Ising ground state. This identity also follows from known results on the chromatic vertex stability of graphs; we give a constructive proof. Hence $E_0 (D_3)=\min(D_3,1) \operatorname{fr}$ for all $D_3$, computable in polynomial time on planar lattices. In graph-theoretic terms, independent odd cycle transversal is solvable in polynomial time on planar subcubic graphs. On planar lattices with maximum coordination four, in contrast, deciding the ground-state energy is NP-complete for every fixed $0\le D_3<2$ and polynomial for $D_3\ge2$. The boundary is set by a local principle: a site of coordination $d$ in the third state relieves at most $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$ frustrated bonds, so the third state is useless once $D_3\ge\lfloorΔ/2\rfloor$; this threshold is sharp for every $Δ\ge3$ and reproduces the triangular-lattice point $D_3^*=3$ of the equivalent spin-1 Blume--Capel antiferromagnet. From a single Ising ground state the proof builds an exact ground state in polynomial time, which for quasicrystalline, foam-like and defective lattices with thousands of sites takes seconds to minutes.
Dimension Changes the Scale-Signal Channel in Nearest-Neighbor Two-Sample Testing

Nearest-neighbor two-sample tests are often analyzed with dimension fixed. We study the power of the generalized edge-count test on a directed 1-nearest-neighbor graph. This statistic combines a weighted sum and a difference of the two within-sample edge counts. For balanced isotropic Gaussian samples with $d/\log N\toγ>0$, we derive the connection probabilities under local location and scale alternatives. Under location alternatives, the two counts have equal mean shifts, which cancel in their difference. Under scale alternatives, the two counts instead have mean shifts of opposite signs. We also derive the growth rate of the null expectation $\mathbb{E}_0C_3$, where $C_3$ counts pairs of directed edges sharing exactly one vertex. On an explicit range of $γ$, we establish local-power limits strictly above the test level for scale alternatives in the difference component at the scale $|\varepsilon_N|\asymp (\mathbb{E}_0C_3)^{1/2}/(Nd)$. Here $\mathbb{E}_0C_3$ gives the variance order of the difference count under these local alternatives. At this scale, the standardized drift of the weighted sum vanishes. When $d=1$, the weighted component instead detects local Gaussian scale alternatives while the difference component has no limiting drift. Thus dimension changes both the magnitude of a detectable scale difference and the component of the test that detects it.
A note on decompositions into 3-chromatic graphs
Bertille Granet; Daniel Horsley; Jeffrey N. Santrio

Delcourt and Postle recently introduced the `discharging in the dual' proof technique, leading to a breakthrough proof of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions. Independently, and almost simultaneously, the first and second authors built on the `condensation' method of Bryant, Dukes, Horsley, Maenhaut and Montgomery to determine the decomposition threshold of all odd cycles of length at least $73$. In this note, we explain how the `discharging in the dual' and `condensation' methods can be combined to determine the decomposition threshold of cycles of any odd length, as well as the approximate decomposition threshold of a range of other $3$-chromatic graphs.
Faster-than-power-law decay of order parameter correlations in the two-dimensional RP$^2$ model: a rigorous result by vibe-proving

We consider the RP$^2$ model on the two-dimensional square lattice with nearest-neighbor interactions. It is obtained by replacing the spin in the standard classical Heisenberg model with a director, which does not distinguish two opposite directions. Unlike the standard classical Heisenberg model or the O(3) nonlinear sigma model, the RP$^2$ (and its cousin RP$^3$) model allows point vortex defects classified by $π_1(RP^2)= Z_2$ in two dimensions. It is tempting to expect the $Z_2$ vortices to induce a phase transition analogous to the well-established Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in the O(2) model (XY model) in two dimensions. Indeed, the possibilities of a critical phase or a critical point with power-law correlations of the order parameter in the RP$^2$ and RP$^3$ models have been discussed in the literature. However, the challenging nature of the problem has prevented a definitive conclusion on the phase diagram so far. In this paper, we report a rigorous mathematical proof by Artificial Intelligence (ChatGPT 6 Astra) that the absolute value of the two-point correlation function of order parameters at distance $r$ in the RP$^2$ and RP$^3$ models on the two-dimensional square lattice is bounded above by $C_β\exp{(-c_β[\log(2+r)]^2)}$ for any finite inverse temperature $β\ge0$, with positive constants $C_β$ and $c_β$ depending only on $β$. Namely, the correlation function decays faster than any power of $r$. The proof is formalized and verified in Lean; the formalization is publicly available at doi:10.5281/zenodo.23548847 . A heuristic argument based on a one-parameter effective theory ansatz at large distances combined with the rigorous correlation bound suggests (but does not prove) that the $Z_2$ vortices are always unbound at any nonzero temperature.
Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 3: expectation under a general distribution

For multinomial counts $X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ on $n$ ordered bins and a reference law $\mathbf r$ we study the expectation of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf r}(X)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|(X_{j+1}-Nr_{j+1})-(X_j-Nr_j)|$, the natural extension of the comb-test statistic to a non-uniform null. For a non-uniform null the raw total variation of the counts carries a deterministic staircase of order $N$ that no centering of the statistic removes; the counts are therefore centered at the reference law, and under the null ($\mathbf p=\mathbf r$) the statistic is the matched $d_{\mathbf p}$. Exact finite-sample expectations are obtained by conditioning on the total mass in each adjacent pair, which reduces every edge to a translated binomial absolute-deviation problem. For fixed $n\ge3$ and a sampling law bounded away from the boundary of the simplex, the matched statistic admits a three-term asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/N$ whose coefficients are explicit continuous periodic functions of $N(p_{j+1}-p_j)$ (a generalized, non-Poincaré asymptotic expansion), obtained by a weighted local Edgeworth estimate and a corner Euler--Maclaurin summation; all half-integer orders vanish by parity. Each correction separates into a smooth Edgeworth part and an oscillatory lattice part, the latter an Edgeworth perturbation of one formal Euler--Maclaurin series of a Gaussian lattice sum. Under a sampling law $\mathbf p\neq\mathbf r$ the leading expectation is the folded-normal profile implied by the central limit theorem; under local alternatives we identify the $O(1)$ correction (a skewness term, plus a variance-gradient term for Pitman alternatives), and fixed alternatives give a law-of-large-numbers limit, the $\ell_1$ distance between the adjacent-gradient profiles of $\mathbf p$ and $\mathbf r$, on which threshold tests are consistent.
POST-MIMO: Partition-Oriented Semantic Transmission for MIMO Point Cloud Delivery
Hang Yue; Junlin Chang; Tianqing Zhao; Yulin Zhao; Rongke Liu

Point clouds have become a fundamental data format for emerging three dimensional (3D) applications, while their wireless delivery remains challenging due to the large data volume and irregular geometric structure. Existing semantic point cloud transmission methods are mainly developed for single-input single-output systems, making them difficult to apply directly to multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems. To address this issue, we propose a partition-oriented semantic transmission framework for MIMO (POST-MIMO) point cloud delivery. POST-MIMO partitions the input point cloud into spatially coherent blocks and aligns them with parallel MIMO streams. Based on this block-aligned representation, the transmitter employs a hierarchical encoder to capture both intra-block local geometry and inter-block global dependency, while the auxiliary side information is transmitted jointly to assist reconstruction. At the receiver, a progressive decoder reconstructs the block geometry in a progressive manner and restores the final point cloud with block-aware adjustment. Experiments demonstrate improved reconstruction quality and lower computational resource consumption than representative reference schemes under the considered MIMO setting.
Stochastic Mirror Descent under Dependent Observations
Gersende Fort; Anatoli Juditsky; Jiaming Liang

We study the non-asymptotic convergence of Stochastic Mirror Descent (SMD) algorithm when the noisy first-order oracle is driven by dependent observations. Departing from the classical i.i.d. assumption underlying most existing guarantees, we introduce a flexible ``forgetting" condition that accommodates geometrically or polynomially dependent sequences. Under this condition we derive explicit finite-sample accuracy bounds for the averaged SMD iterates, recovering the classical $O(1/T)$ and $O(1/\sqrt{T})$ rates in the large- and small-initial-error regimes. We instantiate the general framework on two applications: high-dimensional linear regression with dependent regressors and nonparametric estimation of the drift function of a functional autoregressive model.
A Good-Vorticity Low-Regularity Integrator for the Inviscid Oldroyd--B System with Stress Diffusion
Xinyu Cheng; Zhaonan Luo; Zhaojie Yang; Cheng Yuan

We establish sharp convergence results for a sequential semi-implicit good-vorticity integrator for the two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd--B system with stress diffusion on the torus. For exact solutions satisfying $u\in C_tB^{1+α}_{\infty,1}$ and $τ\in C_tB^α_{\infty,1}\cap L^1_tB^{2+α}_{\infty,1}$, $0\leα\le2$, we prove convergence in the critical norms $B^1_{\infty,1}\times B^0_{\infty,1}$, uniformly over the time nodes on every finite interval where these regularity assumptions hold, including the critical endpoint $α=0$. For $0<α\le2$, we obtain the rate $O(h^{α/2})$ without any additional time Hölder assumption, reaching first order at $α=2$. These algebraic exponents are optimal for this Eulerian scheme over the stated solution classes, as shown by fixed-data lower bounds in the case $a=b=0$ with nonzero velocity mean. For a fixed shear solution at critical regularity, we establish matching logarithmic upper and lower bounds on the numerical error, ruling out every positive algebraic convergence rate. We also prove that the gain of one stress derivative at the time nodes is optimal when the velocity is controlled in $B^1_{\infty,1}$, even for smooth initial stress.
Generative SDEs with Trainable Diffusion and Density-Based Losses

We develop a divergence-kernel method for jointly optimizing neural SDE drift and diffusion fields and the initial Gaussian distribution, using losses that depend directly on the terminal density. In two- and eight-dimensional Gaussian-mixture experiments, we learn time-independent fields and obtain far fewer off-mode samples than score-based generators with similar parameter counts. The drift attracts samples toward the modes, while the diffusion helps disperse excess probability between them.
Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum quantum gauge theory with matter
Goncalo Araujo-Regado; Philipp A. Hoehn; Alok Laddha; Bilyana Tomova

Subregions in gauge theories give rise to edge modes and corner charges supported on their boundaries. While this is well-established classically and in quantum lattice gauge theories, the fate of corner modes remains poorly understood in continuum quantum field theories owing to their distributional nature. In this paper, we revisit this challenge and propose a new corner operator for a regional Cauchy slice algebra generated by local gauge-invariant observables of scalar QED in Minkowski spacetime. The corner mode is given by the longitudinal electric field sourced by the matter outside the subregion and thus constitutes a centre for the regional algebra. Our main goal is to show that there exists a perturbative GNS state on this algebra that quantises this mode. Pulling back the Fock vacuum to the slice, we construct this state by renormalising the divergences arising from the lack of temporal smearing. We clarify that the inclusion of the new centre mode necessitates a further renormalisation on the corner of the region, thereby physically distinguishing it and breaking the translation invariance of the state. Our work shows how the requirements of locality, renormalisability, and positivity together put strong constraints on the existence of a continuum quantum field theory which supports corner modes as genuine quantum operators. We finish with comments about the von Neumann completion of the regional algebra, as well as possible physical interpretations of the renormalised vacuum state.
Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties

Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$. The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $ι_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincaré duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.
Efficient Importance Sampling of Brownian Motion Avoiding Poissonian Obstacles for Long Time
Jose Blanchet; Paul Dupuis; Hao Liu

We design and analyze an efficient importance sampling estimator of the probability that, over a long time horizon, a Brownian particle avoids obstacles of a fixed radius placed according to an independent Poisson random field. Donsker and Varadhan identify the exponential decay rate of this probability as the optimal balance between the volume cleared of obstacles and the spectral cost of confinement, and the confinement results of Sznitman and Povel show that the particle survives by localizing its path in a ball of (roughly) deterministic radius but with a random center. This strategy makes direct Monte Carlo exponentially ineffective over long horizons, and makes a practical yet asymptotically optimal sampler non-trivial to design, since the sampler must track the random region swept out by the path. For every fixed dimension \(d\ge2\) and every fixed obstacle radius, we construct a sequential importance sampler that is unbiased and asymptotically optimal. The full algorithm has finite expected total work at every fixed horizon, and both its expected work and the coefficient of variation grow at most subexponentially with the time horizon. The method avoids repeatedly solving eigenvalue problems on the evolving explored regions and suits parallel implementation. Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency of the method.

Ekholm and Shende's skeins-on-branes formalism provides invariant counts of holomorphic curves with boundary on a Maslov zero Lagrangian within a Calabi-Yau 3-fold. This paper proves the orientation relations required for worldsheet skein relations to cancel codimension-one boundary strata. However, standard Cauchy-Riemann Fredholm orientations reveal an unexpected sign puzzle: the orientation relation at a curve with a hyperbolic boundary crossing depends on whether the crossing lies on distinct boundary components or the same component. This domain-dependent sign contradicts the uniform crossing relations of the HOMFLYPT skein algebra. We show that this discrepancy is resolved by passing to an anti-holomorphic orientation convention. We establish all required orientation comparisons in the general setting of an oriented Lagrangian submanifold of a 6-dimensional symplectic manifold.
Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant Γ_{1,4} = 8

Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants Γ_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.
DistFlow and Its Conic Relaxation: Regularity, Monotonicity, and Hybrid Exactness via Graph Decomposition

Classical exactness conditions for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model rely, among other assumptions, either on all nodal injections being adjustable or on a network-wide path condition. In practice, these conditions may not hold uniformly across a feeder: controllable distributed energy resources (DERs) sit at some buses and fixed loads at others, while reverse flows from DER-rich regions can violate the path condition. This paper certifies exactness region by region and composes the regional certificates, accounting for perturbations that propagate downstream through voltages. We first introduce a subtree voltage stability region, in which the network and all compatible subtrees remain regular. Within it, two endpoint sign conditions, one relaxing the nonnegative-flow assumption and one implied by the classical path condition, yield monotone responses of voltages, currents, and losses to root voltages. Using duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices, we recast both classical arguments as individual sign certificates on branch multipliers. This turns exactness into a branchwise property that can be certified region by region. A partition rule then splits the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees, and a hybrid certificate combines their local conditions into exactness of the full-network relaxation, under additional operating-limit and objective conditions. In particular, placing controllable DERs at both ends of a branch with large reverse flow exempts that branch from the passive sign conditions.
Local Smoothing Estimates of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling

We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schrödinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.
On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
Jiaxin He; Qinfeng Li; Shangfeng Wu; Shuangquan Xie

We compare the maximum points \(P_Ω\) and \(Q_Ω\) of the torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness, strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity \[ \sup_Ω \frac{|P_Ω-Q_Ω|}{\operatorname{diam}(Ω)}=\frac12. \] Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.
Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions

Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $ϕ\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{ϕ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$. This corrects Theorem 6 in [Graphs Combin., \textbf{41}(6)(2025), 119] and relaxes its hypothesis from requiring all $G_i$ to be connected to only requiring that at least one $G_i$ is connected, where $i\in[n-1]$. Moreover, we show that if $n\ge2$ and $e(G_i)\ge \binom{n-1}{2}$ for each $i\in[n-1]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian path unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{n-1}\cong K_{n-1}\cup K_1$, or $n=4$ with $G_1=G_2=G_3\cong K_{1,3}$. As a consequence, Theorem 2 of [Discrete Math., \textbf{347}(2024), 114128] follows immediately.
Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated

We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.
Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness

Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

We also show that the Hopf-cylinder alternative in a theorem of Dorfmeister, Inoguchi and Kobayashi contains no non-CMC surface.
Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
Jae-Hyun Baek; Byung-Sun Won; Jon-Lark Kim

LLM-guided program evolution can produce mathematical constructions, but validity, generality, and reproducibility require distinct evidence.
