Lastly, we characterize complete integral closure for positive rational generators.
Stability and bifurcations of the synchronized layered steady states in membrane-coupled delayed RD systems: The SLEP approach

Inter-layer exchange in biological and chemical systems may involve transport delays and memory effects. In this paper, we mainly study the stability and bifurcations of the synchronized layered steady states in singularly perturbed membrane-coupled reaction-diffusion (RD) systems, where discrete or exponentially distributed delays are introduced into the activator coupling, while the inhibitor coupling remains instantaneous, leading to six representative configurations. By extending the singular limit eigenvalue problem (SLEP) method originally developed by [Nishiura and Fujii, SIMA, 18(6), 1987; Nishiura and Mimura, SIAP, 49(2), 1989] for the non-delayed case, we develop a unified spectral framework that incorporates the symmetric and asymmetric sub-eigenvalue problems arising from all six delayed configurations, demonstrating how the SLEP approach can be adapted to capture the limiting behavior of critical eigenvalues when time delays are present. We then establish sufficient conditions to determine the delay-independent stability, the persistence of Turing instability, as well as delay-induced Hopf bifurcations of the synchronized layered steady states. In particular, we focus on analyzing how time delays could induce in-phase and anti-phase breathers via Hopf bifurcations, leading to spatiotemporal oscillatory instabilities that were absent in the delay-free setting. As an application, we also supply a two-layer membrane-coupled delayed FitzHugh-Nagumo system to illustrate how our results can be applied.
A Parallel Algebraic Multigrid Preconditioned Iterative Method Based on an MPI Process Grouping Strategy for Asynchronous Concurrent Execution of the Setup and Solve Phases
Chunsheng Feng; Shuai Liu; Linjie Zhang; Zirui Zhu

Algebraic multigrid (AMG) is one of the most effective algorithms for solving large sparse linear systems and consists of a setup phase followed by a solve phase. As supercomputer performance improves and the number of MPI processes increases, AMG faces serious challenges in algorithmic scalability and parallel scalability. To address these issues, we propose an asynchronous concurrent algebraic multigrid (ACAMG) model based on an MPI process grouping strategy for setup and solve. The setup and solve phases execute asynchronously and concurrently on separate MPI process groups. This organization can both preserve AMG hierarchy quality through an appropriate choice of the setup-group size and achieve time overlap between the two phases through asynchronous concurrent execution. Based on this model, we design and implement the MPI ACAMG algorithm. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments show that the algorithm exhibits better algorithmic and parallel scalability. For example, for a three-dimensional diffusion problem with spatially localized anisotropy, ACAMG not only reduces the solve-phase iteration count compared with the conventional method, but also achieves speedups of 4.74 and 19.36 at 64 and 128 processes, respectively.
Energy Stability and Error Estimates for a Globally Divergence-Free DG Method of Arbitrary Order
Yuchang Liu; Yan Jiang; Mengping Zhang

We propose and analyze an arbitrary-order globally divergence-free (GDF) discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method for the two-dimensional linear magnetic induction equation on unstructured triangular meshes. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to provide a rigorous energy-based analysis of high-order GDF-DG methods. First, we incorporate the edge normal-trace evolution into a closed, strictly local semidiscrete operator acting on the elementwise magnetic field alone. Then, we introduce two local modifications to the continuous electric field: a weighted patch moment correction that enforces local polynomial orthogonality and a vertex-patch stabilization that damps the remaining high-order modes. On shape-regular, quasi-uniform periodic triangulations, we prove semidiscrete energy stability with a sufficiently large mesh-independent penalty and establish a priori error estimates for smooth solutions. Numerical experiments support the analysis.
On two problems concerning the geodesic transversal number of graphs
Shi Chen; Xuanlong Ma; Tingzeng Wu

We establish sharp upper and lower bounds on the geodesic transversal number of hypercubes. We also obtain a lower bound on the geodesic transversal number of Hamming graphs. As applications, we provide negative answers to two open problems concerning the geodesic transversal number.
There Is No Free Lunch in RLVR: Every pass@1 Gain Has a pass@k Price

Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) makes a language model solve more problems on the first try and fewer when given many tries: it raises pass@1 while the base model overtakes it at large sampling budget k. Is this a failure of RL to add reasoning, or a transient that more training removes? We settle the question with a theorem. The reversal is a price, and we compute its exact rate. Modeling RLVR as an exponential tilt of a base policy over strategies shared across prompts, we prove that under exclusive specialization every update that raises pass@1 strictly lowers the success of some prompt; a strictly positive price on prompts (Stiemke duality) is the exact condition, and being merely the best strategy on a prompt is provably not enough. When the loss reaches the hardest prompts, it forces a pass@k crossover, and the number of crossings is at most the sign variation of the shift in per-prompt success, a totally positive bound that is tight and that recovers the known single-crossover result as its order-preserving case. The crossover is not a bug to patch: a constrained update traces the exact pass@1 versus pass@k frontier, and removing the crossover entirely costs the entire pass@1 gain. The same tilt identity yields entropy collapse and the entropy-performance law with an identifiable exponent, unifying two literatures under one mechanism. Reinforcement cannot widen the reasoning frontier; it can only move along it, at a price we make measurable by a diagnostic that reads the bound, the order-preserving test, and the price from any evaluation log. There is no free lunch, only a price.
Secure Wireless Communications with Flexible Reflectors: Joint Position and Rotation Optimization for Physical Layer Security
Miao Jiang; Xike Wang; Yiqing Li; Guangchi Zhang

By exploiting the spatial selectivity of wireless channels, physical layer security (PLS) protects confidential wireless transmissions. Flexible reflectors (FRs), which are passive metallic plates mounted on movable platforms, offer a low-cost and low-complexity solution for reshaping the propagation environment. However, their potential for secrecy-oriented signal propagation shaping has not been explored. In this paper, we study an FR-aided secure communication over non-line-of-sight links and jointly optimize the positions and rotations of FRs to maximize the secrecy rate under geometric reflection and mutual-blocking constraints. For the single-FR case, we propose a Fibonacci segmentation search (FSS) method, which partitions the feasible region into multiple unimodal intervals and obtains the optimal solution with Fibonacci search over the unimodal intervals. To reduce the computational overhead, we also propose a low-complexity cross-entropy search (CES) method, which employs Gaussian mixture model-based adaptive importance sampling to localize promising search intervals before deterministic refinement. After deriving the blocked placement interval induced by the deployed FRs and integrating it into a sequential deployment scheme, we extend the FSS and CES methods to the multi-FR case. Simulation results show that our proposed FSS method achieves significant secrecy rate performance gains over various benchmark schemes, and our proposed CES method achieves a favorable runtime-performance tradeoff. These results indicate that FRs provide a low-cost and reconfigurable mechanism for PLS.
Generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and unirationality of del Pezzo surfaces of degree $2$

We introduce generalized Iskovskikh surfaces and study their relation to quasi-étale double covers. As an application, we prove that a del Pezzo surface of degree $2$ over an infinite field of characteristic different from $2$ is unirational if it has a rational generalized Eckardt point. This resolves a previously open case not covered by Manin's construction.
Dynamic invisibility of implicit and nested state-dependent delays in a class of externally forced delay equations
Samuel Bolduc-St-Aubin; Priya Subramanian; Bernd Krauskopf

Delayed feedback is a fundamental mechanism in many systems and is often modeled by delay differential equations (DDEs). While delays are frequently assumed to be constant, in realistic feedback processes they may depend on the state and even be defined implicitly or in a nested fashion by the feedback relation itself. In this work, we address the question of how such implicit and nested state-dependent delays affect the observed behavior of a class of externally forced systems with negative switched feedback. Our motivating example and principal case study is the piecewise-smooth limiting form of a conceptual DDE model for the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) with a negative feedback term subject to implicit state-dependent delay. We prove, for a wider prototypical class of DDEs with switched negative feedback and more general forcing, that (subject to an explicit condition on the parameters) any finite level of nested state-dependent delay and the limiting implicit delay are dynamically invisible: they all generate exactly the same trajectory, namely, that of the corresponding constant-delay DDE. We also discuss how the delayed argument functions organize the temporal order of reactions (TOR) in this regime, and show that a more stringent condition is required to ensure TOR for nested state-dependent delays.
Chan-Eui Song; Jeremy J. Michalek; Christopher McComb

Engineering design frequently involves redesigning a prior solution to adapt to changes in context, such as material prices or system requirements. Redesign often leverages simulators too complex and/or computationally intensive for traditional numerical solvers, which lack engineering knowledge and context, to ensure global solution quality. Large language models (LLMs) can interpret semantic information, including engineering knowledge about the system and changes in context, to help guide search, and recent studies have shown that incorporating this knowledge into optimization can improve search performance. However, how best to combine LLMs with numerical solvers in redesign remains unclear. We develop and test an integrated LLM-optimization approach for redesign and compare three methods for leveraging LLMs (warm start, variable fixing and ReAct) and four black-box solvers (Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithms, mesh adaptive direct search and random search) on an electric vehicle battery pack cost minimization case study across four types of redesign scenarios. We find that the integrated approach can match feasible design discovery of the numerical-solver baselines with 80% fewer simulator evaluations while tripling the fraction of runs that find near-optimal solutions. We find that the best LLM-solver integration approach and the way the prior solution is leveraged depend on the structure of the design requirement change, and that the benefit of increasing LLM model size grows with the extent to which the LLM controls the search. These results show clear potential for LLMs in redesign tasks for guiding or replacing numerical solvers.
Sharp potential and Brenier map $W_2$-stability for log-concave sources

We study stability of Brenier potentials and maps under changes of the target measure. Let $κ>0$, for a full support $κ$-strongly log-concave source $ρ$, possibly with a non-smooth potential, the normalized transport potentials satisfy \[ \|u_μ-u_ν\|_{L^2(ρ)}\leqslant\sqrt{2/κ}\,W_2(μ,ν) \] for arbitrary targets with finite second moments. The proof controls normalized Laguerre cell barycentres by their mass derivatives and centers the potential velocity to remove unbounded source cell locations. Bounded variation interpolation then yields the sharp map exponent $1/3$ for targets in a common compact set, \[ \left\Vert T_μ-T_ν\right\Vert _{L^{2}(ρ)}\leqslant \operatorname{Const} \cdot W_{2}\left( μ,ν\right) ^{1/3}. \] Sharpness of the exponents for both the potential and Brenier map stability are established.
Free modules of vector-valued modular forms and applications to Jacobi forms
Jialin Li; Haowu Wang; Bohan Zhang

The space $M(ρ;\mathcal{E})$ of weakly holomorphic modular forms for a dimension-$r$ complex representation $ρ$ of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with growth prescribed by $\mathcal{E}$ at the cusp is a free module over $\mathbb{C}[E_4,E_6]$. We first prove that a $\mathbb{C}[E_4,E_6]$-linearly independent homogeneous family $F_1,\ldots,F_r$ in this module gives a basis if and only if $\sum_{i=1}^r \operatorname{wt}(F_i)=12\operatorname{tr}\mathcal{E}$. We then extend this criterion to Jacobi forms. As applications, we determine the generator weights of free modules of $\mathrm{O}(D_{8d}^+)$-invariant Jacobi forms of index $D_{8d}^{+}(p)$, where $D_{8d}^{+}$ is an even unimodular lattice extending $D_{8d}$, $d\ge2$, and $p=2,3,5$.
Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation

We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders give the same total error, but they divide it differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, with a power series that converges for all time in exponentially weighted trajectory norms. The linearized semigroup has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, exponential stability, Kato smoothing, Crandall-Pazy regularity and analyticity of the solution maps hold uniformly in the mesh size. These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. In exponentially weighted time-integrated norms the semidiscrete solutions converge uniformly on balls, at the rate $h^{1/6}$ in $L^4(0,\infty;L^2)$ for data in $L^2$ and at the rate $h^{2/3}$ in $L^2(0,\infty;H^1)$ for data in $H_0^1$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$. For the unweighted scheme, a grid wave packet of zero group velocity destroys mesh-uniform Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity.
The seeds and silhouettes of optimal gravitational shielding
Bruno Le Floch; Philippe G. LeFloch

We construct complete vacuum initial data sets with prescribed asymptotically flat exterior geometry, including the gluing of two Schwarzschild exterior regions with small masses (which need not be positive). The construction allows for arbitrarily slow leading decay and nonzero second fundamental form. For leading terms with a fixed radial power, we first construct localized seed data sets whose constraint errors decay to any prescribed finite order, then apply the projection and stability theorems of our companion papers. The resulting vacuum data sets differ from seeds by harmonic terms controlled by Hamiltonian and momentum silhouettes, and by super-harmonic corrections. This difference of harmonic terms is measured by a relative notion of ADM energy-momentum, which is defined even for slowly-decaying data sets that do not admit an ADM energy-momentum. Upon adjusting seed data sets by either harmonic-decaying terms or compact transverse-traceless terms, we freely control this relative ADM charge and, when it exists, the total ADM charge. In particular, when gluing Schwarzschild metrics the total ADM mass can be specified independently of the Schwarzschild mass parameters. Together with our companion papers, these results establish a constructive theory of optimal localization beyond harmonic decay.
Network flow-based cuts for binary bilevel programs
Sebastian Vasquez; Leonardo Lozano; Willem-Jan van Hoeve

Binary bilevel programs are challenging to solve due to the lack of compact single-level reformulations. Recent extended network flow-based reformulations have emerged as a promising approach, providing strong dual bounds. However, their increasing size can make them computationally prohibitive. We develop a cutting-plane framework that exploits these networks without requiring an extended-space formulation. We introduce two exact network flow-based reformulations and provide an efficient separation procedure for inequalities that certify the follower's optimality. We further strengthen these inequalities through a tilting procedure that leverages the combinatorial structure of the networks. Computational experiments show that the proposed approach becomes increasingly advantageous as networks grow larger or more numerous. Moreover, incorporating the cuts into state-of-the-art bilevel solvers improves solution times and optimality gaps on BOBILib instances, closing eight more open instances than the baseline solvers. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of using network representations as separation oracles for binary bilevel optimization.
On an affirmative solution to Michael's problem, with applications to automatic continuity theory

In 1952, Michael posed a question about functional continuity of commutative Fréchet algebras in his memoir, known as Michael's problem in the literature. We settle this in the affirmative along with its equivalent forms. Indeed, we continue our previous works to directly attack these problems. We show that the test case for this problem -- the Fréchet algebra $\cal U$ of all entire functions on $\ell^\infty$ -- is, in fact, a Fréchet algebra $\cc[[X]]$, if there exists a discontinuous character on $\cal U$. An important tool is a topological version of the tensor (symmetric) algebra over a Banach space. The elementary, but crucial, idea is to express the test algebra $\cal U$ as a {\it weighted Fréchet symmetric algebra} over the Banach space $\ell^1$. We summarize the effects of our affirmative solution in terms of important applications in automatic continuity theory, including affirmative answers to two significant, long-standing problems from 1966 and 1978.
Uniform estimates for complex Monge-Ampère equations II: Hermitian manifolds
Quang-Tuan Dang; Lei Zhang; Bin Zhou

We establish uniform estimates for degenerate complex Monge--Ampère equations on compact Hermitian manifolds under weak Orlicz integrability assumptions on the densities. Our estimates apply uniformly to Hermitian metrics and to semipositive uniformly non-collapsing reference forms. For arbitrary big reference forms, we obtain uniform relative $L^\infty$-estimates with respect to the extremal function with minimal singularities, and establish continuity of the resulting solutions on the regular locus. As an application, we prove the existence of solutions with minimal singularities to degenerate complex Monge--Ampère equations associated with big forms. The proofs combine local Orlicz estimates with pluripotential-theoretic envelope techniques and uniform control of the Monge--Ampère masses, overcoming the lack of invariance of the total Monge--Ampère mass in the Hermitian setting.
Herman Chau; Spencer Daugherty; Sean Grate; Mark D. Haiman; Juan Carlos Martínez Mori; Anna Pun

We introduce the stable Tamari lattice $\mathcal{ST}_n$, an infinite lattice on $\mathbb{N}^n$. The $r$-Tamari lattices on $r$-Dyck paths of height $n+1$ occur as a nested family of principal lower order ideals whose union is $\mathcal{ST}_n$. Partition-indexed principal lower order ideals recover the $ν$-Tamari lattices associated with partition boundaries. We give an explicit coordinate description of the stable Tamari order in terms of interval vectors determined by the lower endpoint. These coordinates characterize comparability and covering relations, and their sum gives the maximum length of a chain between two comparable elements. Analogous coordinates determined by the upper endpoint give an explicit formula for the Möbius function. We also construct an EL-labeling of every interval and show that every interval in $\mathcal{ST}_n$ is isomorphic to an interval in a classical Tamari lattice. We classify the possible $h$-vectors by Dyck paths and show that each $h$-vector fiber is parametrized by a unimodular basis of interval vectors. Combining this parametrization with the lower-endpoint coordinates, we obtain a finite rational formula for the multivariate generating function of the height generating functions of all principal lower order ideals. Under the $r$-Tamari realization, these height generating functions recover the interval generating functions of Bergeron and Préville-Ratelle.
On Proximity Gaps for One-Point Algebraic Geometric Codes
Songsong Li; Chaoping Xing; Chen Yuan; Ruiqi Zhu

Proximity gaps and correlated agreement underpin the soundness of interactive oracle proofs. We establish these properties for general one-point algebraic geometry (AG) codes, extending corresponding results for Reed-Solomon codes. For codes of length $n$ over $\mathbb F_q$ with designed distance $n-m$, write $ρ=m/n$ and fix $ρ\in(0,1)$. For polynomial curves of degree at most $\ell$ and any $0<\varepsilon<1$, we prove correlated agreement with multiplicative slack $\varepsilon$ and soundness $O(\ell(\ell+1)/(\varepsilon q))$ whenever $e\le(1-\varepsilon)(n-m)/2$, with no additional genus penalty. This gives asymptotically good AG code families from Garcia--Stichtenoth tower of unbounded length over a fixed field with soundness bounds independent of $n$, beyond the RS restriction $n\le q$. We also establish mutual correlated agreement up to radius $(1-\sqrtρ-η)n$, with soundness $O(\ell n/(η^3q))$ for $0<η<1-\sqrtρ$. Our half designed distance proof combines auxiliary divisors, simultaneous Berlekamp-Welch interpolation, and error-incidence counting to obtain a common polynomial representation without a Polishchuk-Spielman divisibility lemma. Finally, two counterexamples on the Garcia-Stichtenoth tower show limitations beyond half the minimum distance, at radii below the Johnson bound and with positive slack. The first requires a positive constant soundness lower bound independent of $q$ and $n$, precluding a uniform $O(1/q)$ guarantee throughout the Johnson regime. The second fixes the field and lets the relative gap above half distance tend to zero while ruling out correlated agreement for every soundness parameter $σ<1$, with positive limiting rate and relative error radius.
Dually flat structure of von Mises-Fisher distributions
Behzad Najafi; Morteza Sharifi-Najjar; Ryu Ueno

The von Mises--Fisher (vMF) distribution is the natural exponential family analogue of the normal distribution on the unit hypersphere. We bring together previous results of its dually flat structure and establish new results on the information geometry of the family of vMF distributions. In particular, we characterize the exponential and mixture autoparallel submanifolds, and give the classification of doubly autoparallel submanifolds. Furthermore, we derive explicit formulas for the unique minimizers of the Kullback-Leibler divergence on these submanifolds and establish the corresponding projection theorems.
The Liouville property for geometric graphs in the plane
Kuijun Liu; Feng Luo; Yanwen Luo; Zhenghao Rao

We show that every bounded discrete harmonic function with respect to the cotangent Laplacian on a Delaunay triangulation of the Euclidean plane is constant; equivalently, the cotangent-weighted triangulation has the Liouville property. Our main theorem establishes this property for a more general class of connected weighted geometric graphs in the plane. Furthermore, we show that a planar Delaunay triangulation with cotangent weights could be transient but is recurrent if edge lengths are uniformly bounded.
Bregman projections and partition design for accelerating finite Markov chains
Michael C. H. Choi; Youjia Wang

We study Gibbs averaging of finite Markov chains with a prescribed stationary distribution $π$. Given a transition matrix $P$ and the Gibbs kernel $G$ induced by a state-space partition, we prove that $GPG$ is an information projection for every admissible Bregman generator $ϕ$, with divergences defined using transition probabilities relative to $π$. A Pythagorean identity characterizes this projection and recovers the relative entropy and weighted Frobenius cases. A dual characterization identifies $GPG$ as a kernel closest to stationarity among those with the same projection chain as $P$; for relative entropy, it maximizes the entropy rate. The identities also give monotonicity under partition coarsening. For every reversible ergodic baseline $P$, Gibbs averaging cannot increase the squared weighted Frobenius distance to stationarity at any positive integer time, and the inequality is strict unless $P=GPG$. The corresponding mixing time therefore cannot increase. To choose the partition, we identify the divergence of $G$ from stationarity as the exact worst-case divergence of $GPG$ over all $π$-stationary baselines $P$. This objective depends only on the block masses. We give an exact algorithm for concave block costs, including those arising from relative entropy and power generators $ϕ(u)=u^p$ with $1<p<2$, and a greedy approximation algorithm with a provable guarantee for $p>2$. For power generators $ϕ(u)=u^p$ with $p>1$, the objective is proportional to Tsallis entropy of order $2-p$: its minimization favors imbalanced block masses when $1<p<2$ and balanced block masses when $p>2$, while all $k$-block partitions have the same objective value when $p=2$. A numerical experiment compares the resulting projected chains with a local Metropolis sampler on a multi-modal $π$.
Higher order Teodorescu transform in the theory of generalized partial-slice monogenic functions

This paper investigates the higher order Teodorescu transform in the context of generalized partial-slice monogenic functions. By introducing the generalized poly-partial-slice Cauchy kernel, we derive some integral formulas including higher order Borel-Pompeiu formula and Cauchy integral formula for generalized poly-partial-slice monogenic functions. Furthermore, we define the higher order Teodorescu transform in this context and establish its existence, continuity, and some mapping properties. These results extend classical integral methods in Clifford analysis to the generalized poly-partial-slice setting.
Error terms for sums of two linear transformations

Let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $\mathcal L_1,\mathcal L_2$ be irreducible and coprime linear transformations from $\mathbb{Z}^d$ to $\mathbb{Z}^d$. In this paper, we prove that, for every finite nonempty set $A\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^d$, \[ |\mathcal L_1A+\mathcal L_2A| \ge \left(|\det\mathcal L_1|^{1/d}+|\det\mathcal L_2|^{1/d}\right)^d|A|-O\left(|A|^{1-1/d}\right). \] This confirms the conjecture of Conlon and Lim on the error term for two linear transformations.
Every group is the automorphism group of a set-theoretic solution of the Yang--Baxter equation

We give an affirmative answer to the \emph{abstract group problem} for the category $\YB$ of all set-theoretic solutions of the Yang--Baxter (YB) equation: every group is isomorphic to the automorphism group of a YB-solution, which can be chosen on a finite set if the group is finite. In the terminology of László Babai, this means that the category $\YB$ is \emph{universal} and \emph{finitely universal}, which is an analogue of Frucht's classical theorem for graphs. Furthermore, the YB-solutions can be chosen within three very small classes: the solutions of the Frobenius-Separability equation, the solutions of the Baaj--Long--Skandalis equation and the recently introduced bipartite solutions. The proof is based on new constructions which associate to any graph a YB-solution in each of these classes, with the same automorphism group as the graph. Explicit YB-solutions with automorphism groups $C_n$, $S_n$, $D_n$ and $Q_8$ are given, as well as a unitary YB-solution, constructed directly from a field $K$, whose automorphism group is ${\rm Aut} (K)$.

In this paper, we introduce and study averaging Zinbiel bialgebras. We first define representations of averaging Zinbiel algebras and prove a semi-direct product characterization. We then introduce matched pairs and Manin triples of averaging Zinbiel algebras, and characterize averaging Zinbiel bialgebras by these two structures. We show that every averaging Zinbiel algebra induces a pre-Lie algebra, and that every averaging Zinbiel bialgebra induces a pre-Lie bialgebra. We also study coboundary averaging Zinbiel bialgebras and introduce the \(S\) admissible Zinbiel Yang-Baxter equation. Its symmetric solutions give rise to averaging Zinbiel bialgebras. Finally, we investigate averaging operators on quadratic Rota-Baxter Zinbiel algebras and relative Rota-Baxter operators on averaging Zinbiel algebras.
Fast rigid rotational alignment of voxelized 3-D density maps in sliced Wasserstein distance
Oscar Mickelin; Yunpeng Shi; Amit Singer; Eric J. Verbeke

We develop a fast method for the rigid alignment of voxelized three-dimensional density functions over $\mathsf{SO}(3)$ using sliced optimal transport. Our approach efficiently transforms each density map into a tensor of one-dimensional quantile functions, taken from central slices over the unit sphere, such that the Euclidean distance of the transformed volumes approximates the sliced 2-Wasserstein distance. Our formulation is therefore compatible with existing, fast, voxel-based Euclidean alignment algorithms. We provide theoretical analysis and numerical experiments demonstrating that the sliced 2-Wasserstein distance is a robust metric for comparing three-dimensional shapes and for computing their rigid alignment.

We develop a framework for equilibrated residual a posteriori error analysis of finite element methods, based on decomposing vector- and tensor-valued Sobolev spaces into $H^2$ and $H^1$ spaces. To estimate the residual functional acting on $H^2$ component, the method reconstructs symmetric and piecewise polynomial tensors on vertex patches in broken $H(\operatorname{div}\operatorname{div})$ spaces. We apply the proposed framework to conforming finite element discretizations of biharmonic equation, Poisson's equation, and linear elasticity in mixed form. As a result, we obtain several novel equilibrated residual a posteriori error estimates, providing guaranteed error control for energy error of biharmonic equation, $L^2$ norm error of Poisson's equation, and stress error of mixed linear elasticity. They also serve as the first polynomial-degree-robust a posteriori lower bounds of discretization errors. Numerical experiments illustrate the effectiveness of the $H^2$-based error estimators.
Unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the Jäger--Luckhaus model on the unit disk

We identify unstable radial equilibria as sharp concentration thresholds for the Jäger--Luckhaus chemotaxis system on the unit disk with no-flux boundary conditions. Concentration is compared through cumulative mass. At fixed total mass, every radial initial profile more concentrated than an unstable equilibrium produces finite-time blow-up, whereas every nonstationary profile less concentrated than that equilibrium generates a global, uniformly bounded solution converging to the least concentrated radial equilibrium. We also classify the radial equilibria and determine their nonlinear stability. Let $Λ= j_{1,1}^{2}$, where $j_{1,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_1$. For $M\ne Λπ$, the least concentrated equilibrium is the unique locally asymptotically stable equilibrium under mass-preserving radial perturbations. It is spatially homogeneous for $M<Λπ$ and strictly increasing for $M>Λπ$. Every other radial equilibrium, including the homogeneous state at $M=Λπ$, is nonlinearly unstable. These results clarify how total population and initial spatial aggregation jointly determine collapse or bounded redistribution, and how stable peripheral enrichment can occur within the radial model.
The small Deborah number limit for the fluid-particle flows: incompressible case
Zhendong Fang; Kunlun Qi; Huanyao Wen

This work is devoted to the study of the hydrodynamic limit for the fluid-particle flows governed by the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck (VFP) equation coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes (INS) equation as the Deborah number approaches to zero. The limit is valid globally in time provided that the initial perturbation is small in a neighborhood of a steady state. The proof is based on a formal derivation of the limiting system via the Hilbert approach, followed by a rigorous justification via introducing a novel decomposition involving some macroscopic quantities and a refined energy estimate motivated by macro-micro decomposition. In contrast to the existing results for the same scaled model, the present work provides the first one on the hydrodynamic limits in a strong sense with an explicit convergence rate.
On the median of the beta distribution in relation to the median of the gamma distribution

The median of the beta distribution has no closed form, but it is closely tied to the median of the gamma distribution. Kerman's approximation has the ratio form $g(α)/(g(α)+g(β))$ with $g(x) = x - 1/3$, a lower bound on the gamma median, and it is a lower bound on the beta median for $1/3 < α< β$. The ratio form built from the true gamma median is a tighter lower bound, asymptotically exact as $β\to \infty$. The ratio form built from the Wilson-Hilferty approximation to the gamma median, implicit in a classical approximation to the $F$ distribution but little known as an approximation to the beta median, is an upper bound on the edge $α= 1$ and for large shape parameters. The ratio form that is exact on the lines $α= 1$ and $β= 1$ yields a new approximation to the gamma median, which is an upper bound on it for shape parameter below 1 and a lower bound above 1; no ratio form gives the beta median exactly. For large shape parameters, the logit of the median has an explicit second-order expansion. For small shape parameters, bounds in elementary functions are asymptotically tight, and odds-corrected forms of the low-$α$ asymptote, with an elementary factor that is exact on the edges $α= 1$ and $β= 1$, are, numerically, one-sided bounds within 0.44% of the median that are exact on the lines $α= 1$, $β= 1$, and $α= β$. Steering their exponents with four fitted constants, and interpolating between two ratio forms where both shape parameters exceed 1, gives an approximation in elementary functions that is exact on those lines and numerically within 0.065% of the median over the whole domain. Most of the proofs are machine-verified in Lean 4.
Generalized Transition Fronts and Spectral Speed Asymptotics in Heterogeneous Cooperative Systems

We study generalized transition fronts for cooperative reaction--diffusion systems with spatially periodic and time-dependent coefficients. We obtain sufficient conditions for the existence of fronts and necessary constraints on their propagation speeds in terms of generalized principal eigenvalues. In the almost-periodic case, we identify the two spectral thresholds and examine the attainment of the critical speed under additional hypotheses on the normalized linear evolution. We then investigate the large-advection limit and construct a time-periodic example showing that a stationary spectral characterization need not extend to time-dependent flows. For symmetric cooperative systems in stationary periodic shears with equal diffusion matrices, we obtain explicit correction terms for the minimal speed in both the small- and large-diffusion limits. The two expansions follow from periodic eigenvalue perturbation, localization near a maximal streamline, and minimization over the exponential weight. We also establish a higher-order large-advection expansion and present numerical illustrations independent of the analytic proofs.
Distributed online learning with growing dimensions for stochastic large regression

This paper investigates distributed online estimation and prediction for stochastic large regression models with infinitely many unknown parameters. Existing distributed estimation methods are mostly restricted to finite-dimensional parameter spaces, making them inadequate for emerging infinite-dimensional modeling applications. To tackle this problem, this paper proposes a fully distributed online recursive least squares algorithm with dynamically growing model dimension.The algorithm is constructed with an incrementally augmentable recursive structure, where new parameter dimensions can be embedded in the recursion via zero-padded covariance and estimate augmentation without re-initialization.The almost sure convergence of the algorithm is established under a weak cooperative non-persistent excitation condition, without requiring independence or stationarity assumptions on the regressors.This condition integrates spatio-temporal network information and extends existing finite-dimensional results. The paper further derives an almost sure upper bound on the accumulated prediction regret without any excitation conditions. It is proven that the average regret converges to zero almost surely for a broad class of dimension growth sequences, with the optimal finite-dimensional regret bound recovered as a special case. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to verify the effectiveness of our theoretical findings.
Pair-Dependent Judge Errors Change the Minimax Rate of Semantic Entropy
Jiamiao Liu; Dewen Qiao; Yu Zhang; Xuetao Chen

Semantic entropy, the entropy of the meanings among a language model's sampled answers, is estimated from the verdicts of a judge that declares pairs of answers equivalent or not, and automatic judges err in ways that depend on the answers they compare. The existing minimax theory covers only judges whose false-equivalence probability is the same for all pairs. We model a known judge that declares two answers with meanings $a$ and $b$ equivalent with probability $q+ΔM_{ab}$, for a symmetric matrix $M$ and $q$ bounded away from $0$ and $1$, and show that for three meanings the rate is set by tree statistics on four answers, while on an open set of channels the consistency threshold is set by trees on five. For every channel in an explicit open class, the minimax squared risk is of order $N^{-1/3}$ with $N=n^4Δ^6$ on polynomial weak windows on which $n^5Δ^8$ exceeds a multiple of $\log n$, and of order $\min\{1,N^{-1/3}\}$ on every polynomial weak window when the tree functions on at most four vertices are injective. The exponent comes from a cubic degeneracy at the equitable point. On an open set of channels in the class, the four-vertex tree functions take equal values at two distributions with different entropies. For such a channel, on every polynomial weak window, the minimax risk is of the order of the sum of $\min\{1,N^{-1/3}\}$ and a term that decays exponentially in $n^5Δ^8$, so no estimator is consistent while $n^5Δ^8$ stays bounded, even as $N\to\infty$. For $Δ=n^{-β}$ with $β>1/2$, channels of the class with injective four-vertex tree functions allow consistent estimation exactly for $β<2/3$, and the channels of this open set exactly for $β<5/8$, at which the risk exponent drops from $1/12$ to $0$. Computer-assisted certificates show that both kinds of channels occur on open sets.
NS-Leibniz bialgebras, the Yang--Baxter equation and relative Rota--Baxter operators

We introduce NS-Leibniz bialgebras and establish their equivalence with matched pairs and Manin triples of NS-Leibniz algebras. In the coboundary case, skew-symmetric solutions of the NS-Leibniz Yang--Baxter equation yield NS-Leibniz bialgebras and correspond to $\mathcal{O}$-operators for the dual regular representation. We study quasi-triangular and factorizable structures, and relate factorizable tensors to quadratic Rota--Baxter NS-Leibniz algebras of any fixed nonzero weight. We also construct compatible bialgebra structures from skew-adjoint Nijenhuis operators commuting with the Rota--Baxter operator.
Generalized Discrete Fractal Dimensions of Graph Families
Jiantao Liu; Cheng Zeng; Yumei Xue; Qingcheng Zeng

Quantifying the self-similarity of complex networks via discrete fractal dimensions is a fundamental problem in network science. In this paper, we investigate some general fractal dimensions of graph families based on q-energy and Rényi entropy. We first establish several bounds for the energy, and then discuss the monotonicity, measure invariance of the dimensions, as well as some concrete graph families.
Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics on nilpotent Lie groups and the quasicentroid condition

We study left-invariant Gray $\mathcal{A}$-metrics (cyclic-parallel Ricci tensor) on nilpotent Lie groups, focusing on the algebraic condition that the Ricci operator belongs to the quasicentroid $\operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ of the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{n}$. We review and develop the abstract structure theory of quasicentroids, and prove a Central Decomposition Theorem: any nilpotent Riemannian Lie algebra with $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$ decomposes as a central product of ideals $\mathfrak{i}_j = E_{λ_j} \oplus \mathfrak{z}$, where $\mathfrak{z}$ is the center of $\mathfrak{n}$ and $E_{λ_j}$ are the negative Ricci eigenspaces. Endowed with the restricted metric, each factor $\mathfrak{i}_j$ is itself a Gray $\mathcal{A}$-space. Finally, we investigate when the general $\mathcal{A}$-metric condition reduces to $\operatorname{Ric} \in \operatorname{QC}(\mathfrak{n})$. We prove this equivalence unconditionally for two-step nilpotent algebras and whenever the metric admits a nice basis, and provide a general characterization via the vanishing of two trace identities.
Sharp derivative inequalities for maximal functions
Sung-Yi Liao; José Madrid; Eyvindur Ari Palsson

We determine the optimal constant in the $L^p$-derivative inequality for the uncentered Hardy--Littlewood maximal operator on the real line for every $1<p<\infty$. It is the unique number $γ_p\in [0,1]$ satisfying $(2p-1)γ_p+(p-1)γ_p^{(2p-1)/(p-1)}=p$. As $p$ goes from $1$ to $+\infty$, $γ_p$ decreases from $1$ to $\sqrt2-1$, and at the endpoints the limiting arguments recover the classical total-variation and Lipschitz inequalities, with the qualitative regularity ingredient at the $BV$ endpoint supplied by Aldaz and Pérez Lázaro.
Adaptive Bayesian Estimation of Conditional Densities Based on Orthogonal Polynomials

We study Bayesian estimation of conditional densities represented by normalized squares of orthogonal polynomial series. We specify the conditional density without modeling the marginal distribution of covariates. A prior on smoothness, the number of terms, and the coefficients gives adaptive posterior contraction at the minimax rate without a logarithmic factor when the normalized square-root representation of the true density is bounded away from zero and sufficiently smooth. For one outcome and $d_x$ covariates, the rate over classes with degree smoothness $s$ is $n^{-s/(2s+d_x+1)}$. The posterior predictive density attains the corresponding minimax squared Hellinger risk. For bounded nonnegative representations in Legendre and Chebyshev classes, we establish the minimax rate at every $s>0$. A prior that also permits a small mixture with the reference density adapts over these classes up to a logarithmic factor and retains the exact rate on the positive, sufficiently smooth subclass. Additional results concern identification, conditional distribution functions and quantiles, coefficient recovery and uniform convergence, independent Gaussian coefficient priors, and selection of polynomial terms.
Simplified dense model theorem for random discrete structures

Dense model theorems of Conlon and Gowers associate to each subset of a sparse random structure a dense set with approximately the same size and configuration counts after rescaling. This allows dense extremal results to be transferred to the random setting. Allen, Böttcher, Lada, and Mergoni Cecchelli recently generalised this approach and established a dense model theorem in an abstract hypergraph framework, with hypotheses that are readily verified in many applications. Both proofs use the separating hyperplane theorem to reduce the existence of dense models to an anti-correlation estimate. We give a simplified proof of a version of this theorem, inspired by the method of hypergraph containers. Our proof constructs dense models from small fingerprints, combining sampling with the Rödl-Ruciński deletion method.

Can random real carry arbitrary information. In terms of (Turing) computability, Kučera and Gács addressed this question in affirmative. i.e., Every real $x\in 2^ω$ is computable from some Martin-Löf random real. This result motivated quantitative versions of coding into random reals. i.e., How many bits of the random oracle are needed to compute the first $n$ bits of $x$. Barmpalias and Lewis-Pye obtained a coding that uses $n+O(\log n)$ many bits. Is it possible for the coding to use $n$ bits exactly? This is equivalent to say, if every real is $rK$-reducible to a Martin-Löf random real. In this paper, we prove that such a coding does not exist. i.e., There exists some real that is not $rK$-reducible to any Martin-Löf random real.
Cardinality of the K-cones below a non infinitely often $K$-trivial

Given a real $x\in 2^ω$, how many reals are there that are simpler (or equally simple) to describe than $x$. With ``simpler to describe" characterized by $K$-complexity of initial segments (hence we call such $y$ with $y\leq_K x$ a solution to $x$), if $x$ is infinitely often $K$-trivial (hence i.o. $K$-trivial), then a simple counting argument shows that the number of solutions to $x$ is countable. If $x$ is non i.o. $K$-trivial, then must it admit uncountably many solutions? Motivated by this question, we show that: (1) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ such that most of its solution is i.o. $K$-trivial. i.e., Only countably many solution to $x$ are non i.o. $K$-trivial. In particular, the cardinality of $K$-degree of $x$ is countable. (2) There is a minimal pair of K-degree (meaning their common solutions are all $K$-trivial) so that each of the pair is non i.o. $K$-trivial, generalizing a result of Csima and Montalbán (where the pair is not required to be non i.o. $K$-trivial but non $K$-trivial). (3) There is a non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$ whose $Δ_K$ complexity grows arbitrarily slow (in a weak sense: $\inf_{m\geq n}Δ_K(x\upharpoonright m)\leq h(n)$ with $h$ a given unbounded and nondecreasing function) such that $x$ admits uncountably many solutions. (4) An ample excess lemma holds for non i.o. $K$-trivial. Namely: $$ \sum_n 2^{-(K(x\upharpoonright n)- \log_2 n)}<\infty. $$ for all non i.o. $K$-trivial $x$. Actually, this even holds for non i.o. $b$-$K$-trivial with $b$ only depends on the universal prefix free machine. The same argument also gives a constant complexity return phenomenon for $K$-trivial where this constant only depends on the universal prefix free machine.
On the well-posedness of a certain model with mixed diffusion appearing in the mathematical biology

The work deals with establishing the global well-posedness in the space $W^{(1,2),2}(R^{2}\times R^{+})$ of the integro-differential equation in the space of two dimensions in the situation when the diffusion term involves the standard Laplace operator in one direction and the fractional Laplacian in another direction in the presence of the drift term. Such model is relevant to the cell population dynamics in the Mathematical Biology. The proof is based on a fixed point technique.
Classification of Anti-symmetric Solutions to Fractional Lane-Emden System in Borderline Case

We investigate the existence and non-existence of anti-symmetric solutions to the fractional Lane--Emden system in the half-space $\mathbb{R}^n_+$: \begin{equation*}\begin{cases} (-Δ)^s u = v^p & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n_+, (-Δ)^s v = u^q & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^n_+, \end{cases}\end{equation*} where $0<s<\frac{1}{2},p,q>0,2s+p=1$, with $u,v$ nonnegative in $\mathbb{R}^n_+$ and anti-symmetric with respect to $\partial\mathbb{R}^n_+$. Li and Zhuo [2023, Sci. China Math.] previously proved non-existence in $L_{2s}$, as well as non-existence in the extended space $L_{2s+1}$ when $1-2s<p,q<\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$ and existence in $L_{2s+1}$ when $p+2s<1,q+2s<1$. In this paper, we fill the remaining borderline case $p=1-2s$ in $L_{2s+1}$ space. We establish a non-existence result for $1-2s=p\leq q\leq\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$ and an existence result for $0<q<p=1-2s$. For the non-existence result, we combine a maximum principle for anti-symmetric functions with the method of moving planes to derive a Liouville--type theorem when $1-2s<q\leq\frac{n+2s}{n-2s}$. We then iterate the lower-bound estimates to obtain a contradiction through blow-up. To prove the existence of nontrivial solutions when $0<q<1-2s$, we construct a nonhomogeneous solution by a monotone iteration scheme in $L_{2s+1}$ as well as analyze a homogeneous profile. Surprisingly, the homogeneous profile serves as a universal lower bound for all solutions.
Locally unital $C^*$-algebras and limitations of seminorm criteria for compact operators

We study the problem of geometric characterization of Banach-compact and $\mathcal A$-compact operators on Hilbert $C^*$-modules in terms of uniform structures generated by seminorms. Previously, such a criterion for $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators was obtained by Troitsky for countably generated range modules with a suitable system of seminorms. Using locally unital $C^*$-algebras as modules over themselves, we establish fundamental limitations of such characterizations. Namely, we show that for nonunital locally unital $C^*$-algebras not only does Troitsky's criterion fail to extend, but, more generally, no system of seminorms can characterize $\mathcal A$-precompactness by total boundedness, nor Banach-compactness of bounded operators or $\mathcal A$-compactness of adjointable operators by total boundedness of the images of the unit ball. Moreover, the same statement holds for Hilbert $C^*$-modules $\mathcal N$ whenever the algebra $\mathbf K(\mathcal N)$ of $\mathcal A$-compact operators is locally unital and nonunital. We also study Troitsky-type systems of seminorms and their relation to $\mathcal A$-precompactness. We prove that every $\mathcal A$-precompact subset is totally bounded with respect to the strongest of such structures. Consequently, for Hilbert $C^*$-modules admitting a standard frame, all the corresponding notions of total boundedness coincide.
Capillary-gravity water waves with compactly supported vorticity II. Continuation and folds of the solution curve

This five-part series establishes the first systematic theory of capillary--gravity water waves carrying compactly supported vorticity with fixed positive circulation. Treating the free surface and the vortex as coupled unknowns, we study the well-posedness of traveling-wave equilibria, including the existence and continuation of solution branches with respect to bifurcation parameters, as well as their variational structure, geometric rigidity, canonical classification, and conditional dynamics. In this second paper of the series, we apply the Haziot-Wheeler analytic continuation theorem to extend the small-speed point-vortex branch constructed in Part I to a global curve of coupled equilibria. We establish two alternatives: either the geometric control quantity diverges, or it remains bounded along a sequence of solutions with no strongly convergent subsequence. If the second alternative occurs, we use concentration--compactness to obtain a finite profile decomposition without assuming monotonicity of the free surface: a nontrivial centered vortex wave and finitely many reflected pairs of irrotational waves, with a remainder converging strongly to zero. At any simple speed fold, a Schur-complement reduction in the physical vortex coordinate shows that the static energy-momentum Hessians of the two nearby equal-speed waves differ by one in negative index within the symmetric class. Finally, we use a joint two-parameter Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction to extend the regularization of Part I to compact arcs of the global solution curve, carrying the canonical smooth-core branches through their specified simple speed folds. These results provide a global point-vortex reference for the variational construction in Part III and canonical smooth-core comparison arcs for the rigidity and uniqueness theory in Part IV.
Well-posedness of Rough Differential Equations at the Krylov-Röckner Integrability Threshold

We study rough differential equations (RDEs) driven by Brownian (Itô) rough paths with uniformly locally integrable drifts. The diffusion coefficient is assumed to be uniformly elliptic, of class $C^{2+}$ in space and of bounded variation in time, while the drift is $q$-integrable in time and $p$-integrable in space, uniformly on balls of a fixed radius, for some $p,q$ satisfying the Krylov--Röckner condition $\frac dp+\frac2q<1$. We show that, for almost every realization of the Itô rough path lift of the Brownian motion, such an RDE has a unique solution for every initial value. In other words, for almost every realization of the Itô lift, the corresponding rough differential equation has exactly one solution in the class of Davie-type solutions, for every initial value; this is the appropriate notion of path-by-path uniqueness for the corresponding stochastic differential equation (SDE) with multiplicative noise. The proof follows the strategy of Shaposhnikov (2016). The principal new ingredients are the stability of RDEs with bounded variation perturbation and Davie-type estimates for the flow of the driftless equation with non-constant diffusion coefficients, which we derive from known maximal regularity estimates for the corresponding parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs).
Capillary-gravity water waves with compactly supported vorticity I: Local constructions and regular drift

This five-part series establishes the first systematic theory of capillary--gravity water waves carrying compactly supported vorticity with fixed positive circulation. Treating the free surface and the vortex as coupled unknowns, we study the well-posedness of traveling-wave equilibria, including the existence and continuation of solution branches with respect to bifurcation parameters, as well as their variational structure, geometric rigidity, canonical classification, and conditional dynamics. In this first paper, we construct small-speed solitary waves carrying a point vortex of fixed circulation by solving the free-surface Bernoulli equation and the regular-drift condition simultaneously. We derive the free-surface expansion through fourth order, including the first capillary correction, and second-order corrections to the conformal and physical vortex depths. We also characterize vortex equilibria in prescribed domains through the Kirchhoff--Routh function, proving existence and uniform localization. A joint Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction then regularizes the point vortex into a smooth, compactly supported vorticity core while preserving its circulation and the prescribed vorticity law. Finally, in the periodic setting, we construct a local branch under a nonresonance condition and show that the vortex depth diverges logarithmically as the wave speed approaches a positive limit, in contrast to its inverse-speed growth in the solitary-wave setting.
Sharp approximation thresholds for power means of common-subspace volumes

We study how well a single $k$-dimensional subspace can preserve volume from several positive semidefinite matrices at once. Each matrix is compressed to the subspace and scored by the geometric mean of the eigenvalues of that compression; the scores are aggregated by a weighted power mean of order $p \le 1$. For every fixed $k$ and every fixed rational $p$ we determine the optimal approximation factor: it is achieved by a randomized polynomial-time algorithm, and every larger constant is NP-hard. Above a critical power ($p=-k/2$ over the reals and $p=-k$ over the complex numbers) the factor is an explicit product of Gamma functions. At and below the critical power, every positive constant-factor approximation is NP-hard. The factor comes from a concave relaxation over the positive semidefinite matrices of trace one, which agrees with the volume score at every subspace, followed by ordinary Gaussian rounding. For two rank-$k$ matrices the relaxation is exact, giving a closed-form optimum for Martin means of two subspaces.
Power-Type Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with the Logarithmic Laplacian

We prove global existence of the Cauchy problem of a Schrodinger equation with the logarithmic laplacian and a pure power linearity. We address the focusing and the defocusing cases, and we obtained a sharp blow-up in time result.
Phase Retrieval of Bandlimited Signals Using a Morlet Wavelet and an Admissible Companion
Bei Liu; Meng Ning; Liping Wu; Qingyue Zhang

In this paper, we demonstrate that complex bandlimited signals can be uniquely recovered (up to a global phase factor) from two families of wavelet transform magnitudes, sampled at twice the Nyquist rate in two frequency bins. These families come from translations of the fixed dilated Morlet wavelet and a fixed companion wavelet. The companion wavelet admits an augmented Morlet--Gaussian representation. We rewrite the two families as two modulated Gaussian convolution measurements of an auxiliary bandlimited signal. Using a Gaussian convolution uniqueness result, we prove that samples on \((4B)^{-1}\mathbb{Z}\) determine every signal in \(PW_B^2\) (up to a global phase factor). Compared with earlier wavelet phase retrieval results, our approach requires significantly fewer sampling points.
Convergence rates of mixed primal-dual dynamical systems with implicit Hessian damping and Tikhonov regularization
Hong-lu Li; Yi-bin Xiao; Xin He; Kequan Zhao

We propose a mixed-order primal--dual dynamical system with implicit Hessian damping and Tikhonov regularization for linearly constrained convex optimization, and derive a corresponding fast primal--dual algorithm. The proposed dynamical system couples a second-order primal equation with a first-order dual equation without requiring twice differentiability of the objective function. An energy analysis establishes $\mathcal{O}(t^{-2})$ convergence rates for the augmented Lagrangian gap, feasibility violation, and objective residual along an extrapolated primal trajectory. For the proposed algorithm, we construct discrete energy estimates and establish the corresponding $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2})$ rates at the extrapolated primal iterates. In particular, in the critical regularization regimes $ε(t)=a/t^2$ and $ε_k=a/k^2$, these accelerated rates hold simultaneously with strong convergence of the primal trajectory and primal iterates to the minimum-norm solution, respectively, under suitable parameter and trajectory conditions. Numerical experiments illustrate the convergence behavior of the proposed dynamical system and the corresponding algorithm.
A Paley-Wiener-Type Theorem with Applications to Inverse Medium Scattering for the Schrödinger Equation
Guanghui Hu; Yubiao Zhang; Tianyi Zheng; Jun Zou

This paper develops a new uniqueness framework for inverse scattering problems for the time-harmonic Schrödinger equation using multi-frequency data. Our approach is based on a Paley-Wiener-type theorem that characterizes the support of the potential through the asymptotic growth of a generalized Fourier integral along imaginary frequencies, allowing for nontrivial amplitude functions. Within this framework, we obtain two major results on identifying the shape of the support of the potential in three dimensions, for both the plane-wave incidence and point source incidence, respectively. For plane-wave incidence, we prove that the location and shape of the convex compact support of an essentially bounded potential are uniquely determined by fixed-angle far-field data from two opposite incident directions or by backscattering far field data, provided that the potential is real-valued and sign-definite near the boundary of its support. For point-source incidence, we show that near-field backscattering data, namely the scattered field evaluated at the source point as the source ranges over a sufficiently large sphere, uniquely determine the location and shape of the convex support under the same assumptions on the potential. The proofs rely on meromorphic extension and the Paley-Wiener-type theorem.
Numerical schemes for 1D capacitively coupled plasma fluid simulation
Yipei Chen; Ganghua Fan; Yuwei Fan; Haoran Guan; Kangxin Liu; Zhonghua Qiao; Yufeng Wei; Peiting You; Zhenyu Zou

Capacitively coupled plasmas (CCP) are widely used in semiconductor manufacturing, where fluid models provide an efficient approach to the simulation of the low-temperature discharge. The model considered in this work couples the electron and the ion continuity equations, the electron energy equation and the Poisson's equation for the electric potential. We investigate the numerical schemes for the simulation of the 1D-CCP. In particular, a semi-implicit Scharfetter-Gummel (SG) scheme is adopted for the Poisson's equation, while the remaining equations are solved using the implicit SG schemes. The proposed strategy can be naturally extended to the 2D cases. Several alternative schemes are also discussed and tested. Numerical experiments compare these methods in terms of the admissible time step $Δt$, total simulation time, accuracy against a reference solution and robustness of the scheme. We propose a numerical scheme for the 1D-CCP and, to the best of our knowledge, provide the first detailed numerical analysis of such a scheme for CCP.
The estimate of lifespan for ideal incompressible MHD systems

This paper concerns the lifespan estimate for three-dimensional ideal incompressible MHD systems. By introducing $L^{3/2}$-type energy, we lower the regularity assumption for the initial data as well as the order of the highest derivatives involved in the total weighted energy estimate. The new weights proposed in this paper are symmetric, unified, and compatible with both $L^2$-type energy and $L^{3/2}$-type energy.
Beyond energy bounds: comparing Schrödinger eigenstates
Xiao-Ke Wang; Han Jia; Shengjun Wu; Zeng-Bing Chen

We derive eigenstate comparisons from ordered Schrödinger operators, extending energy bounds to overlaps, spatial distributions and nodes. For three form-ordered operators with discrete comparison ground states, suppose the upper ground-state energy lies in the lower operator's ground-state gap. Three comparison spectral values then bound all three squared ground-state overlaps and guarantee a simple discrete intermediate ground state. Related gap estimates control low-energy subspaces and individual excited-state overlaps under additional gap conditions. In one dimension and radially, a single crossing of the potential difference relative to the energy shift orders ground-state likelihood ratios and monotone observables; a nondecreasing difference suffices. The results cover asymmetric wells and shortened right Dirichlet walls, with coordinatewise comparisons for submodular reference potentials and coordinatewise nondecreasing perturbations. A two-sided Sturm argument orders corresponding internal nodes for nondecreasing potential differences, even between orthogonal one-dimensional excited states. For Yukawa ground states, Hulthén comparisons bound overlaps, radial moments and the density at the nucleus; the latter two-sided bounds hold for screening $0<δ<2/\sqrt6$. Optimizing scaled Hulthén majorants gives a lower bound of approximately $1.13611$ for $n^2δ_c(n,0)$, where $δ_c(n,0)$ is the critical screening for the $n$th $s$-wave bound state. This bound is optimal within that two-parameter comparison family.
Revisiting Guo-Huang-Wang-Wei pointwise estimates for radial solutions to the fourth-order Hénon equation in the punctured space

We study pointwise estimates for positive, $C^4$-solution $u$ to the fourth-order Hénon equation \[ Δ^2 u = |x|^σu^p \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] with $n \geq 5$, $p>1$, and $σ>-4 $. In an earlier work published in J. Anal. Math. 140 (2020) 371-394, Z. Guo, X. Huang, L. Wang, and J. Wei established the following pointwise estimate \[ -Δu \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac {n(n-4)}{n^2-4}} u^\frac{n}{n-4} \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] for radial solutions to the critical, fourth-order Lane-Emden equation, namely $σ= 0$ and $p=(n+4)/(n-4)$. Inspired by this interesting result, we establish a similar pointwise inequality \[ -Δu \geq \frac 2{n-4} \frac{|\nabla u|^2}u + \sqrt{\frac 2{p+1- \frac 8{n(n-4)}}} |x|^{\frac σ2} u^\frac{p+1}2 \quad \text{in } \mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\} \] for radial solutions to the fourth-order Hénon equation in $\mathbf R^n \setminus \{0\}$ for any $σ\geq 0$ and $p \geq (n+4 + σ)/(n-4)$. We also show that the constant $2/(n-4)$ is sharp and that the thresholds $σ\geq 0$ and $p \geq (n+4 + σ)/(n-4)$ are necessary. As in our previous study on the case of $\mathbf R^n$, our proof is also based on the Bernstein technique via the maximum principle, hence appears to be simpler and more constructive. However, to avoid possible singularity at the origin, we develop a Bernstein technique in one-dimensional space, which is capable of handling equations in punctured spaces.
Tikhonov-Regularized Dynamics and Inexact Algorithms for Nonlinear Saddle-Point Problems

In this paper, we study a Tikhonov-regularized second-order primal--dual dynamical system for smooth nonlinear convex--concave saddle-point problems in real Hilbert spaces. The dynamical system incorporates a vanishing damping coefficient $α/t$, a Hessian-driven term, and a critical Tikhonov regularization coefficient $c/t^2$. By constructing suitable Lyapunov functions, we establish strong convergence to the minimum-norm saddle point and fast convergence rates under the same parameter conditions, without imposing any eventual inside/outside-ball condition. Specifically, the primal--dual trajectory converges strongly to the minimum-norm saddle point, while the primal--dual gap and the velocity norm decay at rates $o(t^{-2})$ and $o(t^{-1})$, respectively. Furthermore, we propose an inexact primal--dual algorithm with a computable relative residual criterion and prove strong convergence of the generated sequence to the same minimum-norm saddle point, together with an $o(k^{-2})$ convergence rate for the primal--dual gap. Finally, numerical experiments on nonlinear and bilinear problems of different dimensions illustrate the minimum-norm selection property and compare the performance of the proposed dynamical system and algorithm with related methods.
Convergence of Levenberg--Marquardt method in Banach spaces

We study the Levenberg--Marquardt method for nonlinear inverse problems in Banach spaces under a Hölder stability estimate. Under suitable assumptions on the geometry of the Banach space and the Fréchet derivative of the measurement operator, we establish the well-definedness of the method, local convergence and convergence rates for exact data, and the monotonic decrease of the Bregman distance up to the stopping index for noisy data. These results extend the corresponding Hilbert space theory to the Banach space setting.
The inverse local-relative correspondence and the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation
Jianjun Fu; Shuai Guo; Qingsheng Zhang

We prove the Nekrasov--Shatashvili vanishing blowup equation for the local Gromov--Witten theory of smooth weak del Pezzo surfaces, by identifying its unique formal solution with the inverse of the local-relative correspondence. We construct this inverse through an associative set-partition convolution and establish the identification using Zagier's recursion for the Bloch--Okounkov $n$-point function. The proof applies in all genera and includes non-toric surfaces.
CA2 numbers and the Riemann hypothesis: a numerical investigation of Ramanujan's inequalities
Dmitry R. Leshchiner; Oleg R. Musin; James Thompson

Robin's criterion reduces the Riemann hypothesis to an inequality for colossally abundant (CA) numbers, and Wu's theorem reduces the test further to the subclass CA2. We study this reduction numerically and consider smaller subsets on which the same criterion remains sufficient. We also show that the logarithmic decay law suggested by Briggs's computations follows from Ramanujan's conditional bounds. To investigate the next term, we compare the normalized Robin difference with Ramanujan's oscillatory expression involving the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function. The resulting difference has a slowly varying component on both CA and CA2. Its scaled values continue to vary over the computed range, leading to questions about convergence, upper bounds, and higher-order terms. We describe the sampling used in the figures and estimate the error from truncating the sum over zeros.
Some results on intersecting families of triangulations

Kalai conjectured that the largest intersecting family of triangulations of an $n$-gon is the family consisting of all triangulations that contain a fixed ear (a chord of length $2$). What happens if we strengthen the intersecting condition to the condition that any two of the triangulations must intersect on a chord from a specified family of chords -- for example, what if any two triangulations intersect on a chord from some fixed point of the $n$-gon, or intersect on an ear? In this paper we verify Kalai's conjecture for families of triangulations in which any two intersect on a chord from some fixed point. We also show that any ear-intersecting family of triangulations has size at most $T_{n-1} +T_{n-3} = T_{n-1}(17/16 + o(1))$, where $T_{n-1}$ is the upper bound in Kalai's conjecture, namely the number of triangulations of an $(n-1)$-gon. This is based on an exact upper bound of $T_{n-1}$ for the size of a family of triangulations in which any two intersect on some ear from the set of all ears with one ear excluded.
An Autonomous Spectral Representation for Fully Asymmetric Spherical Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Dynamics

We study the large size dynamics of a fully asymmetric spherical Sherrington- Kirkpatrick model, allowing for a distinguished random signal that interacts with the evolving spin configuration. We first derive the large-N dynamical mean-field limit and characterize the law of a typical coordinate by an effective Gaussian process whose covariance must satisfy a self-consistency relation. The resulting formulation is intrinsically nonlocal in time and is not, in its usual form, a closed finite-dimensional dynamical system. Our main contribution is an autonomous spectral representation of this limiting dynamics. We introduce an auxiliary stationary chain of Gaussian replicas whose one-step marginal reproduces the effective field appearing in the dynamical mean- field equation. Applying a matrix-valued Herglotz representation, or equivalently Fourier analysis in the replica index, converts the covariance structure of the chain into a family of finite-dimensional matrix-valued evolution equations indexed by the unit circle. The macroscopic observables, including the signal overlap, are then recovered from explicit spectral integrals. This representation replaces the original two-time self-consistency problem by an autonomous spectral closure and provides a convenient framework for both analysis and numerical computation. We prove the validity of the representation and compare its predictions with direct simulations of the finite-dimensional system
Frequency-induced Tipping: Resonance-Driven Tipping in a Threshold Predator-Prey System
Shan Gao; Silas Poloni; Hao Wang; Mark Lewis

Tipping points refer to abrupt, substantial, and often irreversible transitions in dynamic systems that can be triggered by minor perturbations. Existing tipping mechanisms are usually classified by the nature of the trigger: bifurcation-induced tipping occurs when a parameter crosses a critical threshold, noise-induced tipping is caused by random perturbations, rate-induced tipping occurs when a system fails to track a moving attractor, and phase-induced tipping is triggered by timed perturbations relative to an oscillatory state. In this paper, we identify a new mechanism for tipping: frequency-induced tipping, in which periodic forcing drives a transition through resonant amplification. This occurs by destabilization of an equilibrium via subthreshold perturbations of the appropriate frequency. Filippov analysis of a piecewise-smooth model identifies admissible crossings that lead either to predator loss or to extinction of predator and prey, and numerical simulations show that tipping persists after smoothing of the thresholds. These results extend the current tipping framework to include critical transitions under recurrent environmental forcing.
Communication and Privacy Trade-Offs in Distributed Storage With Shared Secret Keys

We study distributed storage over public communication channels where privacy is realized using shared secret keys. Specifically, a user wishes to store a file across $L$ servers such that any subset of at least $t$ servers can reconstruct the file, while any subset of at most $z$ colluding servers learns no more than a fraction $α$ of the file. Unlike classical secret-sharing models that assume secure communication channels between the user and each server, we consider a setting where all transmissions occur over a public channel and the user shares an individual secret key of length $n$ bits with each server. For a fixed key length $n$, we characterize the trade-off between the privacy leakage parameter $α$ and the maximum file size that can be securely stored. Additionally, we determine the minimum local randomness, public communication, and storage required to achieve this optimal trade-off.
Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
Andrea Novero; Mudasir Ahmad Sheikh; Danish Nisar; Saif Khan Mohammed; Michele Zorzi; Robert Calderbank

Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. Deciding two-variable logic with global and local Presburger quantification

We look at a two-variable logic over finite graphs that allows Presburger quantifiers: linear arithmetic inequalities between the number of elements that satisfy subformulas. The prior literature shows that closing two-variable logic under Presburger quantification leads to undecidability, while closing under \emph{local quantification} -- the counts are always over neighbors of a given node -- preserves decidability. Here we show decidability of satisfiability for an intermediate logic that allows both local counts and global counts, but where the linear constraints do not mix the two. The proof requires a significant extension of the prior machinery developed for two-variable logic with counting. As a corollary we obtain decidability of satisfiability for an important family of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). GNNs are a popular graph learning formalism. For example, in a variation of GNNs considered in the past literature, local aggregation is used in each layer to create modified values at each vertex of a graph, and then global aggregation is used in a final layer to obtain a single numerical value for the graph as a whole. Our logic is motivated by the fact that mixing of local counting and global aggregation in GNNs has been shown to lead to undecidability. Our results here show that if global and local aggregation are separated, one regains decidability. Decidability of other static analysis problems, like equivalence of GNNs, follows from the decidability of satisfiability.
Minimally-coupled Quasilinear Symmetric Hyperbolic Systems, Naturally

We consider symmetric hyperbolicity and well-posedness in the context of natural equations, which are closed subobjects of jet bundles over natural bundles. We show how non-natural equations can be "naturalized", and we discuss how a precise version of "minimal coupling" offers a (provably unique, up to isomorphism) method for constructing natural equations from certain equations defined on a single manifold.
