Two oscillators at fixed total energy give exact master evolution, an exact realization of this covariance shear, and the reduced symplectic limit. For the non-Abelian SL(2,$\R$) model we compute the coherent and Weyl master symbols, prove essential self-adjointness and a finite-time propagation estimate, and derive the spectral bottom $\hbar^2/2$.

If $F$ is a number field and $F = F_0 \subset F_1 \subset F_2\subset \cdots$ is a tower of Galois extensions with $\mathrm{Gal}(F_n/F)$ cyclic of order $p^n$, K. Iwasawa gave a closed formula for the growth of the $p$-part of the class number of $F_n$ whenever $n$ is large enough. We present a new proof of this formula, obtained by reinterpreting its summands in terms of Sylvester matrix rank functions on the Iwasawa algebra $Λ$ without resorting to the classification of finitely-generated $Λ$-modules up to pseudo-isomorphism.
AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
David Voderholzer; Leonard Vetter; Thomas O'Leary-Roseberry

Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its spectral parameterization has no tensor-product dependence on the spatial dimension, it scales favorably to three dimensions, where FNO's spectral weights grow as $m^3$ with the number of spectral modes $m$. We prove that AMOR is a universal approximator of continuous operators. On two-dimensional structured-grid benchmarks, AMOR is competitive with FNO overall and surpasses PCANet: it outperforms FNO on nonlinear diffusion and Helmholtz problems, while a static snapshot basis keeps it from matching FNO's accuracy on the time-dependent Kolmogorov flow problem. On three-dimensional problems it matches or exceeds FNO's accuracy at lower inference cost on linear elastostatics while trailing FNO on a turbulent lid-driven-cavity flow and scales favorably to problems demanding high capacity. On irregular meshes, where FNO is not directly applicable, AMOR reduces the relative $L^2$ error over the FNO extension Geo-FNO by $31\%$ (airfoil) and $42\%$ (elasticity). Finally, AMOR maintains strong performance across three physically distinct, experimentally motivated loading regimes on a topologically nontrivial three-dimensional aircraft-rib mesh, demonstrating its applicability to realistic engineering problems without modification.
Minimal acceleration and the topology of premonotonic cocycles

In his global theory of one-frequency Schrödinger operators~\cite{Av15}, Avila asked whether the acceleration of a real-analytic $\SL(2,\R)$ cocycle over an irrational circle rotation is bounded below by the absolute value of its topological degree and whether equality in nonzero degree characterizes premonotonicity. We answer this question affirmatively for every irrational frequency, without arithmetic restrictions. Here premonotonicity means that some iterate becomes strictly monotonic in the base variable after a periodic change of coordinates~\cite{AK15}. In the positive Lyapunov exponent regime, this provides a nonzero-degree counterpart to Avila's characterization of uniform hyperbolicity by vanishing acceleration. In nonzero degree, we also characterize minimal acceleration through signed connections and invariant positive matrix-valued measures. In the positive-degree, positive Lyapunov exponent case, the proof constructs an analytic positive connection using invariant positive matrix-valued measures and a transfer--scattering representation. A complex-analytic construction then produces a periodic gauge. As a further consequence, for each fixed irrational frequency and nonzero degree, the premonotonic locus is path connected: every cocycle in this locus can be joined to the linear rotation of the same degree by a path preserving premonotonicity.
The Assouad Dimension of Graphs: An Affirmative Answer to Fraser's Question
Binyan Yu; Bilel Selmi; Jia Liu; Yongshun Liang

This article primarily investigates the Assouad dimension of graphs of continuous functions. Initially, the Assouad spectrum of the graph of a Hölder and count-Hölder continuous function has been derived. It has been shown that the Assouad dimension of the graph of a continuous function $f:[a,b]\to \mathbb{R}$ with the count-Hölder condition is at least \( 1 + \sup \left\{ \overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}L_f(y) : y \in \mathscr{R}_f[a,b]\right\} \) where $\overline{\dim}_{\mathrm{B}}$ denotes the upper box dimension, $L_f(y)$ is the level set of $f$ at level $y$, and $\mathscr{R}_f[a,b]$ is the range of $f$ on $[a,b]$. As a consequence, non-trivial lower bounds are obtained for the Assouad dimension of the graphs of classical functions such as the Weierstrass and Takagi functions. We have also employed a unified projection solely in the direction of the $y$-axis to establish lower and upper bounds for the Assouad dimension. On this basis, we have shown that the lower bound is sharp in terms of level sets, namely the upper box dimension cannot be replaced by the Assouad dimension. A supplementary explanation of why Brownian motion has the full Assouad dimension has also been provided based on the preceding work of Howroyd and Yu \cite{Howroyd2019}.
No Connectedness Lemma for Alexandrov spaces

Since its introduction in 2003, Wilking's Connectedness Lemma has become a powerful tool in the study of manifolds with positive sectional curvature. In recent work of the authors, this has been extended to orbifolds. The purpose of this note is to exhibit counterexamples in the class of Alexandrov spaces for the Connectedness Lemma in both its ordinary and dual formulation. This answers a 2007 question of Wilking.
Multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds and the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials

We establish uniform multicritical pseudo-Siegel bounds for polynomials of Zakeri type, where all free critical points are on the boundary of an invariant Siegel disk of bounded type. This generalizes the unicritical result~\cite{DL:wZ}. As an application, we show the optimality of the Brjuno condition under the Zakeri restriction: as the rotation number becomes non-Brjuno, the Siegel disk evolves into the Cremer Hedgehog. Combined with~\cite{BCR26}, this implies the optimality of the Brjuno condition for all neutral polynomials, resolving a conjecture by Douady from the 1980s.
Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts

We establish a quantitative local law for random $N$-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple graph with minimum degree at least three. Away from the singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum, we obtain high-probability entrywise Green's function estimates down to spectral scales $(\log N)^C/N$, uniformly in the bulk and near regular edges and cusps. As a consequence, we establish complete eigenvector delocalization: every normalized eigenvector $u$ whose eigenvalue stays a small but fixed positive distance away from the singular energies satisfies $\|u\|_\infty\leq(\log N)^C/\sqrt{N}$ with high probability.

A formation $\mathfrak{F}$ is said to be $S_n$-closed if every subnormal subgroup of every group in $\mathfrak{F}$ belongs to $\mathfrak{F}$. A. N. Skiba and L. A. Shemetkov posed the problem of proving that $\mathrm{form}(G)$ has only finitely many $S_n$-closed subformations for every group $G$ (Problem 14.81 of the Kourovka Notebook). In this paper we propose a negative answer to this problem. We prove that for the group $G_0=(\mathrm{SL}_2(5)\rtimes C_2)\times\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ of order 28800, where $C_2$ acts on $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)$ by an outer automorphism, the formation $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ has an infinite strictly descending chain of $S_n$-closed subformations. The main tool is a family of central-valued multilinear maps, defined for every group in $\mathrm{form}(G_0)$ by its outer actions on its components; their vanishing is preserved under taking epimorphic images, subdirect products and subnormal subgroups. The members of the chain are separated by central quotients of the groups $\mathrm{SL}_2(5)^{2^d-1}\rtimes C_2^d$, $d\geq 2$. Finally, we determine the intersection of the chain and give an explicit generator of it.

This note establishes a rank reduction for RLL-realization of quantum affine supergroups of orthosymplectic type. In the rational limit, this provides a more conceptual proof of the analogous result for orthosymplectic superYangians from arXiv:2311.18818. We also determine the exact scalar prefactor appearing in the evaluation of the universal $R$-matrix, refining the main result of arXiv:2408.16720.
Bubble Tree Convergence for Minimisers of a Regularised Baby-Skyrme Model

We study degree $1$ minimisers $u: (Σ,g) \to S^2$ for a Baby-Skyrme model with a Sacks-Uhlenbeck regularisation term $E^α(u) = \frac{1}{2} \int_Σ (1+\vert \nabla u \vert^2)^{α+1} -1 dv_g$ and establish convergence of degree $1$ minimisers to a simple bubble tree as $α\to 0$. We also obtain a new no-neck result for the classical Sacks-Uhlenbeck energy $E^α$.
A periodic minimal hypersurface in Euclidean 4-space with Clifford cone singularities

Let $σ(t)=\operatorname{sl}(\varpi t)$ be the lemniscatic sine, normalized to have period $2$. We study the zero set $\mathscr{M}$ of $S(x)=σ(x_1)σ(x_3)-σ(x_2)σ(x_4)$ in $\mathbb{R}^{4}$. Near every singular point $\mathscr{M}$ is an analytic image of the Clifford cone, and $\mathscr{M}$ is a stationary integral varifold with density $π/2$ at each singularity. Mert Gürbüzbalaban; M. Hamza Rafi; Necdet Serhat Aybat; Waheed U. Bajwa

With exact, delay-free gradients, Nesterov's accelerated gradient (NAG) achieves optimal $\sqrtκ$ dependence for $L$-smooth, $μ$-strongly convex objectives, where $κ=L/μ$; heavy-ball (HB) achieves the same scaling on strongly convex quadratics. In asynchronous and distributed settings, gradients can be inexact, with delays varying across workers and iterations. We isolate staleness using a fixed delay $τ\ge1$, replacing $\nabla f(y_k)$ with $\nabla f(y_{k-τ})$ at iteration $k$. Arjevani, Shamir, and Srebro establish a worst-case lower bound of $Ω(τ\sqrtκ\log(1/\varepsilon))$ iterations to reach objective error at most $\varepsilon$ as $\varepsilon\to0$. We show that for any fixed positive delay, neither NAG nor HB retains $\sqrtκ$-acceleration on strongly convex quadratics when updating every iteration, for any stable constant step size and positive momentum. DREAM attains a linear convergence rate $1-Θ(1/(τ\sqrtκ))$ for all smooth strongly convex objectives as $κ\to\infty$, yielding complexity matching the delayed first-order lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Our proof combines characteristic-polynomial stability analysis on quadratics with an analytic Zames--Falb integral quadratic constraint certificate. We extend DREAM to smooth convex objectives, obtaining near-optimal iteration complexity up to logarithmic factors for sufficiently small target accuracy. Sharp Planar Anisotropic Capillarity Outside Convex Obstacles and Two-Point Rigidity of Transported Boundary Images
Lisbeth Carrero; Alexander Quaas; Andres Zuniga

For a convex surface tension $φ$ and the wall-energy density $σ(n)=-λ\,φ(-n)$, we prove sharp capillary inequalities outside arbitrary convex planar obstacles for $-1<λ\leq0$ and every finite-perimeter competitor of finite positive volume, including non-even and crystalline tensions. For the transport $DΦ$, $Φ=φ^2/2$, the zero-adhesion boundary-image estimate characterizes centered ellipsoids among even anisotropies with $Φ\in C^3$ away from the origin and positive definite Hessian. Two-point slab tests with arbitrary boundary data suffice: their projection balances yield a cubic identity forcing $Φ$ to be quadratic. Facets and smooth perturbations provide counterexamples to the transported estimate, including failures at prescribed adhesion levels in $(-1,1)$. Strict finite deficits persist under Hausdorff perturbations of the Wulff body. The classification concerns an unrestricted boundary-data property, stronger than the image estimate needed only for traces of auxiliary Neumann solutions.
Measure of Maximal Entropy for Geodesic Flows on Noncompact Manifolds of Nonpositive Curvature

We establish the variational characterization of the measure of maximal entropy on noncompact manifolds of nonpositive sectional curvature. Assuming that the deck transformation group contains an axial isometry with a rank-one axis and has a finite critical exponent, we prove that the supremum of the entropies of invariant probabilities equals the critical exponent and is attained if and only if the Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) measure is finite. In that case, the measure of maximal entropy is unique and equals the normalized BMS measure. The proof combines conditional-entropy rigidity on the regular set with an HTS-based entropy exclusion on the singular set, overcoming both non-compactness and the loss of uniform hyperbolicity due to zero curvature. We also obtain mixing under a non-arithmetic length-spectrum assumption. For nonpositively curved surfaces of genus at least two, the existence of a closed Jacobi rank-one geodesic and the non-arithmeticity of the axial length spectrum are automatic.

The first eigenvalue of the $p$-bilaplacian over a domain $Ω$ is the inverse of the Poincaré constant for $W_0^{2,p}(Ω)$. In dimension two, we prove that it is minimised by disks under area constraint, thereby obtaining a sharp uniform Poincaré inequality.
Phase-type representations for Strong Stability Preserving Runge--Kutta methods
Haijun Yu; Quanfan Zhu; Zhanyang Weng

We develop a phase-type (PH) representation of strong stability preserving (SSP) Runge--Kutta (RK) methods. This representation provides a probabilistic interpretation of the RK coefficients and translates the chain order conditions into absorption-time moment identities. Using moment ratio bounds for PH distributions, we prove the conjectured optimal SSP coefficients for general implicit RK methods of orders two and three. The equality characterizations also establish uniqueness of the optimal RK tableaux.
Privacy-Preserving Over-the-Air Federated Learning over Cell-Free Massive MIMO System with User-Centric Clustering

This paper investigates cross-layer design for differentially private federated learning over cell-free massive MIMO networks with over-the-air (OTA) aggregation. Distributed access points (APs) collaboratively serve user equipments (UEs) through user-centric clustering, where clipped local model updates are perturbed with Gaussian noise and simultaneously transmitted over a shared uplink for OTA averaging at a central processing unit. Exploiting channel hardening, we show that thermal noise inherent in wireless reception can act as a privacy-masking resource, reducing or even eliminating the need for artificial noise. Based on this observation, we formulate a joint optimization problem over AP-UE associations, UE transmit powers, and artificial noise variances to minimize aggregation variance subject to per-UE zero-concentrated differential privacy constraints derived from an ergodic privacy accounting framework. Analysis reveals a regime-dependent structure: stringent privacy requirements favor low transmit powers and sparse AP associations to exploit thermal noise for privacy, whereas relaxed requirements favor larger clusters to improve aggregation quality. The resulting mixed-integer nonconvex problem is solved via alternating optimization combining difference-of-convex power allocation and greedy coordinate-descent clustering. Numerical results show up to 89% lower aggregation variance than conventional baselines and enable 97% test accuracy on MNIST with consistent gains on CIFAR-10. Under strict privacy budgets, competing schemes remain near random-chance performance, while under relaxed budgets they continue to lag significantly behind the proposed design.
Sharp Bounds for Toral Eigenfunctions and Threefold Additive Energy on Circles

For the lattice circle $P_n=\{z\in\mathbb{Z}^2:|z|^2=n\}$, we prove that the threefold additive energy $J_3(P_n)\le C|P_n|^3$, with an absolute constant $C$. This establishes the optimal bound suggested by Krishnapur--Kurlberg--Wigman and Bombieri--Bourgain. We also prove a uniform weak $L^6$ bound for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions on the square torus, and hence uniform $L^p$ bounds for every $1\le p<6$. This extends the classical $L^4$ bounds of Cooke and Zygmund and establishes Bourgain's conjecture in this range. Applications include mean-square convergence for $L^{6/5}$ observables and a logarithm-free remainder in the nodal length variance of arithmetic random waves.
Equidistant Affine Subspaces: Explicit Bounds, Structural Reductions, Transverse Products, and Fixed-Codimension Stability

Let $\mathcal{N}(k,n)$ be the largest size of a family of affine $k$-planes in $\R^n$ at pairwise separation distance one. We develop a unified treatment of upper bounds, dimension reduction, product constructions, and fixed-codimension stability. Orthogonal-projection coordinates give a rank-stratified distance identity; a Veronese lifting converts its polynomial consequences into simultaneous total isotropy. Connected Nash decomposition and an analytic diagonal argument yield an explicit bound \[ \mathcal{N}(k,n)\leqslant 2^{\,2^{\,3(k+1)(n-k)}}. \] For configurations whose direction sums have dimension at most $k+1$, we prove the exact reduction $\mathcal{N}_{\leqslant k+1}(k,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,n-k+1)$. Every codimension-two configuration splits off a common linear factor, so $\mathcal{N}(n-2,n)=\mathcal{N}(1,3)$. A transverse product construction gives multiplicative inequalities. We further prove that for every fixed codimension $c$, the sequence $\mathcal{N}(k,k+c)$ is eventually constant. In codimension three, a sharper normal-span argument gives \[ \mathcal{N}(k,k+3)=\mathcal{N}(7,10)\qquad(k\geqslant7), \] where the numerical threshold uses the computer-assisted theorem $\mathcal{N}(1,3)=7$. The structural and stability results are otherwise independent of that numerical input.
Spectral $L^2$-bounds on Eisenstein series and Diophantine properties of quadratic forms

We give $L^2$-bounds with respect to the height of the spectral parameter for Epstein zeta functions $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ and non-holomorphic Eisenstein series $E_{\mathfrak{c}}(s,z)$ attached to the Hecke congruence subgroup $Γ_0 (p)$ of prime level $p$. Our bounds are completely explicit in the level and, additionally, constitute an almost sure logarithmic improvement over previously established bounds for the level-one Eisenstein series. Following the approach of Kelmer--Kontorovich--Lutsko, we combine the approximate functional equation for $\mathrm{Z}_Q(s)$ with estimates for the number of pairs of lattice vectors at which $Q$ takes nearly equal values. Under a Diophantine hypothesis on $Q$, we sharpen these counting estimates using results of Eskin--Margulis--Mozes on the distribution of values of quadratic forms of signature $(2,2)$.
Typical Kakeya-type sets and their typical code sets

We study properties of compact Besicovitch sets and other Kakeya-type sets which are typical in the sense that the exceptions form a meager set in the Baire category sense in a suitable metric space. The main motivation comes from the known fact that typical compact Besicovitch sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ have minimal Hausdorff dimension among all Besicovitch sets of $\mathbb{R}^n$. Thus, in order to estimate the smallest possible Hausdorff dimension of an arbitrary Besicovitch set, it is enough to estimate the Hausdorff dimension of a typical (compact) Besicovitch set, or analogously of a Besicovitch set satisfying our list of typical properties. Among other results, we prove that a typical Besicovitch set $K$ in $\mathbb{R}^n$ has the following properties: it is not sticky, any line intersects $K$ in a set of ($1$-dimensional) measure zero or in a unit line segment and a set of measure zero, it has no more than $n$ different unit line segments in any direction, and for each $1\le j\le n$ the Hausdorff dimension of the set of those directions in which $K$ has exactly $j$ unit line segments is $n-j$. For compact metric spaces $X$ and $Y$, let $\mathcal{C}(X,Y)$ denote the set of compact subsets of $X\times Y$ whose projection onto the first coordinate is $X$, equipped with the Hausdorff metric. Kakeya-type compact sets can be coded by elements of such spaces, allowing typical properties to be studied through comeager subsets of $\mathcal C(X,Y)$. Among other results, we prove that, under suitable conditions on $X$ and $Y$, a typical $A\in \mathcal{C}(X,Y)$ is totally disconnected and purely unrectifiable, its projection to the second coordinate has Hausdorff dimension zero, and the dimension identities $\dim_H(A)=\dim_H(X)$ and $\dim_P(A)=\dim_P(X)+\dim Y$ hold.

We show that the Frobenius group $\langle x,y,z\mid x^p=y^p=z^4=1,\ xy=yx,\ zxz^{-1}=y,\ zyz^{-1}=x^{-1}\rangle$ of order $4p^2$ contains no $(4p^2,2p^2-p,p^2-p)$ difference set if $p\equiv 3\pmod 4$ is a prime with $p \geq 7$. Together with results of McFarland, Iiams and Liebler this shows that no group of order $4p^2$ with $p \equiv 3 \pmod 4$ and $p \geq 7$ contains a Hadamard difference set.
Displacement Moments and Path-Terminal Separation in Brownian Interpolant Sampling

Brownian stochastic interpolants connect paired endpoint samples, yet their sampling error can depend on displacement moments even when neither endpoint has a first moment. For arbitrary Borel couplings, we prove early-stopped, target-to-output KL guarantees for standard Euler sampling from the true source. A fourth displacement moment gives an explicit $O(N^{-1})$ bound; a second moment suffices for fixed-law convergence as drift error vanishes. For one fixed coupling with no displacement moment above two, original bridge-path KL stays of order one, comparison-path KL is of order $1/\log N$, and terminal KL is at most $C/N^2$ on the same grid. The path decomposition identifies the information about the source discarded by Markov projection. When the original bridge is Markov, current-state Euler sampling instead has a second-moment $O((M_2+d)/N)$ bound; finite-entropy Schroedinger bridges for the probability Brownian reference are included. We also construct a current-state learner with expected output KL consistency from iid endpoint pairs. Numerical diagnostics illustrate the distinct errors. Conditional diffusion identities specify a restoration interface, while image controls find no iterative advantage over cheap probabilistic predictors. Uniform terminal rates for general second-moment couplings remain open.
The Capacity of Private Information Retrieval from Coded Storage Systems with Colluding, Robust and Byzantine Servers

We consider the problem of private information retrieval from MDS-coded databases with $T$ colluding servers, $U$ robust servers, and $B$ Byzantine servers, referred to as U-B-MDS-TPIR. In the U-B-MDS-TPIR setting, $M$ files are stored across $N$ servers, and in this paper each file is independently encoded using an $(N,K)$ GRS code. We characterize the capacity among linear, full support-rank U-B-MDS-TPIR schemes as $C=\frac{N-U-2B}{N-U}(1+\frac{K+T-1}{N-U-2B}+\cdots+(\frac{K+T-1}{N-U-2B})^{M-1})^{-1}$ when $N-U-2B\ge KT$. When $K=1$ or $T=1$, the same expression gives the capacity without the linearity and full support-rank restrictions. We further extend the construction to the retrieval of $P$ out of $M$ files. For $P \ge \frac{M}{2}$, the resulting multi-file scheme achieves capacity when $K=1$ or $T=1$.
Measuring Sudoku Difficulty: Formulation, Propagation and Uniqueness Certification

Finding a Sudoku completion and proving that the completion is unique are different computational tasks. Despite both concerning the same puzzle, their computational effort need not be closely related. In this paper, we investigate how this relationship depends on the mathematical formulation, solver and measure of computational effort. Using 32,000 uniquely solvable puzzles and 64 harder instances, we compare integer programming formulations and CP-SAT. Further, we prove that the raw natural formulation has an extremely weak linear programming relaxation, even with uniqueness exclusions. Computational experiments show that the relationship between completion and certification effort depends on the formulation, puzzle population, solver and effort measure, rather than on the puzzle alone.
High powers of grids in random geometric graphs and thresholds for wide spanning structures

Using results of Leighton and Shor and of Shor and Yukich, we present a connection between $d$-dimensional bandwidth and (sharp) thresholds in $d$-dimensional random geometric graphs: namely, that the sharp threshold for a given graph property in random geometric graphs is determined by its $d$-dimensional bandwidth, and vice versa, whenever the $d$-dimensional bandwidth of this property grows sufficiently fast (at least polylogarithmically) with the order of the graphs. This connection provides a number of corollaries, such as new information about the sharp thresholds for containing different spanning subgraphs in $1$-dimensional random geometric graphs, as well as asymptotically tight bounds for the $d$-dimensional bandwidth of structures such as graphs of bounded treewidth or genus, giving an asymptotic resolution to several problems raised by Chung in 1988.
A semigroup approach for rough partial differential equations with jumps

We establish an infinite-dimensional sewing lemma for discontinuous paths on a scale of Banach spaces. This allows us to construct Young and rough convolutions with jumps. Based on this we analyze the local and global well-posedness of semilinear parabolic rough partial differential equations (PDEs) with jumps in mixed space-time regularity spaces.

We study two obstructions to a finite group $G$ having a generating $d$-tuple whose Cayley graph has spectral gap at least $ε$. Lubotzky and Weiss proved that such a gap forces $\mathrm{ab}_k(G)$, the largest order of the abelianization of a subgroup of index at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_ε(dk))$, while de la Harpe, Robertson and Valette proved that it forces $\mathrm{rep}_k(G)$, the number of irreducible complex representations of degree at most $k$, to be $\exp(O_ε(dk^2))$. For powers of alternating groups, the natural candidates, we show that a spectral gap keeps the number of factors a fixed power below the maximum allowed by $d$-generation, and that random generators have spectral gap tending to $0$ already for superpolynomially many factors.
Finite group actions on the non-minimal nilpotent orbit closures in type A

We study quotients of the closures of the nilpotent orbits of type A by finite groups of inner automorphisms. Assuming the nilpotent orbit is not minimal, we show that the Q-factorial terminalizations of quotients of nilpotent orbit closures are precisely the quotients of the symplectic resolutions of the orbit closures. Spatial tessellations formed by SCM have been applied in preliminary analyses of spatial point pattern recognition,spatial topology, and Voronoi diagram generation. Unlike previous spatial tessellation models, a key feature of SCM is that each subspace (cell) possesses a chromatic code, which serves as the foundation for various theoretical analyses and applications of SCM. Previous studies have demonstrated the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 2-cell and 3-cell connected disjoint clusters. Building on this analysis of connected cluster code characteristics, this paper proves the uniqueness of the chromatic codes of 4-cell connected disjoint clusters. The proof results and the new concepts introduced in this study help further refine the spatial chromatic model and provide a theoretical foundation for its subsequent applications.
The K-property of equilibrium states for systems with non-uniform structure

In this paper, we develop a general criterion for the K-property of equilibrium states within the Climenhaga-Thompson framework. Under suitable pressure-gap and non-uniform expansiveness assumptions, we show that the unique equilibrium state has the K-property, provided that the good collection of orbit segments satisfies an appropriate non-uniform specification property, as well as an appropriate non-uniform distortion control property for the potential function. These results do not require any additional lambda-decomposition structure and apply to a wide range of systems, including those with non-trivial central directions, such as the frame flow over closed rank-one manifolds with bunched nonpositive curvature. Moreover, we also construct several counterexamples to demonstrate that generally the assumptions in our criteria cannot be weakened while keeping the K-property.

It is known that randomly initialized neural networks have Gaussian behaviour in the $n\to \infty$ limit. Unfortunately, this approximation can be poor for finite $n$ and gets worse as one goes deeper into the network. In this work, we develop a more accurate approximation that is \emph{slightly} non-Gaussian, which we call the para-Gaussian distribution and is constructed from the Hermite polynomials. We show how this para-Gaussian approximation can lead to a practical recursive method to approximate the deeper layers of the network. Finally, we apply this theory to linear neural networks (where things can be solved exactly) and to ReLU neural networks (where things can be approximated).

We derive first-order necessary conditions for $\mathcal{H}_2$ optimal model reduction of these polynomial systems and use them to construct an efficient iterative algorithm for computing reduced BQO models that approximately satisfy these conditions. Numerical results on two examples demonstrate the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed reduction approach.

We prove that if $L$ is norm Euclidean, then $L$ is $\mathcal{O}_{F}$-maximal of class number one, and the class number of $F$ equals the class number of $L\perp\mathbf{H}$, where $\mathbf{H}$ is the hyperbolic lattice with quadratic form $xy$. We study stationary coexistence in stochastic Gause predator-prey systems with independent multiplicative environmental noise and trophic responses depending on both population densities. A weighted population balance cancels the trophic interaction and yields moments of order greater than one without imposing predator self-regulation. These estimates give a direct occupation-measure proof of a sufficient coexistence criterion based on prey establishment and predator invasion of the prey-only stationary environment. A zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions in the weight aspect

In this paper, we prove a zero-density estimate for the symmetric square $L$-functions associated with Hecke eigencuspforms in the weight aspect. The proofs are based on the mollified second moment of these $L$-functions.
The Geometry of Manifold Learning: Singular foliations via Deep Learning models

A key challenge is determining whether these algorithms truly capture the intrinsic geometry of their training data in order to better understand what they learn from data. In this theoretical work, we explore a new geometric structure defined on the data space by a trained neural network through the Data Information Matrix (DIM), a variation of the Fisher Information Matrix. This new geometric structure is a foliation and the main focus of this work is to explore the non-smooth case of ReLU activation functions, where traditional geometric tools often fail. The foliation is defined through a distribution spanned by the columns of the DIM. We first prove that this distribution is non-smooth in the sense of distributions, rendering the existence of an associated foliation much more complex. To circumvent this issue, we introduce a smoothed version of this distribution that differs from the original only on a set of measure zero. Finally, we prove that this smoothed distribution induces a singular foliation on the data space, which is based on the data the network has been trained with. Our theoretical contributions provide a geometric framework to better understand how neural networks organize their input space in non-smooth settings, bridging differential geometry and deep learning theory.
A switching proximal gradient method for constrained difference-of-convex optimization problems

We study difference-of-convex optimization problems with several composite inequality constraints and develop a majorization-guided switching proximal gradient (MGSPG) method. Specifically, at each feasible outer point, quadratic majorization and linearization yield a strongly convex composite surrogate problem. To solve this surrogate approximately, we employ a switching proximal gradient (SPG) method, which takes a proximal gradient step for the objective when the current point is nearly feasible and for a most violated constraint otherwise. This construction requires neither projection onto the joint surrogate feasible set nor multiplier computation. By establishing a common invariant ball and using an increasing weight argument, we obtain an \(O(τ^{-1})\) inner complexity bound for SPG. Building on this bound, we show that, under boundedness of the feasible level set and a uniform Slater condition for the surrogates, MGSPG finds an \(\varepsilon\)-KKT point in \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) outer iterations and \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) selected component proximal gradient updates. The method is built on score-function estimators for the evidence lower bound (ELBO), which avoid differentiation through the PDE model but are known to suffer from high variance. We investigate strategies for adapting the ROM and estimating the approximate control-variate gains, examining tradeoffs between estimator bias, variance reduction, and computational cost. The resulting approach facilitates derivative-free variational inference for large-scale inverse problems through a reduction in overall computational cost. Rigoberto Flórez; Robinson Higuita-Diaz; José L. Ramírez

We study the $p$-adic valuation trees associated with the sequence \[ e_n=\int_0^\infty e^{-t}F_n(t)\,dt, \] obtained by evaluating the Laplace transforms of the Fibonacci polynomials at $1$. Finally, we develop a recursive lifting procedure that determines the unique surviving residue class at each level of a branch associated with a simple root and computes the $p$-adic valuations of the corresponding terms.
Simultaneous diagonalization via congruence: Nondegenerate families of symmetric matrices
In this letter, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the real symmetric matrices $A_1 , \ldots , A_m$ to ensure they are simultaneously diagonalizable via congruence.

First, the restriction to box divisions is removed via a direction bound and a uniform Riemann-sum estimate for all $δ$-fine cylindrical divisions. Second, the coordinate measure on $\mathbb{R}^k$ is identified with the standard Gaussian one. Third, the Saks-Henstock lemma and additivity are proved. Fourth, the Fresnel formula $\int_{\mathbb{R}} e^{i a x^2/2} dx = \sqrt{2π/a} e^{iπ/4}$ is proved as an improper (gauge) integral. This yields the projective consistency of the oscillating Gaussian premeasure and the existence of the free-field integral. The interacting field $λφ^4$, unbounded generators, and renormalisation remain open. All results are machine-verified with no sorry or new axioms.

We study a scalar finite-horizon controlled diffusion with a finite action set. An action may affect the drift, the instantaneous variance, or both, and performance is assessed by a uniformly convex terminal deviation cost. The model represents systems in which decisions are made continuously in time but only finitely many operating settings are available. Under uniform nondegeneracy and an explicit shape condition on the terminal cost, we show that the value function is classical at positive times, establish global positive upper and lower bounds for its second state derivative, and prove that the ratio of its first and second state derivatives is strictly increasing. This ordering implies that each action's optimality region is connected, the active actions occur in monotone order, and adjacent regions are separated by unique switching boundaries. It also yields an exact coefficient-based screen that removes actions that cannot be optimal on any open state region. For smooth continuous-action benchmarks, both the value loss from restricting the action set and the additional loss from rounding the continuous optimal feedback to the nearest available action decrease quadratically with the action-set resolution. Numerical experiments illustrate the resulting action screens, threshold policies, and implementation losses.
Universality Criterion Sets for Definite Quadratic Lattices over Polynomial Rings

Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $\neq 2$. Under suitable assumptions on the dimensions of anisotropic quadratic forms over $k$ and $k(x)$, we show that a definite integral quadratic form over the polynomial ring $k[x]$ is universal if the form represents all scalars from $k$ and all scalar multiples of $x$. We have a finite universality criterion set over $k[x]$ for some coefficient fields $k$, including some cases where $k$ has infinitely many square classes (e.g., $k=\mathbb{C}(t)$).

We demonstrate that the conjugacy growth series for the Heisenberg groups $H_n(\mathbb{Z})$ is never algebraic, irrespective of the generating set. This makes progress towards the conjecture that all finitely presented groups that are not virtually abelian have irrational conjugacy growth series. Contrary to the group $H_3(\mathbb{Z})$, where the conjugacy growth is $n^2\log(n)$, the conjugacy growth of the other Heisenberg groups is polynomial, making these groups the first known nilpotent groups where the irrationality does not follow from the asymptotic growth.

Our main object of study is the so-called window process, which allows us to study the fine details of the mechanism that drives the SOC behavior of this dynamic random graph. We prove two scaling limit theorems. First, we show that the fluctuations of the window process around its deterministic fluid limit converge to a stationary Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process, whose mean-reverting property captures the SOC nature of the model. Second, by zooming in on a finer space-time scale, we prove that the scaled increments of the window process converge to a tempered stable Lévy process.

We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.
The maximum size of intersecting $k$-graphs with covering number $k$

Let $m(k)$ be the maximum size of an intersecting $k$-graph with covering number $k$. In the present paper, it is proved that for all $k>e^{32}$, \[ m(k)\ge k^k\exp\bigl(-50\sqrt{k\log k}\bigr). \] Together with Zakharov's upper bound \cite{Z}, this implies $m(k)=k^k\exp\bigl(-k^{1/2+o(1)}\bigr)$.

A symmetric positive-definite resistivity tensor is constructed so that the resistive differential expression preserves the spatial form of a known sheared toroidal equilibrium. A two-temperature extension admits a $T_e^{-3/2}$ prefactor and positive interspecies heat exchange on a finite state interval. Material magnetic flux decays while the rotational-transform profile is preserved. Both branches satisfy local total-energy conservation, moving-boundary power balance and material transport of dissipation histories. A seed-specific obstruction excludes positive scalar resistivity along the same homologous trajectory; the two-temperature exchange law has a nonremovable endpoint pole. Symbolic identities, independent Cartesian differentiation and surface--volume quadrature verify these results. The solutions provide coupled MHD benchmarks with passive, inverse-designe

We study perfect sampling algorithms for Ising spin glasses based on coupling from the past and bounding chains, on several graph families and coupling distributions. Non-split groups of Lie type and iSchur algebras with unequal parameters

We present a geometric framework for realizing quantum Schur algebras with unequal parameters, via constructible sheaves on flag varieties arising from non-split groups of Lie type. In the special cases of general unitary groups and minus-type orthogonal groups, this framework yields the iSchur algebras with unequal parameters, which are closely related to the quasi-split iquantum groups of type AIII. A nontrivial arithmetic structure is imposed on the geometric structure of split groups, giving rise to many new phenomena. We derive explicit overlap functions for integrable matrix product states associated with arbitrary finite-dimensional irreducible evaluation representations of the orthogonal and symplectic twisted Yangians. The central step is to relate the commuting quasi-determinants entering the universal overlap formula to Sklyanin determinants of nested subalgebras. For orthogonal evaluation representations, this relation determines their spectra directly in the Gelfand--Tsetlin basis. In the symplectic case, we combine Sklyanin determinants and minors with a factorization of the nested rank-two boundary matrices to obtain the corresponding spectra. The resulting overlap functions are explicit products parametrized by Gelfand--Tsetlin patterns and require only the highest-weight data of the underlying orthogonal or symplectic representation. Together with the universal ratio of Gaudin determinants and the model-dependent pseudovacuum overlap coefficients, they determine the normalized MPS overlaps. We also express the overlap functions in the orthogonal case beyond evaluation representations in terms of the highest weights arising along the nested twisted-Yangian subalgebras.
Effective Gromov-Witten computations for GKM spaces and a semisimple application

We report a major update to our original software GKMtools and record multiple improvements in the computation of Gromov--Witten invariants of GKM spaces. This includes a refined divisor equation that reduces the complexity from exponential to linear in the number of marked points, three tricks to accelerate the computation of curve class relations in the GKM graph, and an implementation of Mihalcea's algorithm for homogeneous varieties using the equivariant quantum Chevalley formula. As an application, we prove that the small quantum cohomology of the type-$E$ generalized Grassmannians $E_7/P_2,E_7/P_4,E_7/P_5,E_8/P_6$ is generically semisimple. These are precisely the remaining exceptional Grassmannians for which generic semisimplicity of small quantum cohomology was still unknown.
A Posteriori Error Analysis of Finite Element Approximation to an Evolution Equation with a Positive-Type Memory Term
Sandhya Mel; Amiya Kumar Pani; Gujji Murali Mohan Reddy

This paper develops reliable a posteriori error estimates for finite element approximation of an evolution equation with a positive-type memory kernels on bounded convex polygonal or polyhedral domains, including both smooth and weakly singular kernels. For the weakly singular kernel $t^{α-1}/Γ(α),\; 0<α<1,$ the model captures the transition from parabolic diffusion to wave propagation, recovering the corresponding limiting equations as $α\to0^+$ and $α\to1^-$, respectively, with the memory term governing the intermediate dynamics. The spatial discretization employs time-dependent finite element spaces, while the backward Euler method combined with numerical quadrature is used for time integration. A unified \emph{a posteriori} analysis is established for both semidiscrete and fully discrete approximations. Elliptic reconstruction yields optimal spatial error estimates, while a memory-lag estimate preserves the essential cancellation in the convolution term, yielding a first-order temporal estimator whose kernel dependence is characterized by its integral. The resulting estimators are robust, with constants independent of the final time, spatial mesh size, and time step. Their kernel dependence involves only computable quantities, avoiding exponential growth in time. Moreover, for the weakly singular kernel, the $α$-dependent factors remain uniformly bounded for $α\in(0,1).$ Numerical experiments on a convex domain validate the theoretical results, and a space-time adaptive algorithm is also demonstrated on an L-shaped domain featuring a corner singularity and two temporal layers.
On-shell reduction of spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau covariants and implications for the relativistic impulse approximation

We analyze the on-shell content of the local Lorentz covariants of the five-dimensional spin-zero Duffin-Kemmer-Petiau algebra in elastic spin-zero-spin-$1/2$ scattering. The scalar, vector, and tensor structures are reduced explicitly to the two independent amplitudes allowed by the physical parity-conserving process. The two scalar structures are proportional on shell, the genuine nonminimal vector $i[P,β^μ]$ is longitudinal and vanishes after contraction with the conserved fermion vector current, and the projected vectors $Pβ^μ$ and $β^μP$ each reduce to one half of the minimal-vector contribution. The tensor covariants introduce no additional on-shell directions. We discuss the consequences for the four invariant choices used in meson-nucleus optical-potential calculations and show that different nuclear equations can arise only after on-shell-equivalent representatives are promoted to optical operators and iterated beyond the order at which the elementary impulse approximation is fixed. These results provide a systematic basis for distinguishing genuinely independent elementary amplitudes from representation-dependent effects generated by the optical embedding.
Explicit Serre weights for modular Galois representations of $U(2)$

Let $p$ be an odd prime. Let $F$ be a totally imaginary CM field and $F^+$ be the maximal totally real subfield such that $F/F^+$ is unramified at all finite places, and every place $v | p$ of $F^+$ is split in $F$. We allow arbitrary ramification of $p$ in $F^+$. Let $G$ be a rank two definite unitary group over $F^+$ as defined in [2]. Fix a place $\mathfrak{p} | p$ in $F$. In this article, we determine explicit local Serre weights at $\mathfrak{p}$ attached to a modular mod $p$ Galois representation $\barρ_h$ of the absolute Galois group of $F$, associated to an eigenform $h$ of $G$. The eigenform $h$ has arbitrary weights and small slope at $\mathfrak{p}$. We also show analogous results for certain Hilbert modular eigenforms with arbitrary ramification of $p$ in the totally real field. The eigenforms come from totally definite and indefinite quaternion algebras over totally real fields, split at places above $p$. In proving our results, we identify the non-singular submodules in quotients of certain symmetric power $\mathbb{F}_q[\text{M}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$-modules by Dickson polynomials and their twisted versions.
Mathematical Reality Capture: from the age of discoveries to mathematical topography and surveys

A proof answers a precise question, but mathematical understanding also grows through the relationships that its answer makes visible. A point measurement likewise differs from a photograph or a three-dimensional reconstruction of a building. In this work, we argue that, with the help of AI, mathematics should move from a discipline focused on isolated investigations of mathematical objects towards one capable of mapping them systematically. We therefore introduce the idea of "Mathematical Reality Capture", inspired by digital surveying and the reconstruction of a scene from several viewpoints. An elementary example shows how comparing algebra and geometry can illuminate the same phenomenon, provided that we distinguish diversity of explanations from validity of proof. From this analogy we derive criteria for building verifiable atlases, an experiment with which to assess their usefulness, and a reflection on the role of mathematicians in interpreting them.

We study the asymptotic behavior as \(d\to0^+\) of the principal eigenvalue \(λ(d)\) of the one-dimensional elliptic problem \[ \begin{cases} -dϕ''(x)-2αm'(x)ϕ'(x)+c(x)ϕ(x) =λ(d)ϕ(x), & x\in(a,b),\\ ϕ'(a)=ϕ'(b)=0, \end{cases} \] where \(α>0\) is fixed, \(m\in C^{1,1}([a,b])\), and \(c\in C([a,b])\). We assume that \(m'=0\) only at \(x_0\in(a,b)\), where \(m\) attains a strict minimum. Within this class, we construct a counterexample $m\in C^{1,1}$ for which \(λ(d)\) has two distinct subsequential limits as \(d\to0^+\), leading to the non-convergence of $λ(d)$. We then consider another class of $C^{1,1}$ advection functions for which $m'(x)/(x-x_0)$ has positive one-sided limits at $x_0$. For this class, we prove that $λ(d)$ converges as $d\to0^+$. Thus, \(C^{1,1}\) regularity alone does not ensure convergence of the principal eigenvalue, even when \(m\) has exactly one strict interior critical minimal point.

The present paper is devoted to exhibit solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic. With ambiguous non-conservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. This jump condition is obtained from the information given by the travelling wave solutions of the viscous extension of the system that involves the diffusion terms arising from the physics of the problem. We are then able to determine the simple waves of the non-conservative system studied here and we are able to construct some solutions of the Riemann problem of interest.

We construct smooth, compactly supported stationary Euler flows in two and three dimensions. The three-dimensional flows are axisymmetric with swirl, and their pressure varies along some streamlines. The planar flows are not locally radial. Both constructions start from simple radial profiles, which we perturb by solving scalar elliptic equations on fixed domains. We choose these equations so that their solutions can be exactly constant on open sets and meet these constant regions smoothly. Comparison arguments produce the constant regions, while an a priori regularity theorem ensures that all derivatives vanish where a solution meets them. This gives compact support and smoothness without having to describe the boundary of the support.
Sharp helical maximal estimates in all dimensions
Shengwen Gan; Changkeun Oh; Jaehoon Shin

We establish sharp $L^p$ maximal estimates for averages over smooth nondegenerate curves in $\mathbb R^n$ for $p>n$. More precisely, we show that for any nondegenerate curve $γ$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and the associated maximal operator \begin{equation} M f(x):=\sup_{t>0} \Big|\int_{-1}^1f(x-tγ(s))χ(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|, \end{equation} the estimate \begin{equation} \| Mf\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\lesssim_{γ,p,n} \|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)} \end{equation} holds for all $p>n$. A new ingredient is a weighted Kakeya-type estimate.

We construct explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress formulation of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media using Schrödingerisation. For physical boundaries, interleaved encoding swaps the spatial and field-component registers, enabling a more efficient circuit construction using shift operators. Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model

In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. In this paper, we investigate the classes of \lq\lq unicorns" of general $(α,β)$-metric types, namely, Landsberg general $(α,β)$-metrics that are non-Berwaldian. We provide explicit solutions for these metrics, including several new classes. Furthermore, we identify and exclude the cases that yield degenerate metrics to guarantee the geometric validity of the established solutions.
Three quantitative central limit theorems for the unbounded excursion component of a Gaussian field

For a class of smooth stationary Gaussian fields, we study the fluctuations of the volume, surface area and Euler characteristic of the unbounded excursion component in growing boxes $Λ_n=[-n,n]^d$. In this regime, time resonances may occur and the relevant curvature quantity may vanish.
